Rationale_SHINOBU_154.md
SHINOBU154 Rationale
Status: STATIC IMPLEMENTATION IN PROGRESS - UNITY/BURST RUNTIME PROOF BLOCKED BY DEPENDENCY COMPILE WALL
Initial Scope Decision
Problem: Dynamic entity saves require byte-level delta persistence without JSON, reflection, object traversal, or main-thread file stalls.
Solution: Build within SaveSystem/Core memory reality discovered on disk. Use explicit unmanaged DTOs, AUP sector keys, Burst extraction jobs, RLE preconditioning, native LZ4 binding if present, and WAL handoff through bounded staging buffer.
Rejected Alternatives: JSON/BinaryFormatter/object graph traversal rejected by task and SaveManager mandate; direct .sav writes rejected by atomic save contract; dictionary LZ4 rejected unless existing binding supports it and corpus evidence exists.
Scalability potential: Low uses RLE-fast and coarse profiling cadence; Middle uses RLE+LZ4 fast; High uses deeper LZ4 effort if latency budget allows; Ultra spends saved CPU on denser telemetry and editor diagnostics, not larger authority structs.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 target is reduced autosave hitch by moving extraction/compression to jobs and disk write to WAL background path; estimated hot main-thread savings are pending source inspection and compile verification.
First-20-Minutes Route
Problem: Autosave hitch during early scavenging/base-module placement can break first 20 minutes route.
Solution: Persist only deltas for dropped items, fauna state records, base modules, and depleted nodes so route-critical scavenging state survives without visible freeze.
Rejected Alternatives: Full snapshot saves and scene-wide serialization rejected due unbounded latency and managed heap pressure.
Scalability potential: Same byte format scales by sector paging; high-tier improves diagnostics/compression effort without changing gameplay truth.
Hardware Impact: PENDING MEASUREMENT; static target is sub-0.1 ms scheduling overhead on main thread, worker latency visible only in telemetry.
Loop 1 - Tasks 01-05
Problem: entitysaveschema.h8bin and dedicated entity delta DTOs were absent; live entity save truth is spread across managed/Unity-facing compatibility types.
Solution: Added EntityDeltaCompressionArchitecture with deterministic emergency schema bytes, explicit EntityDeltaHeaderDTO and EntityDeltaDataRecordDTO, Vault buffers now spanning 70340..70357, and GenerateMockEntityStateJob.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing ModuleDTO, WorldStateDTO, ProceduralWorldStateDTO, PersistentWorldItemRecord, or FaunaBrain was rejected because those are live compatibility/domain-owner surfaces and would cause cross-domain blast radius. New save-only DTOs avoid CS1612 and Pack=1 without rewriting unrelated owners.
Scalability potential: Low uses sparse mock mutation, byte-RLE and low write cadence; Middle uses RLE plus fast LZ4; High increases hash-table coverage; Ultra raises diagnostics/profile fidelity without changing authoritative payload schema.
Hardware Impact: Expected i3/MX350 win is removal of object graph traversal and serializer allocations from autosave. Static estimate: thousands of records reduce to deltaCount 80 bytes before compression; measured microseconds pending guarded compile/runtime proof.
Loop 2 - Tasks 06-10
Problem: Saving every entity slot produces full snapshot and blocks on CPU/disk.
Solution: Added EntityTombstonePruneJob, ExtractEntityDeltaJob, dense byte pack, RLE preconditioner, deterministic LZ4-format Burst job, and WAL payload pack routed to IAsyncPersistenceService.
Rejected Alternatives: NativeListbyte in prompt was rejected for runtime route because H-PHI Vault law requires pre-owned Vault buffers and explicit cursors. Native LZ4 P/Invoke was rejected inside Burst because existing project route does not expose Burst-callable dictionary binding; current house pattern is deterministic LZ4 block encoder in Burst job.
Scalability potential: Compression effort is math.lerp/smoothstep-driven by GlobalQualityWeight, I/O pressure, and disk latency. Below 0.3 quality LZ4 hash coverage collapses toward 512 slots, match probe step widens, and write Hz trends to low endpoint.
Hardware Impact: Expected i3/MX350 win is bounded worker compression cost under I/O pressure and no main-thread disk write. Exact frame cost remains pending Unity/Burst proof.
Loop 3 - Tasks 11-16
Problem: Delta bytes need corruption detection, rollback determinism, and postmortem telemetry.
Solution: Checksums use SaveStateMerkleTree.Hash128 folded to 64 bits into EntityDeltaHeaderDTO.XXHash3Checksum; read helper verifies bytes before hydration. pipeline uses deterministic Burst float mode and simulation-frame/tick inputs, stores integer AUP sector coordinates plus local offsets, and writes 300-entry telemetry ring with latency spike dump support.
Rejected Alternatives: Unity Time.deltaTime, UnityEngine.Random, absolute float3 world coordinates, and synchronous file writes were rejected. WAL handoff uses existing save pager background thread and typed payload route instead of direct file ownership.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra tiers share same byte format; quality changes only workload cadence, LZ4 probe depth, RLE threshold, and diagnostics. This prevents save incompatibility across hardware.
Hardware Impact: Expected i3/MX350 win is bounded cache-line-friendly DTO scanning and false-sharing-padded block counters. Static layout proof: header 32 bytes, entity record 80 bytes, block counter 64 bytes.
Global Authority Route Card
Owner: SystemID.SavePersistence
Fact: Dynamic entity save deltas.
Route: live producer systems write flat EntityDeltaDataRecordDTO records into GlobalDataVault; EntityDeltaCompressionArchitecture.ScheduleCompressionPipeline consumes current/baseline Vault arrays and returns JobHandle; completed WAL bytes are enqueued through IAsyncPersistenceService.TryEnqueueChunkPageWrite.
Buffers: SaveEntityDeltaSchemaBytes, SaveEntityDeltaCurrentRecords, SaveEntityDeltaBaselineRecords, SaveEntityDeltaRecords, SaveEntityDeltaBlockCounters, SaveEntityDeltaDenseBytes, SaveEntityDeltaRleBytes, SaveEntityDeltaCompressedBytes, SaveEntityDeltaLz4HashTable, SaveEntityDeltaHeaders, SaveEntityDeltaCounters, SaveEntityDeltaTelemetryRing, SaveEntityDeltaTelemetryCursor, SaveEntityDeltaTuning, SaveEntityDeltaSectorStats, SaveEntityDeltaCsvScratch, SaveEntityDeltaProfiles, SaveEntityDeltaWalPayloadBytes.
Proof: Static source and layout manifest hooks added. Unity import, Burst Inspector, profiler, WAL replay, and save/load route proof remain pending.
Compile Wall Reality Check
Problem: Assets/Project/Scripts/Hecton8.Core.asmdef already owns SaveSystem and has pre-existing references to several sibling runtime assemblies. Splitting save lane into new asmdef during this pass would create high-risk circular boundary because BinaryLayoutManifest, SaveManager, and existing voxel/Merkle save lanes currently live in root Core assembly shape.
Solution: Do not mutate root asmdef in this lane. Keep SHINOBU154 code limited to Hecton8.Core, Hecton8.Core.Contracts, Hecton8.Core.Memory, Hecton8.Core.Memory.Layout, Unity Burst/Collections/Jobs/Mathematics, and BCL/Unity editor surfaces. Record asmdef reality rather than pretending root compile wall is clean.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding Hecton8.SaveSystem.asmdef now was rejected because it would force cross-assembly rewiring of existing save contracts and likely break import for unrelated save lanes.
Scalability potential: Local file-level dependency hygiene is preserved; full compile-wall repair needs integrator-owned asmdef split.
Hardware Impact: Avoids broad recompile/refactor blast radius while keeping entity delta compressor source free of new sibling-domain routes.
Compile Gate
Problem: AGENTS forbids launching dotnet/compile when CPU load is above 50 percent or another compiler is running.
Solution: Checked process and CPU state before build; no dotnet/csc process was visible, but CPU load reported 100 percent, so no build was launched.
Rejected Alternatives: Starting dotnet build under thermal/CPU load to satisfy checklist theater.
Scalability potential: Protects iteration hardware and avoids compile wall contention with 20+ parallel-agent batch.
Hardware Impact: Prevents avoidable developer-machine stalls; compile proof remains pending.
Loop 6 - OnDrawGizmos and Ref Mutation Polish
Problem: Task 19 explicitly requires OnDrawGizmos hook, and hot delta/prune jobs still relied on NativeArrayT indexers for record and counter mutation.
Solution: Added EntityDeltaGizmoProbe.OnDrawGizmos, which reads SaveEntityDeltaSectorStats and draws green-to-red sector wire boxes without mutating Vault truth. Added ElementAsRefT and ElementAsReadOnlyRefT helpers backed by UnsafeUtility.AsRef; GenerateMockEntityStateJob, EntityTombstonePruneJob, and ExtractEntityDeltaJob now use ref access for hot record/counter writes and read-only refs for baseline/current comparison.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping SceneView delegate as only visualizer was rejected because it did not satisfy literal OnDrawGizmos hook. Leaving indexer mutation was rejected because mandate demands ref/native pointer mutation in cache-hot DTO loops.
Scalability potential: Low through Ultra tiers share same editor visual truth; heat color scales continuously by compressed bytes rather than switching tier labels. Ref access does not change save format, only lowers copy risk in scanner path.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 expected gain is small per entity but accumulates across thousands of records by avoiding avoidable DTO copy paths in extraction/pruning; exact microseconds still require Unity/Burst profiler proof.
Static Gate Refresh
Problem: New polish could reintroduce forbidden patterns or whitespace defects.
Solution: Ran focused git diff --check, forbidden hot-path pattern scan, direct sibling namespace scan, and compiler process/CPU gate. Added stable Unity .meta files for EntityDeltaCompressionArchitecture.cs, EntityDeltaGizmoProbe.cs, and EntitySaveTunerWindow.cs.
Rejected Alternatives: Running dotnet build while CPU telemetry reports 100 percent, which violates project build-protection rule and user's explicit instruction.
Scalability potential: Static hygiene remains independent of hardware tier; compile/runtime proof waits for safe machine window.
Hardware Impact: No additional runtime allocation surfaced by static scan; build proof remains blocked by CPU gate.
Loop 7 - Task 20 Burst Audit Hardening
Problem: 99 percent compression-ratio proof existed as cold managed helper over telemetry, but Task 20 requires embedded self-audit routine that can participate in job graph.
Solution: Added EntityDeltaCompressionRatioAuditJob with deterministic Burst flags and NoAlias fields. It scans 300-frame telemetry ring, ignores fatal samples, writes CounterAuditSamples, CounterAuditSmallerPayloads, and CounterAuditPass, and is scheduled through ScheduleCompressionRatioSelfAudit.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating Markdown SELFAUDIT block as only verification mechanism was rejected. managed test-only loop remains available for editor/cold validation, but authoritative recurring audit now runs against Vault telemetry as job.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra use identical audit math; quality changes workload and payload size, not pass criterion. This prevents low-tier saves from silently accepting full snapshots as normal.
Hardware Impact: Audit cost is bounded to 300 telemetry entries and one counters buffer write; expected i3/MX350 cost is negligible relative to compression jobs, but profiler proof remains pending.
Loop 7 Static Gate
Problem: new Burst audit job could have broken source hygiene or Burst directive consistency.
Solution: Re-ran focused git diff --check, forbidden-pattern scan, Burst directive scan, NoAlias scan, untracked file trailing-whitespace/brace/meta checks, and guarded compiler-process check.
Rejected Alternatives: Launching build while CPU telemetry failed to produce safe below-50-percent reading.
Scalability potential: audit path is fixed 300-entry work and does not add hardware-tier branching.
Hardware Impact: No source-level allocation or direct sibling namespace regression was found; compile/runtime proof remains blocked by build gate.
Loop 9 - Audit Chain Integration
Problem: schedulable audit job still depends on callers remembering to schedule it after compressor, which is exactly how verification rots.
Solution: ScheduleCompressionPipeline now schedules EntityDeltaCompressionRatioAuditJob immediately after EntityDeltaTelemetryRecordJob when telemetry buffers are present. returned JobHandle includes extraction, pruning, dense packing, RLE, LZ4, checksum, WAL payload pack, telemetry, and ratio audit.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving audit as optional external call was rejected because it weakens Task 20 and makes CI/playmode coverage dependent on call-site discipline.
Scalability potential: fixed 300-entry audit remains independent of hardware tier; GlobalQualityWeight changes payload generation, not proof path.
Hardware Impact: Adds one tiny job after telemetry. Expected i3/MX350 cost is bounded to 300 ring reads and 3 counter writes; runtime profiler proof remains pending.
Loop 10 - RLE Stream Header and WAL Replay Validation
Problem: RLE preconditioning can legitimately bypass pair encoding and copy dense bytes, but previous inner stream had no self-describing mode marker. loader could verify outer checksum and still misinterpret raw dense bytes as run,value pairs.
Solution: Added EntityDeltaRleStreamHeaderDTO as 16-byte inner stream header before RLE/raw payload. It stores magic, exactly one mode bit, dense byte count, and stored payload byte count. RLE preconditioner writes this header before LZ4; WAL read helper validates inner stream when LZ4 stage stores raw bytes, and TryValidateRleStreamPayload is available for post-decompression validation by load code.
Rejected Alternatives: Encoding RLE/raw mode in EntityDeltaHeaderDTO.pad0 was rejected because those bytes are reserved alignment padding in assigned 32-byte header. Guessing by byte pattern was rejected because arbitrary raw dense bytes can look like pair data.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all use same stream contract. Quality changes whether RLE wins and how much LZ4 probes, not how loader interprets bytes.
Hardware Impact: Adds 16 bytes per entity-delta payload and cold validation scan over RLE pairs when replaying raw stream bytes. It prevents corrupt or ambiguous WAL hydration without adding frame hot-path allocations.
Loop 11 - Post-Pack WAL Envelope Audit
Problem: checksum job validates CompressedBytes, but actual WAL buffer is later packed copy with its own byte-count cursor. stale counter or bad copy would not be detected until load if pipeline returned immediately after pack.
Solution: Added EntityWalPayloadEnvelopeAuditJob after EntityWalPayloadPackJob. It runs in Burst, reads serialized outer header from WalPayloadBytes, compares it to Headers0, verifies compressed/uncompressed sizes against packed byte count, recomputes checksum over packed payload, and validates raw RLE stream when LZ4 was bypassed. No-payload headers pass as no-op saves without setting fatal failure. TryEnqueueEntityDeltaWalWrite now requires CounterWalEnvelopeAuditPass == 1 and rejects out-of-range byte counts instead of clamping.
Rejected Alternatives: Rehashing inside TryEnqueueEntityDeltaWalWrite was rejected because that would move O(payload) work back to main-thread enqueue boundary. Trusting pack job blindly was rejected because Task 20 requires verification to be embedded in dependency graph.
Scalability potential: audit uses same byte format on every tier. Low quality may bypass LZ4 more often; in that case audit validates raw RLE envelope in worker chain rather than changing load semantics.
Hardware Impact: Adds one worker job and one extra checksum pass over packed bytes. It does not allocate managed memory and does not block caller with Complete(). Profiler proof remains pending.
Loop 12 - Burst Load-Side WAL Decode Path
Problem: save-only compressor with checksum helper still leaves Task 11 half-proven: load side must verify before decompression and hydrate raw records without managed buffers.
Solution: Added ScheduleWalPayloadDecodePipeline, EntityWalPayloadDecodeJob, and EntityRleStreamExpandToRecordsJob. first job reads WAL header, rejects bad byte counts, verifies XXHash3 over packed payload, and either copies raw RLE bytes or decodes deterministic LZ4 block into Vault RleBytes. second job validates RLE stream header, expands pairs or raw dense bytes into Vault DenseBytes, and copies whole 80-byte records into DeltaRecords.
Rejected Alternatives: managed loader using byte/MemoryStream was rejected by prompt. Decompressing during TryReadAndVerifyWalPayload was rejected because it would force caller-side blocking and blur verification with hydration.
Scalability potential: Low quality often reaches raw RLE, Middle uses RLE+LZ4, High/Ultra can spend more LZ4 probe work; decode contract is stable across all tiers.
Hardware Impact: Adds two worker jobs to load/replay path and no managed allocations. Main-thread work remains scheduling and later dependency tracking; compile/runtime proof remains pending.
Loop 13 - Public Contract and No-Op WAL Guard
Problem: Vault-backed counter buffer is 32 entries, but public enqueue helper was only guarding access through CounterWalPayloadBytes before reading CounterWalEnvelopeAuditPass. short test or integration buffer could throw before returning false. cold WAL verifier also rejected same header-only zero-delta payload that Burst decode path treats as valid no-op replay.
Solution: Tightened TryEnqueueEntityDeltaWalWrite to require CounterCapacity, added exact header-only no-op acceptance to TryReadAndVerifyWalPayload, and made EntityDeltaRleStreamHeaderDTO public so layout manifest/editor tests remain legal if SaveSystem is split out of current root Core asmdef later.
Rejected Alternatives: Silently clamping counter access was rejected because it would hide broken integration buffer. Treating no-delta autosaves as corrupt was rejected because it creates false load failures for sectors with no modified entities.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all share this byte contract; change only hardens boundary validation and does not alter compression workload.
Hardware Impact: Removes exception edge from cold/public route validation and keeps no-op WAL replay branch O(1). No hot-path managed allocation is introduced.
Loop 14 - Symmetric Entity WAL Read Facade
Problem: Entity WAL writes use entity-specific pager key derived from SectorHash + EntityDeltaRle, but no matching helper existed for reads. future loader could request raw sector hash and miss page even though write path was correct.
Solution: Added TryRequestEntityDeltaWalRead(...) overloads for ulong sectorHash and int3 sectorCoord, plus TryCopyCompletedEntityDeltaWalPayload(...). These route only through IAsyncPersistenceService, validate request id/ticket payload type, and feed caller-owned NativeArraybyte that can be passed to ScheduleWalPayloadDecodePipeline.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding new pager interface or SaveManager-specific call was rejected because it would widen compile wall and violate owner-local route. Guessing mixed keys at call sites was rejected because one fact needs one route.
Scalability potential: helper is O(1) and tier-independent; Low through Ultra differ only in compressed payload size and compression effort.
Hardware Impact: Prevents failed read retries and avoids any managed staging buffer on hydration. Main-thread work remains small request/copy call into existing async pager service.
Loop 15 - WAL File Handle Async Flag Repair
Problem: H8BinaryWorldPager already owns background worker thread for WAL and page writes, but WAL append stream was opened with WriteThrough | SequentialScan only. SHINOBU154 task explicitly requires asynchronous WAL semantics, and data stream already used FileOptions.Asynchronous.
Solution: Added FileOptions.Asynchronous to existing WAL FileStream open flags. queue, worker thread, byte format, lock discipline, and owner remain unchanged.
Rejected Alternatives: Moving entity WAL writes into new FileStream owned by compressor was rejected because it would bypass existing pager/WAL owner and create second persistence authority. Rewriting pager to WriteAsync was rejected in this lane because it is broader worker-loop surgery and immediate contract breach is file-handle flag.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all use same pager; flag allows OS async file semantics without adding per-tier routes.
Hardware Impact: Main thread remains unaffected. worker write path keeps write-through durability while no longer opening WAL handle as purely synchronous file handle.
Loop 16 - Dedicated WAL Payload Buffer
Problem: compressor reused RleBytes as serialized WAL payload after pack. That saved one buffer but created load-side alias hazard: if completed page is copied back into RleBytes, decode job reads WAL source while also writing decompressed RLE stream into same array.
Solution: Added SaveEntityDeltaWalPayloadBytes (70357) and WalPayloadBytes field in EntityDeltaCompressionVaultBufferSet. WAL pack/audit/enqueue now use this dedicated Vault buffer. no-argument decode overload reads WalPayloadBytes and writes into RleBytes, preserving non-overlapping source and destination buffers.
Rejected Alternatives: In-place LZ4/RLE replay was rejected because overlapping MemCpy/LZ4 decode is not valid safety contract. Allocating temporary managed byte was rejected by zero-GC and Vault laws.
Scalability potential: One extra pre-owned byte buffer is tier-independent; Low through Ultra still scale compression effort continuously.
Hardware Impact: Costs one preallocated staging buffer. It removes replay corruption class without adding per-frame allocations or main-thread file I/O.
Loop 17 - Compile Gate Reality
Problem: CPU briefly dropped below 50 percent gate and no compiler process was listed, but generated Unity .csproj files are stale. Hecton8.Core.csproj includes H8BinaryWorldPager.cs but not new SHINOBU154 assets such as EntityDeltaCompressionArchitecture.cs, so direct dotnet build would report missing types from BinaryLayoutManifest for project-generation reasons rather than source truth.
Solution: Do not run dotnet build against stale generated projects. Keep static gates current and record that real compile proof requires Unity import/project regeneration or Unity MCP console access.
Rejected Alternatives: Manually editing Unity-generated .csproj files was rejected because those files are generated artifacts and would create churn. Running known false-negative build was rejected because it wastes machine time and pollutes logs.
Scalability potential: No runtime impact; this protects iteration hardware during multi-agent batch.
Hardware Impact: Avoided meaningless compile wall and preserved user's build-protection mandate.
Loop 18 - Saturating Finalize Counters
Problem: EntityDeltaFinalizeJob accumulated block-level uint counters with unchecked +=. Normal entity counts are far below overflow, but corrupted counter row or future larger capacity could wrap to small payload size and make downstream validation reason about false bytes.
Solution: Added SaturatingAdd(uint,uint) and applied it to delta, active, tombstone, dense-byte, pruned, and dehydrated aggregate counters. Overflow now clamps high and then saturates to int.MaxValue at counter export boundary.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving natural wrap was rejected because it creates silent corruption. Promoting all counters to ulong was rejected for this patch because public counter buffer and telemetry fields are currently int/uint; saturating aggregation hardens existing ABI without widening DTOs.
Scalability potential: Low through Ultra share same overflow-safe math; no quality branch is introduced.
Hardware Impact: Adds few scalar comparisons in one-row finalize job per save, not per entity. It prevents bad capacity math from reaching WAL pack.
Loop 19 - Canonical Endian Record Stream
Problem: Dense entity records were previously moved into RLE stream with raw DTO MemCpy. That is fast on current little-endian Unity targets, but it makes WAL payload implicitly host-endian and could silently hydrate corrupt coordinates, hashes, or float locals if legacy/network bytes arrive in another byte order.
Solution: EntityDeltaDensePackJob now writes each EntityDeltaDataRecordDTO field to dense bytes through fixed little-endian offsets. EntityRlePreconditionJob marks stream with RleStreamFlagLittleEndianRecords; validation rejects ambiguous streams with no endian marker, both endian markers, or non-whole-record dense byte counts. Extraction and replay hydration reject non-finite local AUP offsets by setting fatal counter instead of writing corrupt positions. replay expansion job now hydrates records through explicit little-endian or big-endian readers and writes back through UnsafeUtility.AsRef instead of raw record MemCpy. EntityLz4CompressionJob also rejects zero-length hash tables and clamps active hash slots to actual Vault hash-table length.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping host-endian MemCpy was rejected because it treats platform byte order as unstated contract. Converting outer WAL header only was rejected because payload records are actual authority data. Adding managed BinaryReader/BinaryWriter was rejected by zero-GC and raw-byte mandate.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra still share one payload format. Quality changes compression effort and write cadence only; endian correctness does not fork by hardware tier.
Hardware Impact: Adds fixed scalar stores/loads per changed entity during save/load worker jobs. Expected i3/MX350 cost is bounded by delta count and buys deterministic replay safety; no main-thread stall, allocation, or extra Vault ownership is introduced.
Loop 20 - Global Authority Route Card
Problem: compressor adds/uses long-lived GlobalDataVault and WAL persistence route. rationale paragraph is not enough under GLOBALAUTHORITYROUTECARDTEMPLATE.md; missing owner/phase/cadence/failure/proof fields would leave route reviewable only by tribal memory.
Solution: Added Docs/Tasks/RouteSHINOBU154EntityDeltaCompression.md with route ID SAVEENTITYDELTAWALRLELZ4, owner, instrument, producer/consumer phase, cadence, quality behavior, buffer IDs, capacity, failure mode, telemetry fields, stale-handle behavior, rejected alternatives, monolith risk, and proof requirements. Review result is deliberately YELLOW because Unity/Burst/profiler/WAL replay artifacts are still absent.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating status checklist as route card was rejected because it lacks template's shutdown, stale-handle, and review-result fields. Marking GREEN was rejected because route is runtime-facing and static source is not runtime proof.
Scalability potential: Route card locks one format and one owner across Low/Middle/High/Ultra; quality only changes cadence and compression effort.
Hardware Impact: Documentation-only; no runtime cost. It reduces integration ambiguity for multi-agent batch.
Loop 21 - Native Range Alias Guard
Problem: Burst job fields are marked NoAlias, but that promise was previously enforced only by distinct Vault buffer IDs and route discipline. bad integration test or stale Vault resolver could still pass overlapping NativeArray views and make compiler's no-alias assumption false.
Solution: Added stack-only native byte-range overlap guards before save and replay scheduling. HasCompressionPipelineAliasViolation covers current/baseline/delta records, block counters, dense/RLE/compressed/WAL bytes, LZ4 hash table, headers, counters, telemetry, tuning, sector stats, and profiles. HasWalDecodeAliasViolation covers WAL source, RLE destination, dense destination, hydrated records, headers, and counters. Alias failure schedules EntityScheduleFailureJob, deterministic Burst job that sets fatal counters/header/stats and returns tracked JobHandle without starting unsafe pipeline.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting BufferID uniqueness alone was rejected because NoAlias is code-generation contract, not documentation wish. Blocking with JobHandle.Complete() to inspect data was rejected because alias detection needs only pointer ranges and must not serialize pipeline. Allocating managed list of ranges was rejected by zero-GC policy; guard uses fixed stackalloc ranges.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra all use same guard. It adds bounded pre-schedule pointer-range scan and does not change compression quality math.
Hardware Impact: O(16^2) cold scheduling comparisons for save and O(6^2) for replay. Expected cost is below profiler noise compared to entity scanning; it prevents undefined Burst vectorization behavior on all CPUs, including ARM64 NEON.
Loop 23 - Scheduling Profiler Anchors
Problem: route card still had Profiler marker: pending, leaving no named profiler anchor for main-thread scheduling cost even though runtime proof remains unavailable.
Solution: Added static ProfilerMarkers around ScheduleCompressionPipeline and ScheduleWalPayloadDecodePipeline: H8.Save.EntityDelta.ScheduleCompression and H8.Save.EntityDelta.ScheduleDecode. markers stay outside Burst jobs and therefore do not introduce managed profiler scopes into worker kernels.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding ProfilerMarker.Auto() inside Burst jobs was rejected because those jobs must remain unmanaged mathematical kernels. Leaving route-card profiler fields empty was rejected because acceptance requires named capture points.
Scalability potential: Markers are tier-independent. They expose scheduling cost while quality continues to affect compression effort and cadence.
Hardware Impact: Cold static profiler marker allocation at domain load, stack-scope marker on scheduling calls. No per-entity cost and no gameplay DTO bloat.
Loop 24 - Alias Range Capacity Clamp
Problem: pre-schedule alias guard used fixed stack ranges sized exactly to current save/replay buffer count. That was correct today but brittle: later buffer addition could write past stack range before overlap scan ran.
Solution: Added explicit RangeCapacity constants and changed helper to TryAddNativeRange. If created native range would exceed stack capacity, guard returns alias violation and schedules existing fatal failure job instead of silently skipping unchecked buffer.
Rejected Alternatives: Allocating managed range list was rejected by zero-GC policy. Silently ignoring overflow was rejected because it would preserve stack safety while weakening NoAlias proof.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra use same bounded guard; no quality branch is introduced.
Hardware Impact: One integer compare per potential range during scheduling. This is below measurable worker cost and prevents stack overwrite in compile-wall lane.
Loop 25 - Unity Compile Wall Attempt
Problem: Static gates cannot prove Burst import, generated asset inclusion, or Unity compiler acceptance. CPU/dotnet gates opened, so next valid proof path was Unity batchmode, not stale generated .csproj build.
Solution: Ran Unity 6000.4.1f1 batchmode with log Docs/AgentLogs/UnitySHINOBU154Compile.log. import log lists Assets/Project/Scripts/SaveSystem/EntityDeltaCompressionArchitecture.cs, EntityDeltaGizmoProbe.cs, Editor/EntitySaveTunerWindow.cs, and H8BinaryWorldPager.cs in script asset set. Compilation then failed on non-SHINOBU domains before clean project-wide proof could exist.
Rejected Alternatives: Running dotnet build Hecton8.Core.csproj was rejected because generated projects still omit new SHINOBU assets. Fixing Physics/HabitatFluidIncursionJobs.cs, Narrative, Wreckage, Coral, or Hecton8.MockDomain.Runtime from this SaveSystem lane was rejected as domain sabotage.
Scalability potential: No runtime change. failed proof preserves ownership: SaveSystem remains owner-local while compile-wall owners must fix their own assemblies.
Hardware Impact: Unity script compilation took 40.599537 seconds and exited with return code 1 due external compile errors. No SHINOBU file diagnostic appears in compile log, but Task 20 cannot be marked green until dependency wall is removed and Unity/Burst profiler proof is rerun.
Loop 26 - Native Safety Proof Comments
Problem: GenerateMockEntityStateJob, EntityTombstonePruneJob, and ExtractEntityDeltaJob use NativeDisableParallelForRestriction for block-partitioned writes. code was partition-safe, but source only carried one-line comments; that fails native-memory mandate's review standard for suppressed safety checks.
Solution: Added explicit SAFETYJUSTIFICATIONPARAGRAPH1..3 blocks above every suppressed field group. proof states false-positive safety check, rejected alternatives, and exact partition invariant: mock writes own index N, prune owns record block B and counter B, extraction owns delta block B MaxDeltasPerBlock, +MaxDeltasPerBlock) and counter B.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing attribute was rejected because partitioned/block append jobs need ref writes and non-index-equal slices. Replacing design with global atomics or NativeListbyte.ParallelWriter was rejected because it would add contention, allocator/growth risk, and unstable append order to Vault-owned save lane.
Scalability potential: No runtime branch changed. Low/Middle/High/Ultra retain same continuous compression curve; proof prevents future "safe looking" edits from breaking partition invariant.
Hardware Impact: Source-comment hardening has zero runtime cost. Static gates after edit: brace/Burst parity OPEN=308 CLOSE=308 JOBS=17 BURSTDIRECTIVES=17, forbidden hot-path pattern scan empty, direct sibling using scan empty, git diff --check clean for compressor file. Guarded build not launched because CPU telemetry was 59 percent.
Loop 27 - Editor Tuner Telemetry Throttle
Problem: EntitySaveTunerWindow.Update() was editor-only, but it still polled GlobalDataVault, rebuilt summary text, and could repaint histogram every editor frame. That violates spirit of Task 17 "real-time zero-GC histogram" facade because editor repaint noise hides real runtime compressor cost.
Solution: Added 0.25 second telemetry refresh gate, cached last telemetry cursor and payload fields, and only repaints histogram when telemetry actually changes. Replaced per-control callback lambdas with cached UI Toolkit callbacks. Replaced ToString/string-concat summary formatting with fixed 192-char buffer and explicit decimal/hex writers; remaining new string is documented as unavoidable UI Toolkit Label.text editor boundary and is reached only after telemetry changes, not every editor frame.
Rejected Alternatives: Moving editor window into runtime UI was rejected because Task 17 explicitly asks for editor facade. Leaving per-frame Label.text formatting was rejected because it makes editor profiler lie about save-system overhead. Attempting to make UI Toolkit Label consume raw char was rejected because its public text surface is managed string; actual histogram draw remains Vault-driven and string-free.
Scalability potential: Low uses same 4Hz editor telemetry poll and does not chase every autosave graph repaint. Middle/High/Ultra can inspect denser telemetry without adding runtime payload fields or changing continuous compression curve.
Hardware Impact: Runtime impact is zero; file is under #if UNITYEDITOR. Editor overhead is reduced from per-frame Vault/summary/repaint work to 4Hz cursor-change gated work. Static proof: runtime forbidden-pattern scan remains empty, editor brace parity is OPEN=45 CLOSE=45, and build was not launched because CPU sampled at 99.6 percent with external dotnet compiler-host processes running.
Loop 28 - Reflectionless Self-Audit Offsets
Problem: RunSelfAudit() used Marshal.OffsetOf(typeof(...), nameof(...)) through cold helper. That was not hot-path allocation source, but it still left runtime self-audit dependent on reflection-style field lookup and string names inside production SaveSystem file.
Solution: Removed HeaderFieldOffset(string) helper and replaced every self-audit field-offset proof with explicit pointer-delta helpers over stack DTOs using UnsafeUtility.AddressOf. audit now derives offsets for EntityDeltaHeaderDTO, EntityDeltaDataRecordDTO, and EntityDeltaRleStreamHeaderDTO without Marshal.OffsetOf, typeof, GetField, or reflection namespaces.
Rejected Alternatives: Hard-coding offset constants in audit was rejected because it would duplicate struct declarations and could drift silently. Keeping Marshal.OffsetOf was rejected because Task 20 is supposed to prove unmanaged layout with same unsafe memory primitives used by runtime lane, not metadata lookup.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra runtime behavior is unchanged; this is cold audit hardening. proof path now remains valid if SaveSystem lane is later split into its own asmdef with reflection restrictions.
Hardware Impact: No runtime hot-path microseconds claimed. Static checks after patch: no reflection/offset lookup signatures in SHINOBU files, runtime forbidden-pattern scan empty, direct sibling namespace scan empty, and parity OPEN=317 CLOSE=317 JOBS=17 BURSTDIRECTIVES=17 SAFETYPARAGRAPHS=9. Build was not launched because CPU sampled at 100 percent.
Loop 29 - Canonical Little-Endian Black-Box Dump
Problem: TryDumpTelemetryRing wrote dump header and telemetry rows with raw host-endian memory spans. That path is cold diagnostics, but black-box crash evidence is binary artifact and must not depend on CPU byte order or struct padding interpretation.
Solution: Replaced raw dump writes with explicit little-endian field packing. dump now verifies that header and telemetry row strides are 64 bytes, stack-packs EntityDeltaTelemetryDumpHeaderDTO fields, stack-packs every EntityCompressionTelemetryEntry row, and writes float fields through math.asuint.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw ReadOnlySpanbyte((byte)&header, ...) and raw ring-row spans was rejected because it repeats exact host-endian assumption already removed from WAL records. Adding managed BinaryWriter or byte staging buffer was rejected by zero-GC/raw-byte mandate.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra runtime compression behavior is unchanged; this affects forensic dump portability only. 300-frame ring remains fixed-size and owner-local.
Hardware Impact: No hot-path microseconds claimed. Dump work is cold failure/latency-spike I/O. Static proof after patch: forbidden runtime/reflection scan empty, direct sibling namespace scan empty, trailing whitespace clean, parity OPEN=318 CLOSE=318 JOBS=17 BURSTDIRECTIVES=17 SAFETYPARAGRAPHS=9; build was not launched because CPU sampled at 100 percent.
Loop 30 - Canonical Emergency Schema Bytes
Problem: GenerateEmergencyMockEntitySchema wrote 64-byte fallback schema header by raw-copying EntityDeltaMockSchemaDTO into Vault schema byte buffer. This was cold boot only, but fallback schema is binary payload contract and cannot rely on host-endian struct memory.
Solution: Replaced raw UnsafeUtility.MemCpy schema header copy with WriteMockSchemaLittleEndian, which writes Magic, SchemaHash, Version, header/record byte sizes, defaults, seed, and padding through explicit little-endian field stores.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving randomized filler plus host-endian DTO copy was rejected because it contradicts canonical WAL and dump byte-order rules. Adding managed serializer or BinaryWriter was rejected by raw-byte and zero-GC mandates.
Scalability potential: Low/Middle/High/Ultra runtime compression behavior is unchanged. fallback schema remains deterministic and CI-safe; only cold byte contract is hardened.
Hardware Impact: No hot-path microseconds claimed. Cold schema generation replaces one 64-byte memcpy with fixed scalar stores. Static proof after patch: forbidden runtime/reflection scan empty, direct sibling namespace scan empty, trailing whitespace clean, parity OPEN=318 CLOSE=318 JOBS=17 BURSTDIRECTIVES=17 SAFETYPARAGRAPHS=9; build was not launched because CPU sampled at 100 percent.
Loop 31 - Aggregate Byte-Savings Audit
Problem: telemetry ratio audit counted samples where compressed bytes were merely smaller than full snapshot bytes. That proves "usually smaller", not stronger 99 percent byte-savings claim implied by Task 20 acceptance language.
Solution: Added integer PPM aggregate audit math. RunCompressionRatioSelfAudit and EntityDeltaCompressionRatioAuditJob now accumulate full and compressed bytes across 300-frame telemetry ring, compute compressed ratio and savings in millionths, and require both sample pass ratio and aggregate byte-savings threshold. New counters are CounterAuditCompressedRatioPpm, CounterAuditSavingsPpm, and CounterAuditByteSavingsPass.
Rejected Alternatives: Floating-point aggregate ratios were rejected because audit is deterministic proof, not presentation. Keeping old sample-only test was rejected because payload at 99 percent of full size would pass even though it saves almost nothing.
Scalability potential: Low uses audit to detect whether quality/load shedding is still producing real byte wins. Middle/High/Ultra can spend more LZ4 effort, but proof threshold is same and does not fork payload contract.
Hardware Impact: Fixed 300-entry telemetry scan with integer additions/division in existing audit job. No per-entity hot-path work is added; expected i3/MX350 impact is below profiler noise and remains pending Unity/Burst proof. Static gates after patch: forbidden runtime/reflection scan empty, direct sibling namespace scan empty, touched-file trailing whitespace clean, scoped diff check clean with CRLF warnings only, parity OPEN=321 CLOSE=321 JOBS=17 BURSTDIRECTIVES=17; build was not launched because CPU sampled 100 percent.
Loop 32 - WAL Failure Hygiene and Counter Reuse Guard
Problem: EntityWalPayloadPackJob returned silently when its counter buffer was short or its header/source buffers were invalid. main pipeline resolves valid Vault buffers, but isolated tests or stale integration handles could leave previous WAL byte count visible. decode path also reset decode counters but left audit counters stale when reusing same counter row for replay.
Solution: EntityWalPayloadPackJob now requires CounterCapacity; if counters are valid but headers/source buffers are missing or empty it writes CounterFailure, HeaderFlagFatal, and zero WAL bytes. EntityWalPayloadDecodeJob.ResetDecodeCounters now clears CounterAuditSamples, CounterAuditSmallerPayloads, CounterAuditPass, CounterAuditCompressedRatioPpm, CounterAuditSavingsPpm, and CounterAuditByteSavingsPass.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving invalid pack inputs as no-op was rejected because no-op is indistinguishable from stale success when counters are reused. Adding separate managed guard wrapper was rejected because Burst job already owns byte-boundary failure state.
Scalability potential: No quality branch changed. Low/Middle/High/Ultra share same deterministic failure semantics; compression curve remains driven by GlobalQualityWeight.
Hardware Impact: Adds few scalar checks and counter writes on failure/replay reset only. No per-entity hot-path work is added. Static gates after patch: forbidden runtime/reflection scan empty, direct sibling namespace scan empty, touched-file trailing whitespace clean, scoped diff check clean with CRLF warnings only, parity OPEN=321 CLOSE=321 JOBS=17 BURSTDIRECTIVES=17; build was not launched because CPU sampled 100 percent.
Loop 33 - Cross-Stage Stale Counter Scrub
Problem: Several Burst stages could still leave stale success evidence when invoked by isolated tests or stale Vault aliases outside normal full pipeline. Dense pack only zeroed dense bytes, RLE precondition treated missing headers as silent return, LZ4 silently returned on missing mandatory buffers, WAL decode failure left old byte counters possible outside normal reset path, and RLE expand failure left previous dense/decode counts visible.
Solution: Dense pack, RLE precondition, and LZ4 now fail closed when mandatory inputs are missing after valid counter row is present. Failure paths clear downstream byte counts, WAL payload/audit pass, decode counts, and compression audit counters while setting HeaderFlagFatal. WAL decode and RLE expand failure paths now also scrub byte/decode counters instead of relying on caller ordering.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting happy-path ScheduleCompressionPipeline ordering was rejected because Task 20 must survive replay/autopsy tooling and CI mocks that call stages independently. Adding managed wrapper validation was rejected because authoritative failure state belongs in same Burst jobs that own counter row.
Scalability potential: No quality tier branch changed. Low/Middle/High/Ultra keep same GlobalQualityWeight compression curve; this pass only makes failure evidence deterministic under stale-handle or partial-pipeline conditions.
Hardware Impact: Adds scalar counter writes only on invalid/failure paths and few mandatory-input checks at stage entry. No per-entity hot-path work is added. Static gates after patch: forbidden runtime/reflection scan empty, direct sibling namespace scan empty, touched-file trailing whitespace clean, scoped diff check clean with CRLF warnings only, parity OPEN=328 CLOSE=328 JOBS=17 BURSTDIRECTIVES=17; build was not launched because CPU sampled 100 percent.
