Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays flat generation checks when path APIs or tick phases touch Vault lanes. dominant cost remains bounded scan of active corridors against WFC cell masks; stale pointer metadata is removed from path invalidation state.
Decision 040 - WFC laser cut tool writes Vault progress through phase-local arrays
Problem: WfcLaserCutRuntime.cs persisted two static VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and converted their cached .ptr fields into raw float progress and telemetry pointers. same file used GlobalRegistry.ScalabilityTier for visual overkill, producing hard tier branch in user-facing VFX path.
Solution: Convert cut progress and blackbox lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve local NativeArrayT views per cut attempt, and rewrite progress clear/telemetry/dump paths to index those views instead of pointers. Replace tier branching with continuous smoothstep over HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight, modulated by system stress headroom.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw pointers as "short-lived" locals was rejected because they were derived from persistent pointer-bearing descriptors and used in gameplay truth writes. Keeping tier switch was rejected because quality-weight already supplies required continuous control scalar.
Scalability potential: Low devices collapse molten/spark overkill smoothly as quality/stress drops; middle/high/ultra regain richer cut visuals continuously without feature pop. No binary quality branch remains in this file.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation checks per active cut attempt and few scalar ops for visual curve. expensive work remains shader feedback and signal fanout; stale Vault pointer writes are removed from tool path.
Decision 041 - Ladder climb IK schedules only generation-resolved views
Problem: ProceduralLadderClimbRuntime.cs persisted five VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and staged its IK solve job through .Resolve(dataVault) views. Disable/destroy only cleared handles, leaving Vault refcount/generation state untouched.
Solution: Convert IK input/output, ladder AUP, telemetry ring, and telemetry cursor descriptors to VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve method-local views before reads/writes/scheduling, and release five owned descriptors after completing any outstanding IK job during teardown or DataVault replacement/loss.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handles because this is presentation IK was rejected; job consumes Vault-backed AUP and telemetry data and can race relocation if manager keeps pointer metadata. Owner-wide release was rejected in favor of exact descriptor release.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same cheap slide/grip solve cadence; middle/high/ultra retain richer IK targets and telemetry without pointer retention. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays five generation checks when staging or reading IK views. dominant cost remains Burst IK solve; stale Vault handle metadata is removed from animation locomotion.
Decision 042 - Tool haptics front/back lanes stop refreshing legacy handles
Problem: ToolHapticsRuntime.cs persisted front/back VaultBufferHandleHapticCommand descriptors and called ResolveBuffer(ref handle) before every haptic buffer access, keeping pointer-bearing metadata alive in manager.
Solution: Convert both lanes to VaultGenerationHandleHapticCommand, cache active IDataVault, resolve local NativeArrayHapticCommand views per haptic operation, and release old descriptors on DataVault loss/replacement or teardown.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping ReadOnlySpan snapshots as only change was rejected because stale descriptor route would still exist before span is created. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact front/back descriptors are known.
Scalability potential: Low devices still compact and decay 16-command buffer; middle/high/ultra keep richer command blending and sinusoidal feedback without pointer retention. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation compare per front/back lane access. dominant haptic work remains bounded command compaction/merge; stale Vault metadata is removed from tool rumble.
Decision 043 - Procedural bone blender schedules only generation-resolved views
Problem: ProceduralBoneBlenderRuntime.cs persisted eleven VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and used .Resolve(vault) in editor, CSV, mock rig, telemetry, GPU upload, and Burst scheduling paths. Disable/destroy and DataVault replacement cleared descriptors without releasing owned Vault lanes.
Solution: Convert all fauna procedural bone lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT, add shared resolve/acquire helper that uses IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, resolve NativeArrayT views only inside active method/phase, and release exact descriptors after completing outstanding solver jobs on disable, destroy, or DataVault replacement.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy descriptors for editor-only routes was rejected because those same handles feed runtime solver and telemetry paths. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact buffer IDs are known and broader release would cross another owner boundary if future lanes share SystemID.AnimationFauna.
Scalability potential: Low devices still collapse update cadence through existing continuous GlobalQualityWeight; middle/high/ultra keep GPU matrix upload and richer procedural bone response without pointer retention. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays eleven generation compares when staging fauna solve and few compares on editor/telemetry reads. dominant cost remains Burst solve and GPU buffer copy; stale Vault metadata is removed from animation path.
Decision 044 - Kinetic character animator removes descriptor and direct-view debt
Problem: KineticCharacterAnimatorRuntime.cs persisted twelve VaultBufferHandleT descriptors, resolved them through .Resolve(vault), and also fetched PlayerKinematicState / VoxelSdfTexture3D through direct TryGetBuffer calls. Teardown and DataVault replacement cleared descriptor fields without releasing Vault lanes.
Solution: Convert all locomotion animation lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT, add generation-checked owned and external resolve helpers, route player and SDF reads through method-local TryGetGenerationHandle + TryResolveHandle, and release exact owned descriptors after solver completion on disable, destroy, and DataVault replacement.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping TryGetBuffer for external read-only lanes was rejected because read-only does not make stale aliases safe after relocation. Releasing all SystemID.AnimationLocomotion buffers was rejected because adjacent locomotion runtimes can share owner ID.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain existing continuous quality-weighted locomotion/SDF degradation; middle/high/ultra keep richer IK and GPU matrix output without persistent Vault views. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays twelve generation compares for owned staging and two local external descriptor resolves on player/SDF frames. dominant cost remains Burst locomotion/matrix work; stale Vault descriptors and direct external Vault views are removed from manager.
Decision 045 - Laser cutter scalability read uses generation descriptor
Problem: LaserCutterDodRuntime.cs had one remaining TryGetBufferHandle route for ShinobuScalabilityState, leaving legacy descriptor path inside otherwise generation-descriptor tool runtime.
Solution: Replace quality-weight read with TryGetGenerationHandleScalabilityStateDTO and TryResolveHandle, keeping resolved NativeArrayScalabilityStateDTO local to ResolveGlobalQualityWeight().
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping old route because it is read-only was rejected; relocation still invalidates pointer-bearing handle metadata regardless of write intent.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra visuals continue to use same continuous quality scalar; only descriptor acquisition route changed.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 cost is one generation handle resolve on quality reads. It removes final legacy handle API hit in this runtime without changing cut math.
Decision 046 - Tool kinematics editor facade stops using legacy handles
Problem: ToolKinematicsTunerWindow.cs cached seven VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and used ResolveBuffer(ref handle) / .Resolve(vault) while Play Mode editor tuning can observe and mutate live Vault lanes.
Solution: Convert editor descriptors to VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve local editor views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, and release exactly editor-acquired descriptors when window closes or Vault reference changes.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating editor windows as harmless was rejected because they run against Play Mode memory and can hold stale descriptors across defrag/rebind events.
Scalability potential: Runtime scalability is unchanged; editor facade now observes same quality-weighted tool kinematics state without preserving pointer-bearing handles.
Hardware Impact: No player-frame cost. Editor draws pay generation checks while tuner window is open; stale Vault metadata is removed from facade.
Decision 047 - Tool kinematics runtime drops legacy handles and ref-return API
Problem: ToolKinematicsRuntime.cs persisted fifteen VaultBufferHandleT descriptors, resolved them through ResolveBuffer(ref handle) / .Resolve(vault), and exposed unused public ToolKinematicsVaultAccess class that returned refs via GetElementAsRef.
Solution: Convert all runtime lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve method-local NativeArrayT views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, release exact descriptors on disable/destroy or Vault rebind, and remove unused ref-return accessor class.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping ref-return accessor with generation handles was rejected because returning refs from transient views invites callers to keep byref access beyond safe execution phase. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact ToolKinematics buffer IDs are known.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous LOD hold and beam raymarch limits; middle/high/ultra keep richer tool beam/IK/spark output without persistent Vault descriptors. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays fifteen generation compares while staging tool jobs. dominant cost remains Burst raymarch/beam jobs; stale Vault descriptor metadata and public byref mutation routes are removed.
Decision 048 - Tool durability removes false-positive legacy naming
Problem: ToolDurabilitySystem.cs already used VaultGenerationHandleT and TryResolveHandle, but its local helper was named TryResolveBuffer, which caused broad legacy Vault scans to surface false-positive ResolveBuffer-like route.
Solution: Rename helper and callers to TryResolveDurabilityView without changing allocation, BufferID, DTO, or job behavior.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving name was rejected because audit noise slows detection of real stale pointer routes in tools and animation.
Scalability potential: Runtime scalability is unchanged; durability still uses existing generation-descriptor state lanes.
Hardware Impact: No runtime change. benefit is audit precision: broad scans now separate safe generation views from forbidden legacy resolve calls.
Decision 049 - Vocal warning manager stops storing Vault aliases
Problem: VocalWarningSystem.cs persisted six Vault-backed NativeArrayT aliases and six legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for queue, warning state, and telemetry lanes. Vault relocation after boot could leave manager indexing stale array metadata.
Solution: Replace all six descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, add phase-local VwsVaultViews value, resolve views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle inside queue mutation, slow tick, telemetry, and dump paths, and release exact descriptors during teardown/rebind.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping aliases because VWS has no Burst job was rejected; UAF risk is independent of job scheduling. ReleaseOwnerBuffers was rejected because exact BufferIDs are known and owner-wide teardown hides descriptor ownership mistakes.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same small priority queue and cooldown cadence; middle/high/ultra keep full warning telemetry and radio-degrade presentation. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays six generation compares on VWS mutation/slow paths. This is below clip submission and subtitle routing cost and removes stale Vault metadata from audio warning manager.
Decision 050 - Native audio frame ring resolves buffers per operation
Problem: NativeAudioFrameRingBuffer.cs persisted Vault-backed frames and sharedState aliases plus two VaultBufferHandleT descriptors. native output ring also exports raw pointers to audio bridge, so cached manager aliases were direct relocation hazard.
Solution: Replace both handles with VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve local RingVaultViews value for buffer state, writes, clearing, shared metadata access, and native descriptor creation, and release exact frame/shared-state descriptors on dispose.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping frames/sharedState because ring is internal was rejected; internal managers still survive across defrag. Owner-wide release was rejected because ring owns exactly two known BufferIDs.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain same bounded SPSC copy and overflow drop reporting; middle/high/ultra keep larger ring capacities and native bridge output without retaining stale managed-side Vault aliases.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation compares for ring state/write/descriptor operations. hot cost remains sample copy and native plugin handoff; stale manager-resident Vault aliases are removed.
Decision 051 - Dynamic music resolves DSP buffers from generation views
Problem: DynamicMusicGranularSynthesizer.cs persisted Vault-backed arrays for DSP voices, scalars, tuning, output buffers, biquad, telemetry, CSV scratch, preset rules, grain bank, shared state, and scalability state. It also cached output pointers. bounded Vault relocation would invalidate those aliases while manager, editor facade, audio callback, or scheduled jobs still believed metadata was stable.
Solution: Replace all owned descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, add method-local DynamicMusicVaultViews resolver, pass local views into editor/cold CSV/audio/job/telemetry paths, take raw pointers only immediately before job scheduling or file/native copy, and release exact owned descriptors on teardown. external scalability state is borrowed through TryGetGenerationHandle and resolved transiently.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached aliases because this is audio system was rejected; audio paths are relocation-sensitive and must not retain stale manager-side Vault metadata. Releasing by owner was rejected because synth owns fixed BufferID set and exact release exposes descriptor drift.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous density/cutoff/sample cadence collapse through GlobalQualityWeight; middle/high/ultra keep full granular voices, telemetry, and stinger richness. No binary hardware branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation checks at scheduling/cold/editor/audio-copy boundaries. hot DSP loop still runs from phase-local pointers inside Burst jobs; stale persistent aliases are removed without adding GC.
Decision 052 - Adaptive stem mixer stops retaining Vault aliases
Problem: AdaptiveStemAudioMixer.cs persisted eleven Vault-backed arrays and eleven legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for stem state, commands, rules, mock signal rows, telemetry, CSV scratch, and scalability state. mixer also used binary low/high scalability fallback after signal ingress.
Solution: Replace owned descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, add method-local AdaptiveStemVaultViews resolver, resolve views before editor/tick/job/telemetry/CSV operations, borrow scalability state through TryGetGenerationHandle, release owned descriptors exactly, and map HectonQualityTier through Smooth01 into continuous 0.1..1.0 fallback weight.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping aliases because mixer is presentation-only was rejected; presentation systems still schedule Burst jobs and can crash after relocation. Binary LowMx350 ? 0.1f : 1f was rejected because it creates hard quality discontinuity.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep slow update cadence and cheap crossfade; middle/high/ultra smoothly restore faster cadence and richer stem blending without branch pop.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation checks on mixer phase boundaries, not per sample. gain is removing stale Vault aliases from adaptive-stem job scheduling and telemetry paths.
Decision 053 - Player critical renderer first removes pointer-bearing ownership
Problem: PlayerCriticalProceduralAudioRenderer.cs is last large audio file with broad Vault debt. It held 50 persistent NativeArrayT aliases and acquired them through pointer-bearing VaultBufferHandleT plus handle.Resolve; teardown used owner-wide release.
Solution: First isolate ownership from pointer metadata: add 50 VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors, make central ResolveVaultBuffer helper use GetGenerationHandle plus TryResolveHandle, and replace owner-wide release with exact release of known descriptors after outstanding audio/SDF/composite jobs are completed.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting entire 11k-line renderer in one pass was rejected because producer thread, sonar jobs, VWS double buffer, and reverb state share lifetime constraints. Keeping VaultBufferHandleT until final pass was rejected because it leaves highest-risk pointer-bearing API in largest audio owner.
Scalability potential: Runtime audio quality behavior is unchanged in this slice. Low/middle/high/ultra renderer math and existing perceptual audio fakes remain stable while ownership metadata becomes generation-checked.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays no new sample-loop cost. Bind/release paths pay O(buffer-count) generation descriptor work; remaining work is phase-local view migration for persistent aliases.
Decision 054 - Player critical low-risk rings move to phase-local views
Problem: After descriptor ownership was fixed, PlayerCritical still kept 50 persistent Vault aliases. smallest safe runtime slice was isolated VWS double-buffer lane plus granular/prologue telemetry and prologue command rings; these are bounded and do not require rewriting full producer DSP graph.
Solution: Remove five persistent NativeArrayT fields and resolve VWS clip buffers, granular telemetry, prologue transition telemetry, and prologue transition command rings through generation handles at operation boundaries. Keep producer sample loops free of per-sample resolve calls.
Rejected Alternatives: Attempting to migrate all frame scratch/reverb/sonar/granular voice arrays in one patch was rejected because those arrays cross audio producer loop and scheduled sonar jobs. Deferring all aliases was rejected because isolated rings were easy to harden immediately.
Scalability potential: No visual/audio quality behavior changed. Low-tier and high-tier renderer fakes keep their existing cadence; postmortem and VWS lanes now survive relocation more predictably.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays O(1) generation checks on VWS submit/playback, prologue queue, and telemetry operations. No inner DSP loop resolve was introduced.
Decision 055 - Player critical granular SOA resolves once per producer block
Problem: PlayerCritical still retained metallic grain bank and eight granular voice SOA buffers as long-lived NativeArrayT fields. Those arrays are mutated in audio-rate code, so resolving them per sample would be correct but too expensive; keeping them as fields preserved stale-alias UAF risk.
Solution: Remove nine persistent aliases, add GranularVoiceVaultViews, resolve view once in CanProduceAudioBlock, pass it through RenderHullStressBlock, RenderStructuralGranularVoices, and MixAndFilterBlock, and update voice arm/trim/slot helpers to mutate local NativeArray descriptors copied from phase view.
Rejected Alternatives: whole-renderer DSP view was deferred because sonar/reverb/frame scratch buffers cross scheduled jobs and require separate dependency pass. Per-voice/per-sample resolution was rejected because it burns audio-thread cycles without improving safety over block-scoped view.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain cheap granular voice budgets and linear envelopes; middle/high/ultra still unlock denser voice counts and interpolation through existing continuous tuning. migration does not add hardware binary branch.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays nine generation validations once per produced block. hot sample loop reuses local NativeArray descriptors and keeps existing O(active voices) granular fake instead of heavier structural simulation.
Decision 056 - Player critical binaural and low-pass state resolves once per producer block
Problem: Binaural ITD delay, ear-shadow history, and final listener low-pass histories remained as long-lived NativeArrayT fields. They are small, but they are mutated every producer block and are still invalid after Vault relocation.
Solution: Remove six aliases, add BinauralFilterVaultViews, resolve it once in CanProduceAudioBlock, pass it by ref through MixAndFilterBlock and ApplyBinauralSpatializationBlock, and resolve same view in ClearLowPassState for cold reset.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping histories as fields because they are tiny was rejected; UAF risk is independent of byte count. Resolving inside SampleBinauralDelay or ApplyBinauralShadowEar was rejected because those functions execute per sample/ear and would add avoidable validation branches.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous binaural mix, underwater shadow cutoff, narcosis chorus, and abyssal low-pass curves stay unchanged from low through ultra. change is pointer-lifetime only.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays six generation validations per produced block. per-sample binaural and low-pass loops use local descriptors and keep their existing arithmetic profile.
Decision 057 - Player critical reverb state resolves once per producer block
Problem: Sabine reverb, cave convolution, and interior FDN delay buffers remained as persistent NativeArrayT fields. These are among larger PlayerCritical buffers and are mutated in hot sample loops, so stale aliases can crash and per-sample resolution would be too expensive.
Solution: Remove four aliases, add ReverbVaultViews, resolve view once in CanProduceAudioBlock, pass local descriptors through Sabine comb, cave convolution, and interior FDN helpers, and resolve same generation view for cold impulse bake and reset clears.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping reverb fields because they are audio-private was rejected; Vault relocation can invalidate audio-private views exactly like cross-domain views. Resolving inside each comb/convolution tap was rejected because it would multiply handle validation by sample count and tap count.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous reverb DSP tier selection, wet mix, openness, and acoustic density curves remain unchanged. Low devices still fall back to cheaper Unity/profile-only paths; high/ultra keep native Sabine/convolution richness.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays four generation validations per produced block. Hot reverb loops keep local NativeArray descriptors and avoid new branches inside comb, convolution, and FDN tap math.
Decision 058 - Player critical transient delay lines resolve once per producer block
Problem: Impact clang and thruster comb delay lines remained as persistent NativeArrayT fields. Both are small compared with reverb, but they are audio-rate mutable delay lines and can become stale after Vault relocation.
Solution: Remove two aliases, add TransientDelayVaultViews, resolve it once in CanProduceAudioBlock, pass it through impact event consumption, hull stress rendering, and thruster rendering, and clear it through method-local view during reset.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping these fields until frame-scratch pass was rejected because they are isolated and cheap to harden now. Resolving in RenderImpactClangSampleInternal or each thruster comb iteration was rejected because it would add per-sample validation.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous thruster pressure/cavitation and impact metallic fakes stay unchanged across low/mid/high/ultra. migration changes lifetime only.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation validations per produced block. Hot Karplus/comb loops use local NativeArray descriptors.
Decision 059 - Player critical frame scratch resolves once per producer block
Problem: Hull, sonar, impact echo, thruster, heartbeat, bubble, mix, and stereo scratch buffers were still manager-held NativeArrayT aliases. These buffers are re-used every audio block, so stale aliases would survive Vault relocation and crash in producer path.
Solution: Remove nine scratch aliases, add FrameScratchVaultViews, resolve view once in CanProduceAudioBlock, and pass it by ref into render, mix, and binaural stages. Cold reset and prologue probe paths resolve same view only for duration of their clear/probe operation.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping scratch fields because they are short-lived data was rejected; alias lifetime was manager lifetime, not scratch semantic lifetime. Resolving inside each render function was rejected where producer already has block view.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous quality curves for granular FM, reverb tier, binaural blend, and bubble intensity remain unchanged. Low devices pay one block-level validation set and keep same cheap DSP fakes; high/ultra keep dense procedural output.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays nine generation validations per produced block. Hot sample loops use local descriptors and retain prior arithmetic profile.
Decision 060 - Player critical sonar storage is split into phase-local Vault views
Problem: remaining sonar buffers were highest UAF risk: publish taps, worker taps, DSP echo delay/filter state, SDF hit cache, and composite coalescing scratch were all persistent NativeArrayT fields. Some are touched from read accessors, some from audio producer blocks, and some from scheduled jobs.
Solution: Remove all 15 sonar aliases and split resolution into SonarTapVaultViews, SonarDspVaultViews, and SonarSpatialVaultViews. UI read accessors resolve only tap buffers, audio DSP resolves tap+DSP state once per block, and SDF/composite phases resolve spatial buffers at schedule/publish boundaries. editor smoke test now verifies handle/view usage instead of stale fields.
Rejected Alternatives: single PlayerCriticalAudioVaultViews blob was rejected because TryGetCockpitSonarEchoTaps must stay pure read accessor and must not over-resolve DSP or SDF buffers. Per-tap generation resolution was rejected because it would multiply validation by echo count inside sonar publish loop.
Scalability potential: Sonar keeps existing capped echo tap fake and continuous SDF probe budget. Low devices use fewer probes/ghost taps through existing quality weights; high/ultra can keep richer SDF returns without changing authority or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes all sonar manager-held native aliases. Validation cost is bounded to phase entry: four checks for tap views, six for DSP views, five for spatial views. Delay/filter loops use local descriptors.
Decision 061 - Vocal warning pending queue is collapsed into Vault priority queue
Problem: VocalWarningSystem.cs still owned pendingWarningIds as private NativeQueuebyte allocated with Allocator.Persistent. It was tiny, but it was still manager-owned native allocation outside GlobalDataVault, and it duplicated Vault-backed AudioVocalWarningQueue fact.
Solution: Remove private NativeQueuebyte, pendingNativeCount, prewarm, drain, sentinel registration, and dispose path. TryQueueWarning now resolves VwsVaultViews once, writes cooldown/severity/source state, and inserts warning id directly into Vault-owned bounded priority queue via InsertOrPromote.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing queue with another Vault staging buffer was rejected because bounded priority queue already handles duplicate suppression, capacity, and priority replacement. Keeping staging queue because it is only 16 bytes was rejected because UAF and ownership violations are independent of capacity.
Scalability potential: Low devices skip extra staging dequeue pass on slow tick. Middle/high/ultra keep same warning priority behavior, telemetry ring, and radio-degrade presentation without changing DTO layout or authority route.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes one persistent native allocation and one TryDequeue drain loop per slow tick. TryQueueWarning already paid six generation checks for VWS state; direct insert reuses same resolved view and does not add sample-loop or job-loop cost.
Decision 062 - Spectrum sonar discovery and telemetry views move to Vault descriptors
Problem: SpectrumSystem.cs owned aupDiscoveryGrid and activeSonarGeoTelemetryRing as local persistent NativeArrayT fields, manually allocated and registered with NativeMemorySentinel. editor smoke test also asserted that old ownership model, making unsafe route self-reinforcing.
Solution: Replace both fields with VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors. AUP discovery grid uses BufferID 71030; active-sonar telemetry ring uses BufferID 71031. TryGetAupDiscoveryGrid, reveal stamping, telemetry writes, and dump code resolve local views from cached IDataVault and release exact descriptors on destroy.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping grid local because it is visor presentation was rejected; sonar reveal memory is read by UI/audio-facing systems and must survive Vault relocation without cached aliases. Resolving grid once per stamped cell was rejected because octant shell fake stamps nine cells and only needs one phase-local resolve.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same cheap octant-shell discovery fake and 300-frame blackbox cadence. Middle/high/ultra can retain richer sonar shader presentation because CPU path still avoids full flood-fill or physics ray loops.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes two local persistent NativeArray allocation/disposal routes. Sonar reveal pays one generation validation per pulse shell, then writes up to nine grid cells through local descriptor.
Decision 063 - Topographical sonar stops persisting pointer-bearing Vault handles
Problem: TopographicalSonarSynthesizer.cs persisted eleven legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for point cloud rows, hit masks, counters, mock SDF/material payloads, 300-frame telemetry, CSV scratch, indirect args, and shader globals. Even without explicit private NativeArrayT fields, legacy descriptors carried pointer metadata and used handle.Resolve, so Vault relocation could leave stale lease path in UI sonar system.
Solution: Replace all eleven descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, cache IDataVault once through ResolveDataVaultCold, resolve method-local views with IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, and release each exact descriptor during teardown after outstanding scan/fade job fences complete. shutdown path now decrements Vault references instead of only defaulting local handles.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handles because system is visual-only was rejected; visual sonar still schedules Burst jobs and uploads GPU buffers from Vault data. Calling GlobalRegistry.DataVault at every resolve site was rejected because registry is cold identity and dependency injection only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous ray-count collapse, mock SDF fake, and GPU point rendering. Middle/high/ultra keep denser point clouds, material LUT color, indirect draw args, and shader globals without changing ownership or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays O(1) generation checks at scan/fade/upload/telemetry phase boundaries. Per-ray SampleTopographicalSonarJob and per-point fade loops use local NativeArrayT descriptors and do not revalidate handles inside hot loop.
Decision 064 - PDA frequency tuning resolves Vault waves through generation descriptors
Problem: PDADecryptionSpectrogramPanel.cs persisted six legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and one shared helper used handle.Resolve(vault) for wave rows, GPU segments, stage targets, and 300-frame telemetry ring. It also cleared descriptors on teardown instead of releasing Vault references.
Solution: Convert six descriptors to VaultGenerationHandleT, make shared helper validate existing handles through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, reacquire descriptors through GetGenerationHandleT when absent or undersized, and release exact descriptors on teardown/DataVault replacement after completing scheduled wave job.
Rejected Alternatives: Releasing inside resolve helper after transient resolve failure was rejected because compaction fence or temporary Vault unavailability must not decrement ownership from hot resolve path. Keeping old helper was rejected because handle.Resolve can use stale pointer metadata.
Scalability potential: Low devices continue to collapse spectrogram point count through continuous GlobalQualityWeight and VRAM clamp. Middle/high/ultra keep denser wave segments, GPU tube rendering, and telemetry without changing minigame truth route.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays bounded generation checks at phase entry. Burst wave generation/error jobs still receive local NativeSliceT views and do not validate per point.
Decision 065 - Babel subtitle runtime stops retaining legacy Vault descriptors
Problem: BabelSubtitleSyncRuntime.cs persisted two static VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and resolved subtitle cue/telemetry buffers through handle.Resolve. static runtime survives scene churn and can keep pointer-bearing metadata alive across Vault relocation or DataVault replacement.
Solution: Replace both descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve cue and telemetry buffers through cached IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, reacquire with GetGenerationHandleT during cold initialization, and release BufferIDs 15070550 and 15070551 on subsystem reset or DataVault hot-swap after fencing any active cue evaluation job.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handle because runtime already used method-local NativeArrayT values was rejected; persistent descriptor itself still carried pointer metadata. Releasing from ordinary read helpers was rejected because transient compaction fence must not mutate ownership from read accessor.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous subtitle dirty budget collapse through ResolveCanvasDirtyBudget. Middle/high/ultra keep same visual-only cue flow and 300-frame telemetry without changing authority, DTO layout, or save identity.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation validations at cue/telemetry phase entry. Burst cue evaluation job still receives local pointer after fresh resolve and performs no per-cue descriptor lookup.
Decision 066 - CharBufferPool Babel arena removes latest-vault and legacy descriptor routes
Problem: CharBufferPool.cs persisted static VaultBufferHandlechar for Babel arena and resolved it through handle.Resolve. It also used GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated() as fallback, which is bootstrap/editor/diagnostic/crash-only route and should not be UI formatting dependency.
Solution: Replace Babel arena handle with VaultGenerationHandlechar, resolve method-local NativeArraychar views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, acquire with GetGenerationHandlechar, release descriptor on subsystem reset, and use only GlobalRegistry.DataVault for cold Vault injection. When no Vault exists, existing managed TMP bridge arrays remain fallback.
Rejected Alternatives: Releasing on every resolve failure was rejected because compaction fences and temporary Vault unavailability must not mutate ownership from read path. Keeping TryGetLatestCreated() was rejected because it hides implicit global heap/diagnostic dependency in UI helper.
Scalability potential: Low devices can skip native arena and use fixed TMP bridge arrays when Vault is unavailable. Middle/high/ultra retain Vault-backed Babel arena without changing text capacity, save identity, or localization authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation when Babel span or native-to-TMP copy uses native arena. fallback path avoids Vault lookup churn and uses preallocated bridge arrays already owned by pool.
Decision 067 - PDA shell borrows glitch glyph table instead of owning it
Problem: PDAShellChrome.cs persisted VaultBufferHandlebyte and used ResolvePointer against DiegeticGlitchSurgeonRuntime.GlitchTableBufferIdRaw. file also allocated shared table through GetBufferHandle and could fall back to GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated(), making PDA chrome component implicit owner of shared glitch glyph fact.
Solution: Replace field with VaultGenerationHandlebyte, borrow existing descriptor with IDataVault.TryGetGenerationHandle, resolve method-local NativeArraybyte views through TryResolveHandle, and derive raw byte pointer only for immediate GlitchEncoder call. On invalid/missing table, fall back to table-free glitch encoder and clear borrowed descriptor.
Rejected Alternatives: GetGenerationHandlebyte was rejected because it can create shared glyph table from non-owner and then force release ambiguity. Releasing on disable was rejected because PDA shell is now borrower, not owner. Keeping TryGetLatestCreated() was rejected because it is crash/diagnostic bootstrap-only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep table-free glitch encoder path when shared table is absent. Middle/high/ultra use richer glyph substitution table when owner has published it, without changing text layout, save identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation only when stress-reactive strings need table. no-table fallback avoids Vault allocation and keeps existing fixed scratch buffer path.
Decision 068 - UberNoir telemetry ring uses generation descriptors only
Problem: HectonUberNoirRuntimeBridge.cs persisted VaultBufferHandleUberNoirShaderTelemetryEntry for shader feature blackbox and called .Resolve(vault) in push/dump paths. bridge did not persist NativeArrayT, but legacy handle itself still carried pointer metadata across Vault relocation.
Solution: Replace field with VaultGenerationHandleUberNoirShaderTelemetryEntry, resolve method-local views with IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, reacquire existing ShaderFeatureTelemetryRing through TryGetGenerationHandle, allocate only when missing and allocation is unlocked, and release owner-local descriptor on disable/destroy/DataVault replacement. Compaction-fence paths clear only local metadata and fail closed.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handle because ring is graphics-only was rejected; blackbox telemetry is persistent Vault fact and must be relocatable. Releasing from transient resolve failure was rejected because maintenance fences must not decrement ownership. Adding private telemetry array fallback was rejected because it would create second proof artifact.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous UberNoir feature collapse through GlobalQualityWeight, stress shedding, and shader feature masks. Middle/high/ultra keep same visual-overkill feature gating while telemetry ring remains generation-safe.

Decision 069 - Docking spline service stops exporting cached Vault pointers
Problem: DockingAutopilotService.cs persisted VaultBufferHandleActiveSplineData, used ResolvePointer, and read activeSplineHandle.ptr directly in service methods. These methods are called by vehicle automation code across frames, so Vault relocation could leave docking slot reads/writes pointed at dead memory.
Solution: Store VaultGenerationHandleActiveSplineData plus cached row count, resolve method-local NativeArrayActiveSplineData views at each service operation boundary, and remove manager helper that returned ActiveSplineData. Existing buffer recovery uses TryGetGenerationHandle; owner-local creation uses GetGenerationHandle only when allocation is unlocked. Disable/shutdown/DataVault replacement release descriptor through owning Vault.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw pointers for slot scans because buffer is small was rejected; pointer lifetime safety is independent of capacity. Adding private active-spline mirror was rejected because docking truth would split into two owners. Reacquiring via GlobalRegistry.DataVault inside each service method was rejected because registry access is cold DI path only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same bounded 64-slot default and cubic Dear Lie docking curve. Middle/high/ultra can raise serialized capacity up to 256 without changing DTO layout, authority route, or slot semantics.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation per acquire/write/read/evaluate/release call. O(n) slot scans still operate on local NativeArrayT descriptor and do not validate handle per slot.

Problem: VehicleDockingModule.cs persisted VaultBufferHandleDockTelemetryEntry and VaultBufferHandleint, resolved both with ResolvePointer, and returned DockTelemetryEntry / int to record and dump helpers. module is pooled and multi-instance, so cached pointer-bearing descriptors can survive DataVault replacement, compaction fences, and dock lifecycle churn.

Decision 093 - Seed Ship shader slot bridge removes VaultGenerationID cache
Problem: SeedShipAnomalyShaderBridge.cs cached VaultBufferHandlefloat4 plus vault.VaultGenerationID for BufferID.ShaderGlobalState. metadata generation cache could say "current" while pointer-bearing descriptor still represented stale address state.
Solution: Store VaultGenerationHandlefloat4, resolve slot views with TryResolveHandle, and use TryGetGenerationHandle/GetGenerationHandle only to acquire descriptor. Direct shader globals remain as fallback when Vault slot lane is unavailable.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping VaultGenerationID for fast cache was rejected because generation descriptor already carries proof and must be validated by resolve. Removing direct shader globals was rejected because anomaly presentation should fail closed visually even when Vault slot allocation is unavailable.
Scalability potential: Low devices can publish cheap scalar globals only. Middle/high/ultra keep richer shared shader slot route without changing slot index, DTO layout, or quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation per publish path. bridge writes one float4 slot and does not validate per shader parameter.

Problem: SubmarineStructuralGrid.cs persisted VaultBufferHandlefloat4 for active breaches and VaultBufferHandleDamageControlTelemetryEntry for damage-control blackbox telemetry. Solution: Store generation descriptors, resolve method-local views through TryResolveHandle, and borrow existing descriptors during allocation-locked phases. Allocation remains limited to unlocked Vault phases.
Rejected Alternatives: Migrating entire structural grid private native state was rejected for this bounded pass because it includes many owner-local job arrays and requires separate Vault route card. Keeping two handle fields because data is visual/blackbox was rejected because blackbox proof artifacts and long-lived breach visuals must be relocatable.
Scalability potential: Low devices can fail closed on breach VFX/telemetry during Vault maintenance. Middle/high/ultra retain richer breach plume/repair visuals and blackbox evidence through same BufferIDs without changing DTO layout or quality authority.

Decision 095 - Terrain seam baseline and blackbox lanes stop caching native aliases
Problem: WorldGenerativeGeologyTerrainSeamApplier.cs persisted VaultBufferHandlefloat per terrain baseline, NativeArrayfloat baseline alias in TerrainApplyState, and VaultBufferHandleTerrainSeamTelemetryEntry for seam blackbox. Terrain apply state can survive multiple reconcile/preview passes, so both handle and stored native view could point at relocated Vault memory.

Reworking MapMagic, hybrid projection, voxel blend mask upload, or terrain writeback was rejected because defect is descriptor lifetime, not terrain math. Releasing baseline buffers from TerrainApplyState.ReleaseBaseline() was rejected for this bounded pass because existing state did not own reference-count teardown and terrain baseline BufferIDs are per-terrain compatibility lanes.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing low-tier visual-only seam projection path and can fail closed on missing Vault lanes during compaction. Middle/high/ultra keep richer mask detail, blackbox evidence, and shader blend-mask upload through same BufferIDs without changing terrain payload layout or quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation descriptor validation when baseline or blackbox view is opened. Heightmap sample loops, hybrid Burst jobs, and blackbox dump loops operate on local resolved view and do not validate per sample or per entry.
Decision 096 - Submarine fluid wrapper stops carrying raw Vault pointers
Problem: SubmarineFluidDynamics.cs used generic VaultNativeBufferT wrapper holding VaultBufferHandleT, dereferenced handle.ptr in its indexer, refreshed through TryGetBufferHandle, and polled TryGetBufferGeneration. That one wrapper backed all compartment, bulkhead, hydro, blackbox, and exterior thermal lanes, so single stale pointer could contaminate whole submarine fluid route.
Solution: Replace wrapper storage with VaultGenerationHandleT plus cached length scalar. Ensure acquires/grows via GetGenerationHandleT only while Vault is unlocked and borrows via TryGetGenerationHandleT under allocation lock. Refresh, indexer access, and implicit NativeArrayT conversion open method-local views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle.

Keeping cached NativeArrayT view inside wrapper was rejected because NativeArrayT carries native address and can go stale after relocation. Releasing all fluid buffers on disable was rejected for this pass because existing route only clears wrapper state after dependency fences and ownership/refcount policy for shared vehicle lanes needs separate teardown audit.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing fluid math LODs, visual wake/hydro Dear Lie paths, and can fail closed on Vault allocation lock. Middle/high/ultra retain richer hydro blackbox, mass-property, thermal anomaly, and custom-drag behavior through same BufferIDs without changing quality authority or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation when wrapper opens view. Scheduled Burst jobs still receive local NativeArrayT values and do not validate descriptors inside their loops. stale raw pointer path is removed for all submarine fluid lanes.

Problem: ShinobuFloraFaunaSymbiosisSolver.cs persisted VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for all major symbiosis lanes, resolved them with .Resolve(vault), and exposed unused GetFloraRef bridge through GetElementAsRef. These buffers feed long-lived AI ecosystem jobs and can cross Vault relocation, so pointer-bearing descriptors are unacceptable.

Add local helpers for claim, borrow, and resolve so cold setup uses GetGenerationHandleT only when unlocked, allocation-locked phases borrow existing descriptors, and runtime reads/writes derive method-local NativeArrayT views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle.

Keeping byref GetFloraRef bridge was rejected because ref must originate from current phase-local view. Editing simulation jobs was rejected because their inputs already accept NativeArrayT and defect was stale descriptor lifetime, not math.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing capped neighbor samples, mock fish fallback, and reduced ecosystem cadence. Middle/high/ultra retain richer scanner VFX, oxygen emitter, adherence, seed, and acoustic tap lanes through same BufferIDs without changing DTO layout or quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation validation at view-open boundaries. Flora/fish/link Burst loops still receive local arrays and do not validate per entity or per link.
Decision 098 - Thermodynamics file worker is blocked until Core exposes relocation-pinned lease
Problem: ThermodynamicsHazardGridRuntime.FileWorker.cs keeps binaryConstantsWorkerPtr and csvWorkerPtr from Vault byte lanes for background worker thread. worker can outlive Vault relocation, and current evidence does not show defrag honoring active writer metadata strongly enough to make direct worker writes safe.
Solution: Do not apply cosmetic local TryResolveHandle patch. safe migration is to parse binary constants and CSV overrides into worker-local staged scalar payloads, publish staged readiness with Volatile.Write, and apply to constants on owner/main phase after resolving VaultGenerationHandleThermodynamicsHazardConstants.
Rejected Alternatives: Letting worker resolve NativeArraybyte locally was rejected because resolution returns phase-local view, not relocation-pinned lease. Holding normal write lock was rejected because inspected relocation path does not prove it fences external worker writers. Leaving issue undocumented was rejected because this is real UAF class.
Scalability potential: Low devices benefit from avoiding worker/Vault contention and can keep cheap staged constants. Middle/high/ultra keep richer thermal hazard tuning once applied from owner phase; gameplay truth and DTO layout stay unchanged.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids unsafe background writes into relocatable Vault memory. future safe patch shifts file IO parsing to worker-local memory and one owner-phase descriptor validation before writing constants.
Decision 099 - Toxic outgassing chemistry removes pointer descriptors and public constants pointer escape
Problem: ToxicOutgassingChemistryRuntime.cs persisted VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for every density, chemistry, signal, telemetry, CSV, binary, and header lane, resolved them with .Resolve(vault), exposed constants through ConstantsRef, and exposed raw pointer through TryGetConstantsPointer. These lanes are long-lived, scheduled, and blackbox-visible; stale aliases here can corrupt gas density, chemical exposure signals, and 300-frame dump.
Solution: Store VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors only. Open method-local NativeArrayT views with IDataVault.TryResolveHandle before owner mutation, job setup, telemetry commit, shader publish, CSV parse, and binary probe. Replace constants ref/pointer facade with value read/write calls and update editor tuner to edit local copy before writing it back.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping editor-only pointer was rejected because editor windows can outlive Vault relocation and still model unsafe API usage. Replacing every call with per-cell generation check was rejected because descriptor validation belongs at phase boundaries, not inside Burst loops. Moving toxicity buffers into private native arrays was rejected because atmosphere chemistry state and blackbox data are Vault-owned proof/state lanes.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain low-resolution radial fallback, continuous quality-weight cadence, and cheap nearest-density sampling. Middle devices keep full scheduled diffusion with lower source budgets. High/ultra retain trilinear sampling, richer mock flow/world sampling, shader scalar publishing, and blackbox detail through identical BufferIDs and DTO layouts.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation at each view-open boundary. 32^3 diffusion, flow, exposure, biolum, and telemetry Burst jobs still run over local NativeArrayT views with NoAlias fields and no per-cell descriptor validation. Removing public pointer escape eliminates one relocation UAF class without adding managed allocations.
Decision 100 - Ambient biota service removes cached Vault handles and read-only aliases
Problem: AmbientBiotaDirector.cs persisted six VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and three NativeArrayT.ReadOnly aliases created through IDataVault.CreateAlias. Reworking IAmbientBiotaService contract was rejected because it is cross-domain contract; same return types can be backed by current generation-resolved views. Replacing indirect draw or macro hydration logic was rejected because defect is descriptor lifetime, not presentation math.

Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation when opening biota/counter/telemetry views. Drift, spawn, hydration, dehydration, and residency loops still iterate local arrays without per-row descriptor validation. Removing CreateAlias fields eliminates three persistent native-address aliases.

Problem: CartographyGridJobs.cs defined CartographyVaultHandles with VaultBufferHandleT fields, allocated them through GetBufferHandle, borrowed through TryGetBufferHandle, and opened all cartography views through .Resolve(vault). Problem: ShinobuEcosystemBalancer.cs persisted VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for ambient entity/AUP rows, boid states, frame snapshots, sector/tuning/counter/telemetry/debug lanes, render matrices/custom data/indirect args, spatial hash buffers, CSV scratch, legacy scratch, and species profiles. Problem: EcosystemPopulationBalancer.cs persisted eight VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and resolved them through .Resolve(vault). High/ultra keep richer route planning, acoustic signatures, telemetry, and visual proxy payloads through same DTO layouts and BufferIDs.

Decision 115 - Submarine dyno tuner removes latest-vault and legacy handle reads
Problem: SubmarineDynoTunerWindow.cs used GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated, TryGetBufferHandle, GetElementAsReadOnlyRef, and .Resolve(vault) to read and mutate submarine kinematic/config/force buffers from editor window.
Solution: Route editor snapshots through cold GlobalRegistry.DataVault, borrowed VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors, and IDataVault.TryReadHandle. Route config writes through existing generation descriptor plus short SystemID.CoreDiagnostics writer fence with guaranteed release.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping TryGetLatestCreated was rejected because it is documented as bootstrap/editor diagnostic only and still bypasses registry-owned dependency route. Keeping direct .Resolve(vault) mutation was rejected because write had no explicit writer fence. Releasing or allocating submarine buffers from editor was rejected because VehiclesPhysics owns those lanes.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same submarine dynamics truth and editor-only refresh cadence. Middle/high/ultra retain full dyno tuning and SceneView vector visualization without changing DTO layouts, BufferIDs, job cadence, rollback identity, or quality-weight semantics.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is zero because window is editor-only. Editor refresh pays three descriptor reads; slider edits pay one descriptor open plus one writer-fence transition, with no descriptor validation inside handle drawing.
Decision 116 - Verlet tow editor tuner stops using latest-vault pointer handles
Problem: VerletTowTunerWindow.cs used GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated, GetBufferHandle, TryGetBufferHandle, and .Resolve(vault) for tuning, material CSV reload, and SceneView tension visualization.
Solution: Use editor-only GlobalRegistry.DataVault, generation descriptors, and method-local NativeArrayT views. Tuning/material rows open through TryResolveHandle and only allocate with GetGenerationHandleT when allocations are not locked; visual positions/tensions read through TryReadHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handles for editor-only code was rejected because mandate is pointer-retention removal, and editor windows are long-lived enough to survive relocation. Releasing tether visual lanes from editor was rejected because physics owns them. Adding runtime job or new telemetry buffer was rejected because existing gizmo is visual diagnostic facade.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep cheap editor gizmo drawing and existing cable math-LOD values. Middle/high/ultra retain CSV material tuning and full 8-slot, 10-segment tension visualization without changing cable DTO layouts, BufferIDs, or physics authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is zero because window is editor-only. SceneView pays two descriptor reads per pass, then draws up to 80 line segments without descriptor validation inside segment loop.
Decision 117 - Somatic tuner removes direct TryGetBuffer editor routes
Problem: SomaticTunerWindow.cs used direct IDataVault.TryGetBuffer views for kinematic tuning, blackbox cursor/ring, VR comfort profile, comfort state, comfort telemetry, CSV scratch, and profile lookup lanes.
Solution: Replace editor reads with borrowed generation descriptors and TryReadHandle. Replace editor writes with TryAcquireWriteLock using SystemID.CoreDiagnostics, releasing tuning/profile/CSV scratch/lookup writer fences in finally.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping direct TryGetBuffer for editor convenience was rejected because editor UI is long-lived and mandate is to eliminate raw buffer access outside phase-local descriptor validation. Adding new somatic runtime telemetry or jobs was rejected because existing blackbox/comfort telemetry lanes already prove facade without changing gameplay ownership.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep cheap editor graph/vector drawing and existing somatic comfort scalability. Middle/high/ultra retain full 300-sample comfort graph and CSV authoring without changing DTO layouts, BufferIDs, job cadence, or gameplay authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is zero because file is editor-only. Editor UI pays one descriptor read per lane and one writer-fence transition per changed tuning/profile batch; graph construction remains fixed 300-point editor scratch path.
Decision 118 - Volumetric silt editor tuner uses descriptor writes and read-only gizmo views
Problem: VolumetricSiltTunerWindow.cs used GetBufferT for VFX tuning mutation and TryGetBufferT for dynamic wake gizmo reads. first migration draft also assumed strict 16-byte VaultGenerationHandleT carried length/creation fields, which would violate handle ABI.
Solution: Read tuning and wakes through borrowed generation descriptors with TryReadHandle. Seed and write tuning through TryAcquireWriteLock under SystemID.CoreDiagnostics, releasing in finally. Validate required capacity only after resolving local NativeArrayT view; keep VaultGenerationHandleT at 16-byte BufferID/SystemID/Generation/Flags contract.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping direct GetBufferT was rejected because editor UI can outlive relocation. Expanding VaultGenerationHandleT with length was rejected because Task 04 requires rigid 16-byte ARM64-friendly descriptor. Adding runtime wake telemetry was rejected because existing editor gizmo is visual facade over VFX-owned lanes.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same cheap capped 16-wake wire-disc visualization and VFX tuning facade. Middle/high/ultra retain full marine snow tuning, CSV-owned renderer behavior, and wake visualization without changing DTO layouts, BufferIDs, shader payloads, or VFX authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is zero because file is editor-only. Editor repaint pays one descriptor read for tuning; edits pay one writer-fence transition; SceneView pays one descriptor read before capped gizmo loop.
Decision 119 - Ecology symbiosis editor tuner removes byref legacy handles
Problem: EcologySymbiosisTunerWindow.cs used TryGetBufferHandle, GetElementAsReadOnlyRef, GetElementAsRef, and .Resolve(vault) for tuning, counters, and six SceneView gizmo buffers.
Solution: Replace tuning/counter/gizmo reads with borrowed generation descriptors and TryReadHandle. Replace tuning writes with TryAcquireWriteLock under SystemID.CoreDiagnostics, writing row 0 and releasing in finally.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping byref tuning mutation was rejected because it bypasses explicit writer authority. Releasing ecology-owned lanes from editor was rejected because SystemID.AIEcology owns symbiosis buffers. Adding new gizmo caches was rejected because cached native views are pointer-retention class being removed.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same capped 128-line SceneView visualization and existing ecology runtime quality behavior. Middle/high/ultra retain full symbiosis tuning and AUP line visualization without changing DTO layouts, BufferIDs, job cadence, or ecology authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is zero because file is editor-only. Editor refresh pays two descriptor reads; SceneView pays six descriptor reads before bounded AUP search/draw loops.
Decision 120 - Economy recipe editor live DTO panel uses descriptor views
Problem: EconomyRecipeTunerWindow.cs used direct TryGetBufferT live views for recipe DTOs, recipe masks, and ingredient rows, then wrote recipe/mask/ingredient edits through those views.
Solution: Replace live panel reads with borrowed generation descriptors and TryReadHandle. Replace recipe/mask/ingredient edits with TryAcquireWriteLock under SystemID.CoreDiagnostics, writing only affected rows and releasing every writer fence in finally.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting cold H8CR/CSV importer helpers was rejected in this pass because live editor panel had direct Vault read/write debt and import helper ownership belongs to SHINOBU19 ledger code. Holding writer locks for whole repaint was rejected because no-change UI pass should remain read-only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep read-only live DTO inspection and bounded edit writes. Middle/high/ultra retain full recipe/mask/ingredient authoring without changing DTO layouts, BufferIDs, H8CR identity, or economy authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is zero because file is editor-only. Live panel repaint pays descriptor reads only; edits pay short row-scoped writer-fence transitions.
Decision 121 - Abyssal swarm editor facade removes raw Vault reads
Problem: AbyssalSwarmTunerWindow.cs used VaultBufferHandleShinobuEcosystemTuning with GetElementAsRef for tuning mutation and direct TryGetBufferT views for bridge status, counters, telemetry, spatial hash cells, ambient entities, and ambient AUPs. window is editor-only but long-lived enough to survive Vault relocation and kept obsolete pointer-style access active in SHINOBU-facing tooling.
Solution: Replace every read with borrowed VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors plus IDataVault.TryReadHandle. Replace tuning edits with short SystemID.CoreDiagnostics writer fence on ShinobuEcosystemTuning, writing row 0 and releasing in finally.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping direct TryGetBufferT for editor convenience was rejected because mandate is consumer-wide pointer route removal, not runtime-only cleanup. Caching descriptor/view pairs in window was rejected because SceneView/UI repaint cadence does not justify persistent native aliases. Releasing ecosystem lanes from editor was rejected because balancer/runtime owner owns those buffers.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep cheap editor counters, 300-sample telemetry graph, capped hash-grid cells, and capped vector visualization. Middle/high/ultra retain full tuning, species profile visibility, spatial hash debugging, and boid vector diagnostics without changing DTO layouts, BufferIDs, GlobalQualityWeight behavior, or AIEcology authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is zero because file is editor-only. Editor UI/SceneView pays descriptor reads per pass; species scan, graph bars, hash cells, and vector loops remain descriptor-free after local view opens.
Decision 122 - SHINOBU 143 cable tuner removes latest-vault pointer route
Problem: Shinobu143CablePhysicsTunerWindow.cs used GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated, GetBufferHandleT, and .Resolve(vault) to open tuning and material lanes. window duplicated cable editor debt already removed from SHINOBU 132 tuner and kept legacy pointer route for VerletCableTuning, VerletCableMaterials, and Shinobu143CableMaterials.
Solution: Use cold GlobalRegistry.DataVault, acquire/grow lanes through VaultGenerationHandleT only when allocation is not locked, and mutate them under SystemID.CoreDiagnostics writer fences with guaranteed release. Keep telemetry and dump reads delegated to existing TetherAupRuntimeIntrospection bridges instead of adding new editor state.
Rejected Alternatives: Reusing TryGetLatestCreated was rejected because registry is cold DI route for editor facades. Returning write-locked NativeArrayT from helper without handle was rejected because release ownership would be implicit. Adding new cable telemetry buffers was rejected because telemetry already exists and defect was stale descriptor access.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep cheap editor-only tuning and 0.25s telemetry refresh. Middle/high/ultra retain CSV material authoring, tuning precision, and cable surgeon dumps without changing DTO layouts, BufferIDs, cable solver cadence, or physics authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is zero because file is editor-only. CSV reload pays two writer-fence transitions before parsing and performs no descriptor validation inside material parse loop.
Decision 123 - Abyssal atmosphere tuner separates read and write Vault intent
Problem: AbyssalAtmosphereTunerWindow.cs used mutable TryResolveHandle for fog param refresh/slider edits, direct GetBufferT for extinction profile and CSV scratch writes, and mutable telemetry resolve for read-only graph. file had generation descriptors in places but not explicit write/read authority.
Solution: Route fog param refresh/default seeding and slider writes through TryAcquireWriteLock under SystemID.CoreDiagnostics. Route CSV scratch and extinction profile lanes through same writer-fence helper. Route telemetry graph through borrowed descriptors and TryReadHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping TryResolveHandle for editor convenience was rejected because code mutates defaults during refresh and mutates slider values during callbacks. Holding profile writer lock during file IO was rejected; scratch is written first, then profile lock is taken for parse/upsert. Adding new VFX telemetry buffer was rejected because graph already consumes runtime telemetry ring.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep cheap editor graph and continuous fog quality controls. Middle/high/ultra retain extinction CSV authoring, visual-overkill quality sliders, ray-step tuning, and telemetry visualization without changing DTO layouts, shader payloads, BufferIDs, or VFX authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is zero because file is editor-only. CSV load validates scratch/profile descriptors once and parses without descriptor checks; graph repaint validates telemetry once before sample loop.

Problem: AUPPrematureCastScanner.cs still read AupPrecisionVault.TelemetryRingBuffer through direct TryGetBufferT for histogram.

Reworking scanner jobs or TempJob fallback was rejected because direct Vault read was only defect in this pass.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same optional telemetry histogram and TempJob fallback. Middle/high/ultra retain full AUP precision histogram without changing DTO layout, scan output, or math authority.

Problem: ConstructionSocketEditorTools.cs read construction counters, telemetry, socket states, and socket AUPs through direct TryGetBufferT in editor summary and gizmo paths.
Solution: Add shared editor-only read helper that borrows VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors and opens read views through IDataVault.TryReadHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving editor gizmos on TryGetBufferT was rejected because SceneView tools are long-lived diagnostics and can survive Vault relocation. Adding writer locks was rejected because paths are read-only summary/gizmo consumers.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep cheap socket counts and bounded gizmo drawing. Middle/high/ultra retain construction socket visualization without changing DTO layout, tuning ownership, candidate budgets, or construction authority.
