Problem: VocalWarningSystem.cs persisted six Vault-backed NativeArrayT aliases and six legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for queue, warning state, and telemetry lanes. Vault relocation after boot could leave manager indexing stale array metadata.
Solution: Replace all six descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, add phase-local VwsVaultViews value, resolve views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle inside queue mutation, slow tick, telemetry, and dump paths, and release exact descriptors during teardown/rebind.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping aliases because VWS has no Burst job was rejected; UAF risk is independent of job scheduling. ReleaseOwnerBuffers was rejected because exact BufferIDs are known and owner-wide teardown hides descriptor ownership mistakes.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same small priority queue and cooldown cadence; middle/high/ultra keep full warning telemetry and radio-degrade presentation. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays six generation compares on VWS mutation/slow paths. This is below clip submission and subtitle routing cost and removes stale Vault metadata from audio warning manager.
Decision 050 - Native audio frame ring resolves buffers per operation
Problem: NativeAudioFrameRingBuffer.cs persisted Vault-backed frames and sharedState aliases plus two VaultBufferHandleT descriptors. native output ring also exports raw pointers to audio bridge, so cached manager aliases were direct relocation hazard.
Solution: Replace both handles with VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve local RingVaultViews value for buffer state, writes, clearing, shared metadata access, and native descriptor creation, and release exact frame/shared-state descriptors on dispose.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping frames/sharedState because ring is internal was rejected; internal managers still survive across defrag. Owner-wide release was rejected because ring owns exactly two known BufferIDs.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain same bounded SPSC copy and overflow drop reporting; middle/high/ultra keep larger ring capacities and native bridge output without retaining stale managed-side Vault aliases.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation compares for ring state/write/descriptor operations. hot cost remains sample copy and native plugin handoff; stale manager-resident Vault aliases are removed.
Decision 051 - Dynamic music resolves DSP buffers from generation views
Problem: DynamicMusicGranularSynthesizer.cs persisted Vault-backed arrays for DSP voices, scalars, tuning, output buffers, biquad, telemetry, CSV scratch, preset rules, grain bank, shared state, and scalability state. It also cached output pointers. bounded Vault relocation would invalidate those aliases while manager, editor facade, audio callback, or scheduled jobs still believed metadata was stable.
Solution: Replace all owned descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, add method-local DynamicMusicVaultViews resolver, pass local views into editor/cold CSV/audio/job/telemetry paths, take raw pointers only immediately before job scheduling or file/native copy, and release exact owned descriptors on teardown. external scalability state is borrowed through TryGetGenerationHandle and resolved transiently.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached aliases because this is audio system was rejected; audio paths are relocation-sensitive and must not retain stale manager-side Vault metadata. Releasing by owner was rejected because synth owns fixed BufferID set and exact release exposes descriptor drift.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous density/cutoff/sample cadence collapse through GlobalQualityWeight; middle/high/ultra keep full granular voices, telemetry, and stinger richness. No binary hardware branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation checks at scheduling/cold/editor/audio-copy boundaries. hot DSP loop still runs from phase-local pointers inside Burst jobs; stale persistent aliases are removed without adding GC.
Decision 052 - Adaptive stem mixer stops retaining Vault aliases
Problem: AdaptiveStemAudioMixer.cs persisted eleven Vault-backed arrays and eleven legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for stem state, commands, rules, mock signal rows, telemetry, CSV scratch, and scalability state. mixer also used binary low/high scalability fallback after signal ingress.
Solution: Replace owned descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, add method-local AdaptiveStemVaultViews resolver, resolve views before editor/tick/job/telemetry/CSV operations, borrow scalability state through TryGetGenerationHandle, release owned descriptors exactly, and map HectonQualityTier through Smooth01 into continuous 0.1..1.0 fallback weight.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping aliases because mixer is presentation-only was rejected; presentation systems still schedule Burst jobs and can crash after relocation. Binary LowMx350 ? 0.1f : 1f was rejected because it creates hard quality discontinuity.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep slow update cadence and cheap crossfade; middle/high/ultra smoothly restore faster cadence and richer stem blending without branch pop.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation checks on mixer phase boundaries, not per sample. gain is removing stale Vault aliases from adaptive-stem job scheduling and telemetry paths.
Decision 053 - Player critical renderer first removes pointer-bearing ownership
Problem: PlayerCriticalProceduralAudioRenderer.cs is last large audio file with broad Vault debt. It held 50 persistent NativeArrayT aliases and acquired them through pointer-bearing VaultBufferHandleT plus handle.Resolve; teardown used owner-wide release.
Solution: First isolate ownership from pointer metadata: add 50 VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors, make central ResolveVaultBuffer helper use GetGenerationHandle plus TryResolveHandle, and replace owner-wide release with exact release of known descriptors after outstanding audio/SDF/composite jobs are completed.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting entire 11k-line renderer in one pass was rejected because producer thread, sonar jobs, VWS double buffer, and reverb state share lifetime constraints. Keeping VaultBufferHandleT until final pass was rejected because it leaves highest-risk pointer-bearing API in largest audio owner.
Scalability potential: Runtime audio quality behavior is unchanged in this slice. Low/middle/high/ultra renderer math and existing perceptual audio fakes remain stable while ownership metadata becomes generation-checked.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays no new sample-loop cost. Bind/release paths pay O(buffer-count) generation descriptor work; remaining work is phase-local view migration for persistent aliases.
Decision 054 - Player critical low-risk rings move to phase-local views
Problem: After descriptor ownership was fixed, PlayerCritical still kept 50 persistent Vault aliases. smallest safe runtime slice was isolated VWS double-buffer lane plus granular/prologue telemetry and prologue command rings; these are bounded and do not require rewriting full producer DSP graph.
Solution: Remove five persistent NativeArrayT fields and resolve VWS clip buffers, granular telemetry, prologue transition telemetry, and prologue transition command rings through generation handles at operation boundaries. Keep producer sample loops free of per-sample resolve calls.
Rejected Alternatives: Attempting to migrate all frame scratch/reverb/sonar/granular voice arrays in one patch was rejected because those arrays cross audio producer loop and scheduled sonar jobs. Deferring all aliases was rejected because isolated rings were easy to harden immediately.
Scalability potential: No visual/audio quality behavior changed. Low-tier and high-tier renderer fakes keep their existing cadence; postmortem and VWS lanes now survive relocation more predictably.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays O(1) generation checks on VWS submit/playback, prologue queue, and telemetry operations. No inner DSP loop resolve was introduced.
Decision 055 - Player critical granular SOA resolves once per producer block
Problem: PlayerCritical still retained metallic grain bank and eight granular voice SOA buffers as long-lived NativeArrayT fields. Those arrays are mutated in audio-rate code, so resolving them per sample would be correct but too expensive; keeping them as fields preserved stale-alias UAF risk.
Solution: Remove nine persistent aliases, add GranularVoiceVaultViews, resolve view once in CanProduceAudioBlock, pass it through RenderHullStressBlock, RenderStructuralGranularVoices, and MixAndFilterBlock, and update voice arm/trim/slot helpers to mutate local NativeArray descriptors copied from phase view.
Rejected Alternatives: whole-renderer DSP view was deferred because sonar/reverb/frame scratch buffers cross scheduled jobs and require separate dependency pass. Per-voice/per-sample resolution was rejected because it burns audio-thread cycles without improving safety over block-scoped view.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain cheap granular voice budgets and linear envelopes; middle/high/ultra still unlock denser voice counts and interpolation through existing continuous tuning. migration does not add hardware binary branch.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays nine generation validations once per produced block. hot sample loop reuses local NativeArray descriptors and keeps existing O(active voices) granular fake instead of heavier structural simulation.
Decision 056 - Player critical binaural and low-pass state resolves once per producer block
Problem: Binaural ITD delay, ear-shadow history, and final listener low-pass histories remained as long-lived NativeArrayT fields. They are small, but they are mutated every producer block and are still invalid after Vault relocation.
Solution: Remove six aliases, add BinauralFilterVaultViews, resolve it once in CanProduceAudioBlock, pass it by ref through MixAndFilterBlock and ApplyBinauralSpatializationBlock, and resolve same view in ClearLowPassState for cold reset.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping histories as fields because they are tiny was rejected; UAF risk is independent of byte count. Resolving inside SampleBinauralDelay or ApplyBinauralShadowEar was rejected because those functions execute per sample/ear and would add avoidable validation branches.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous binaural mix, underwater shadow cutoff, narcosis chorus, and abyssal low-pass curves stay unchanged from low through ultra. change is pointer-lifetime only.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays six generation validations per produced block. per-sample binaural and low-pass loops use local descriptors and keep their existing arithmetic profile.
Decision 057 - Player critical reverb state resolves once per producer block
Problem: Sabine reverb, cave convolution, and interior FDN delay buffers remained as persistent NativeArrayT fields. These are among larger PlayerCritical buffers and are mutated in hot sample loops, so stale aliases can crash and per-sample resolution would be too expensive.
Solution: Remove four aliases, add ReverbVaultViews, resolve view once in CanProduceAudioBlock, pass local descriptors through Sabine comb, cave convolution, and interior FDN helpers, and resolve same generation view for cold impulse bake and reset clears.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping reverb fields because they are audio-private was rejected; Vault relocation can invalidate audio-private views exactly like cross-domain views. Resolving inside each comb/convolution tap was rejected because it would multiply handle validation by sample count and tap count.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous reverb DSP tier selection, wet mix, openness, and acoustic density curves remain unchanged. Low devices still fall back to cheaper Unity/profile-only paths; high/ultra keep native Sabine/convolution richness.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays four generation validations per produced block. Hot reverb loops keep local NativeArray descriptors and avoid new branches inside comb, convolution, and FDN tap math.
Decision 058 - Player critical transient delay lines resolve once per producer block
Problem: Impact clang and thruster comb delay lines remained as persistent NativeArrayT fields. Both are small compared with reverb, but they are audio-rate mutable delay lines and can become stale after Vault relocation.
Solution: Remove two aliases, add TransientDelayVaultViews, resolve it once in CanProduceAudioBlock, pass it through impact event consumption, hull stress rendering, and thruster rendering, and clear it through method-local view during reset.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping these fields until frame-scratch pass was rejected because they are isolated and cheap to harden now. Resolving in RenderImpactClangSampleInternal or each thruster comb iteration was rejected because it would add per-sample validation.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous thruster pressure/cavitation and impact metallic fakes stay unchanged across low/mid/high/ultra. migration changes lifetime only.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation validations per produced block. Hot Karplus/comb loops use local NativeArray descriptors.
Decision 059 - Player critical frame scratch resolves once per producer block
Problem: Hull, sonar, impact echo, thruster, heartbeat, bubble, mix, and stereo scratch buffers were still manager-held NativeArrayT aliases. These buffers are re-used every audio block, so stale aliases would survive Vault relocation and crash in producer path.
Solution: Remove nine scratch aliases, add FrameScratchVaultViews, resolve view once in CanProduceAudioBlock, and pass it by ref into render, mix, and binaural stages. Cold reset and prologue probe paths resolve same view only for duration of their clear/probe operation.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping scratch fields because they are short-lived data was rejected; alias lifetime was manager lifetime, not scratch semantic lifetime. Resolving inside each render function was rejected where producer already has block view.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous quality curves for granular FM, reverb tier, binaural blend, and bubble intensity remain unchanged. Low devices pay one block-level validation set and keep same cheap DSP fakes; high/ultra keep dense procedural output.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays nine generation validations per produced block. Hot sample loops use local descriptors and retain prior arithmetic profile.
Decision 060 - Player critical sonar storage is split into phase-local Vault views
Problem: remaining sonar buffers were highest UAF risk: publish taps, worker taps, DSP echo delay/filter state, SDF hit cache, and composite coalescing scratch were all persistent NativeArrayT fields. Some are touched from read accessors, some from audio producer blocks, and some from scheduled jobs.
Solution: Remove all 15 sonar aliases and split resolution into SonarTapVaultViews, SonarDspVaultViews, and SonarSpatialVaultViews. UI read accessors resolve only tap buffers, audio DSP resolves tap+DSP state once per block, and SDF/composite phases resolve spatial buffers at schedule/publish boundaries. editor smoke test now verifies handle/view usage instead of stale fields.
Rejected Alternatives: single PlayerCriticalAudioVaultViews blob was rejected because TryGetCockpitSonarEchoTaps must stay pure read accessor and must not over-resolve DSP or SDF buffers. Per-tap generation resolution was rejected because it would multiply validation by echo count inside sonar publish loop.
Scalability potential: Sonar keeps existing capped echo tap fake and continuous SDF probe budget. Low devices use fewer probes/ghost taps through existing quality weights; high/ultra can keep richer SDF returns without changing authority or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes all sonar manager-held native aliases. Validation cost is bounded to phase entry: four checks for tap views, six for DSP views, five for spatial views. Delay/filter loops use local descriptors.
Decision 061 - Vocal warning pending queue is collapsed into Vault priority queue
Problem: VocalWarningSystem.cs still owned pendingWarningIds as private NativeQueuebyte allocated with Allocator.Persistent. It was tiny, but it was still manager-owned native allocation outside GlobalDataVault, and it duplicated Vault-backed AudioVocalWarningQueue fact.
Solution: Remove private NativeQueuebyte, pendingNativeCount, prewarm, drain, sentinel registration, and dispose path. TryQueueWarning now resolves VwsVaultViews once, writes cooldown/severity/source state, and inserts warning id directly into Vault-owned bounded priority queue via InsertOrPromote.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing queue with another Vault staging buffer was rejected because bounded priority queue already handles duplicate suppression, capacity, and priority replacement. Keeping staging queue because it is only 16 bytes was rejected because UAF and ownership violations are independent of capacity.
Scalability potential: Low devices skip extra staging dequeue pass on slow tick. Middle/high/ultra keep same warning priority behavior, telemetry ring, and radio-degrade presentation without changing DTO layout or authority route.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes one persistent native allocation and one TryDequeue drain loop per slow tick. TryQueueWarning already paid six generation checks for VWS state; direct insert reuses same resolved view and does not add sample-loop or job-loop cost.
Decision 062 - Spectrum sonar discovery and telemetry views move to Vault descriptors
Problem: SpectrumSystem.cs owned aupDiscoveryGrid and activeSonarGeoTelemetryRing as local persistent NativeArrayT fields, manually allocated and registered with NativeMemorySentinel. editor smoke test also asserted that old ownership model, making unsafe route self-reinforcing.
Solution: Replace both fields with VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors. AUP discovery grid uses BufferID 71030; active-sonar telemetry ring uses BufferID 71031. TryGetAupDiscoveryGrid, reveal stamping, telemetry writes, and dump code resolve local views from cached IDataVault and release exact descriptors on destroy.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping grid local because it is visor presentation was rejected; sonar reveal memory is read by UI/audio-facing systems and must survive Vault relocation without cached aliases. Resolving grid once per stamped cell was rejected because octant shell fake stamps nine cells and only needs one phase-local resolve.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same cheap octant-shell discovery fake and 300-frame blackbox cadence. Middle/high/ultra can retain richer sonar shader presentation because CPU path still avoids full flood-fill or physics ray loops.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes two local persistent NativeArray allocation/disposal routes. Sonar reveal pays one generation validation per pulse shell, then writes up to nine grid cells through local descriptor.
Decision 063 - Topographical sonar stops persisting pointer-bearing Vault handles
Problem: TopographicalSonarSynthesizer.cs persisted eleven legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for point cloud rows, hit masks, counters, mock SDF/material payloads, 300-frame telemetry, CSV scratch, indirect args, and shader globals. Even without explicit private NativeArrayT fields, legacy descriptors carried pointer metadata and used handle.Resolve, so Vault relocation could leave stale lease path in UI sonar system.
Solution: Replace all eleven descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, cache IDataVault once through ResolveDataVaultCold, resolve method-local views with IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, and release each exact descriptor during teardown after outstanding scan/fade job fences complete. shutdown path now decrements Vault references instead of only defaulting local handles.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handles because system is visual-only was rejected; visual sonar still schedules Burst jobs and uploads GPU buffers from Vault data. Calling GlobalRegistry.DataVault at every resolve site was rejected because registry is cold identity and dependency injection only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous ray-count collapse, mock SDF fake, and GPU point rendering. Middle/high/ultra keep denser point clouds, material LUT color, indirect draw args, and shader globals without changing ownership or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays O(1) generation checks at scan/fade/upload/telemetry phase boundaries. Per-ray SampleTopographicalSonarJob and per-point fade loops use local NativeArrayT descriptors and do not revalidate handles inside hot loop.
Decision 064 - PDA frequency tuning resolves Vault waves through generation descriptors
Problem: PDADecryptionSpectrogramPanel.cs persisted six legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and one shared helper used handle.Resolve(vault) for wave rows, GPU segments, stage targets, and 300-frame telemetry ring. It also cleared descriptors on teardown instead of releasing Vault references.
Solution: Convert six descriptors to VaultGenerationHandleT, make shared helper validate existing handles through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, reacquire descriptors through GetGenerationHandleT when absent or undersized, and release exact descriptors on teardown/DataVault replacement after completing scheduled wave job.
Rejected Alternatives: Releasing inside resolve helper after transient resolve failure was rejected because compaction fence or temporary Vault unavailability must not decrement ownership from hot resolve path. Keeping old helper was rejected because handle.Resolve can use stale pointer metadata.
Scalability potential: Low devices continue to collapse spectrogram point count through continuous GlobalQualityWeight and VRAM clamp. Middle/high/ultra keep denser wave segments, GPU tube rendering, and telemetry without changing minigame truth route.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays bounded generation checks at phase entry. Burst wave generation/error jobs still receive local NativeSliceT views and do not validate per point.
Decision 065 - Babel subtitle runtime stops retaining legacy Vault descriptors
Problem: BabelSubtitleSyncRuntime.cs persisted two static VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and resolved subtitle cue/telemetry buffers through handle.Resolve. static runtime survives scene churn and can keep pointer-bearing metadata alive across Vault relocation or DataVault replacement.
Solution: Replace both descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve cue and telemetry buffers through cached IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, reacquire with GetGenerationHandleT during cold initialization, and release BufferIDs 15070550 and 15070551 on subsystem reset or DataVault hot-swap after fencing any active cue evaluation job.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handle because runtime already used method-local NativeArrayT values was rejected; persistent descriptor itself still carried pointer metadata. Releasing from ordinary read helpers was rejected because transient compaction fence must not mutate ownership from read accessor.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous subtitle dirty budget collapse through ResolveCanvasDirtyBudget. Middle/high/ultra keep same visual-only cue flow and 300-frame telemetry without changing authority, DTO layout, or save identity.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation validations at cue/telemetry phase entry. Burst cue evaluation job still receives local pointer after fresh resolve and performs no per-cue descriptor lookup.
Decision 066 - CharBufferPool Babel arena removes latest-vault and legacy descriptor routes
Problem: CharBufferPool.cs persisted static VaultBufferHandlechar for Babel arena and resolved it through handle.Resolve. It also used GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated() as fallback, which is bootstrap/editor/diagnostic/crash-only route and should not be UI formatting dependency.
Solution: Replace Babel arena handle with VaultGenerationHandlechar, resolve method-local NativeArraychar views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, acquire with GetGenerationHandlechar, release descriptor on subsystem reset, and use only GlobalRegistry.DataVault for cold Vault injection. When no Vault exists, existing managed TMP bridge arrays remain fallback.
Rejected Alternatives: Releasing on every resolve failure was rejected because compaction fences and temporary Vault unavailability must not mutate ownership from read path. Keeping TryGetLatestCreated() was rejected because it hides implicit global heap/diagnostic dependency in UI helper.
Scalability potential: Low devices can skip native arena and use fixed TMP bridge arrays when Vault is unavailable. Middle/high/ultra retain Vault-backed Babel arena without changing text capacity, save identity, or localization authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation when Babel span or native-to-TMP copy uses native arena. fallback path avoids Vault lookup churn and uses preallocated bridge arrays already owned by pool.
Decision 067 - PDA shell borrows glitch glyph table instead of owning it
Problem: PDAShellChrome.cs persisted VaultBufferHandlebyte and used ResolvePointer against DiegeticGlitchSurgeonRuntime.GlitchTableBufferIdRaw. file also allocated shared table through GetBufferHandle and could fall back to GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated(), making PDA chrome component implicit owner of shared glitch glyph fact.
Solution: Replace field with VaultGenerationHandlebyte, borrow existing descriptor with IDataVault.TryGetGenerationHandle, resolve method-local NativeArraybyte views through TryResolveHandle, and derive raw byte pointer only for immediate GlitchEncoder call. On invalid/missing table, fall back to table-free glitch encoder and clear borrowed descriptor.
Rejected Alternatives: GetGenerationHandlebyte was rejected because it can create shared glyph table from non-owner and then force release ambiguity. Releasing on disable was rejected because PDA shell is now borrower, not owner. Keeping TryGetLatestCreated() was rejected because it is crash/diagnostic bootstrap-only.

Releasing from transient resolve failure was rejected because maintenance fences must not decrement ownership. Adding private telemetry array fallback was rejected because it would create second proof artifact.

These methods are called by vehicle automation code across frames, so Vault relocation could leave docking slot reads/writes pointed at dead memory.

Existing buffer recovery uses TryGetGenerationHandle; owner-local creation uses GetGenerationHandle only when allocation is unlocked. Disable/shutdown/DataVault replacement release descriptor through owning Vault.

Adding private active-spline mirror was rejected because docking truth would split into two owners. Reacquiring via GlobalRegistry.DataVault inside each service method was rejected because registry access is cold DI path only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same bounded 64-slot default and cubic Dear Lie docking curve. Middle/high/ultra can raise serialized capacity up to 256 without changing DTO layout, authority route, or slot semantics.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation per acquire/write/read/evaluate/release call. O(n) slot scans still operate on local NativeArrayT descriptor and do not validate handle per slot.

Problem: FaunaBrain.cs persisted two VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for one-row corpse-sink kinematic input/output buffers and resolved them through .Resolve(vault). helper also polled GlobalRegistry.DataVault from schedule/complete boundary, which is active runtime work, not cold injection.

Decision 092 - Fluid dynamic wake buffers stop carrying pointer handles
Problem: HectonFluidEngine.cs persisted VaultBufferHandlefloat4 descriptors for WakeGlobalBuffer and WakeVectorBuffer, allocated through GetBufferHandle, and resolved with .Resolve(vault) immediately before GPU upload. Dynamic wake presentation can run across Vault compaction or DataVault replacement, so pointer-bearing descriptors are unsafe even when data is visual.
Solution: Store VaultGenerationHandlefloat4 descriptors, borrow existing wake buffers during allocation-locked phases, allocate with GetGenerationHandle only when unlocked, and resolve method-local NativeArrayfloat4 views with TryResolveHandle before upload.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing dynamic wake route was rejected because shader-side wake fake is cheap visual substitute for CPU fluid simulation. Releasing wake buffers on fluid teardown was not added because prior route only cleared descriptors here and wake ownership is already documented as multi-owner conflict with VFX lanes.
Scalability potential: Low devices can fail closed to existing empty wake buffer and low-tier wake params. Middle/high/ultra keep richer dynamic wake GPU advection from same two 16-slot float4 lanes without changing shader ABI or quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two descriptor validations per dynamic wake upload phase. upload loop still copies local NativeArrayfloat4 views to GPU buffer and does not validate per slot.

Problem: SeedShipAnomalyShaderBridge.cs cached VaultBufferHandlefloat4 plus vault.VaultGenerationID for BufferID.ShaderGlobalState. metadata generation cache could say "current" while pointer-bearing descriptor still represented stale address state.
Solution: Store VaultGenerationHandlefloat4, resolve slot views with TryResolveHandle, and use TryGetGenerationHandle/GetGenerationHandle only to acquire descriptor. Direct shader globals remain as fallback when Vault slot lane is unavailable.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping VaultGenerationID for fast cache was rejected because generation descriptor already carries proof and must be validated by resolve. Removing direct shader globals was rejected because anomaly presentation should fail closed visually even when Vault slot allocation is unavailable.
Scalability potential: Low devices can publish cheap scalar globals only. Middle/high/ultra keep richer shared shader slot route without changing slot index, DTO layout, or quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation per publish path. bridge writes one float4 slot and does not validate per shader parameter.

Keeping two handle fields because data is visual/blackbox was rejected because blackbox proof artifacts and long-lived breach visuals must be relocatable.

Releasing baseline buffers from TerrainApplyState.ReleaseBaseline() was rejected for this bounded pass because existing state did not own reference-count teardown and terrain baseline BufferIDs are per-terrain compatibility lanes.

Problem: SubmarineFluidDynamics.cs used generic VaultNativeBufferT wrapper holding VaultBufferHandleT, dereferenced handle.ptr in its indexer, refreshed through TryGetBufferHandle, and polled TryGetBufferGeneration. That one wrapper backed all compartment, bulkhead, hydro, blackbox, and exterior thermal lanes, so single stale pointer could contaminate whole submarine fluid route.

Middle/high/ultra retain richer hydro blackbox, mass-property, thermal anomaly, and custom-drag behavior through same BufferIDs without changing quality authority or DTO layout.

Decision 098 - Thermodynamics file worker is blocked until Core exposes relocation-pinned lease
Problem: ThermodynamicsHazardGridRuntime.FileWorker.cs keeps binaryConstantsWorkerPtr and csvWorkerPtr from Vault byte lanes for background worker thread. worker can outlive Vault relocation, and current evidence does not show defrag honoring active writer metadata strongly enough to make direct worker writes safe.
Solution: Do not apply cosmetic local TryResolveHandle patch. safe migration is to parse binary constants and CSV overrides into worker-local staged scalar payloads, publish staged readiness with Volatile.Write, and apply to constants on owner/main phase after resolving VaultGenerationHandleThermodynamicsHazardConstants.

Holding normal write lock was rejected because inspected relocation path does not prove it fences external worker writers. Leaving issue undocumented was rejected because this is real UAF class.

Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids unsafe background writes into relocatable Vault memory. future safe patch shifts file IO parsing to worker-local memory and one owner-phase descriptor validation before writing constants.

Problem: ToxicOutgassingChemistryRuntime.cs persisted VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for every density, chemistry, signal, telemetry, CSV, binary, and header lane, resolved them with .Resolve(vault), exposed constants through ConstantsRef, and exposed raw pointer through TryGetConstantsPointer. Problem: AmbientBiotaDirector.cs persisted six VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and three NativeArrayT.ReadOnly aliases created through IDataVault.CreateAlias. Decision 137 - Vehicle damage runtime and contract open local Vault views before pointer use
Problem: VehicleComponentDamageRuntime.cs persisted eleven VaultBufferHandleT descriptors, allocated through GetBufferHandleT, borrowed kinematic config through TryGetBufferHandleT, and used .Resolve, .ResolvePointer, GetElementAsRef, GetElementAsReadOnlyRef, and ResolveBuffer in fixed tick, initialization, CSV reload, editor snapshots, gizmos, root-pose reads, and blackbox dump paths. VehicleComponentDamageContracts.cs also exposed VehicleDamageAccess.GetCellRef(ref VaultBufferHandleVehicleGridCellDTO).
Solution: Replace every persisted vehicle damage handle with VaultGenerationHandleT. Allocate/borrow through generation descriptors. Add local helpers that open NativeArrayT views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, derive raw job pointers from those method-local views, and derive editor/readback refs with UnsafeUtility.ArrayElementAsRef only after descriptor validation. Change VehicleDamageAccess.GetCellRef to accept in VaultGenerationHandleVehicleGridCellDTO and resolve local view before returning ref.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting pointer-based Burst jobs was rejected because job fields already carry deterministic Burst flags and NoAlias; their inputs are safe when derived immediately before scheduling. Keeping legacy byref helpers for editor/contract convenience was rejected because editor windows, gizmos, and contract helpers are long-lived enough to survive Vault relocation. Converting every existing TryLockBuffer call to newer descriptor writer-fence API was deferred because this loop targeted stale handle storage and hidden pointer resolution without expanding lock lifecycle surface.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep continuous mock signal count scaling, bounded gizmo cells, emergency mock damage, and existing damage-grid cadence. Middle/high/ultra retain full grid damage mapping, system scalar outputs, telemetry, CSV layout authoring, and blackbox dumps without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or VehiclesPhysics authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is one generation validation per lane before fixed tick jobs, CSV reload, editor readbacks, or gizmos. Damage mapping, reduction, state evaluation, publish, and telemetry jobs remain descriptor-free after binding.
Decision 138 - Abyssal thermodynamics opens local descriptor views before solver pointers
Problem: AbyssalThermodynamicsSolver.cs persisted sixteen VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and used ResolvePointer, .Resolve, handle .IsCreated, and GetBufferHandleT across tick scheduling, source mutation, sample jobs, boot initialization, CSV profile load, telemetry reads, GPU upload, blackbox dump, and editor gizmos.
Solution: Replace all persisted solver lanes with VaultGenerationHandleT. Allocate through GetGenerationHandleT, validate descriptors with IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, and derive raw job pointers only from method-local NativeArrayT views. Use TryReadHandle for pure read accessors and diagnostic readback. Route editor-facing tuning mutation through SystemID.CoreDiagnostics writer fence released in finally.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting Burst job pointer ABI was rejected because job fields already carry deterministic Burst flags and NoAlias; unsafe defect was stale handle storage and hidden pointer resolution, not scheduled pointer inputs. Keeping direct editor tuning mutation was rejected because UI Toolkit tuner can outlive Vault relocation. Adding new buffer IDs or DTO layouts was rejected because existing lanes already own thermodynamics truth.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep continuous quality-driven cadence, lower stable grid resolution, fewer Jacobi passes, mock vent fallback, and cheap shader upload. Middle/high/ultra retain high-resolution heat diffusion, richer residual telemetry, blackbox dumps, source profiles, and GPU thermal visualization without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or Thermodynamics authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is one generation validation per lane before tick scheduling, source mutation, sampling, CSV load, upload, or dump. Jacobi diffusion, source injection, residual reduction, telemetry, and sample jobs remain descriptor-free after local binding.
Decision 139 - Thermodynamics hazard grid removes stale handles and worker-retained Vault pointers
Problem: ThermodynamicsHazardGridRuntime.cs persisted nineteen VaultBufferHandleT lanes, resolved them through legacy handle APIs, exposed raw constants pointer to ThermodynamicsTunerWindow, and let ThermodynamicsHazardGridRuntime.FileWorker.cs retain Vault byte pointers on background thread. That combination can survive Vault relocation and makes editor/readback accessors mutate state through hidden routes.
Solution: Replace every persisted hazard lane with VaultGenerationHandleT, allocate through GetGenerationHandleT, and open method-local NativeArrayT views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle or TryReadHandle. Replace editor constants pointer with DTO copy reads plus SystemID.CoreDiagnostics writer-fenced writes. Move mirror-grid mutation into explicit PrepareVaultGridReadback() and keep TryGetVaultGridReadback(...) read-only. Convert config worker to cold byte staging arrays; pin only during file reads, then copy into Vault byte lanes on main owner phase under SystemID.Thermodynamics writer fences before parsing constants.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping background thread on Vault pointers was rejected because MMF/disk IO can overlap relocation windows. Moving all config IO to main thread was rejected because it would trade pointer safety for visible frame hitches. Keeping raw editor constants pointer was rejected because editor windows are long-lived consumers and can outlive Vault relocation. Rewriting deterministic Burst job pointer ABI was rejected because unsafe retention defect was descriptor storage and hidden resolution, not scheduled job inputs derived immediately before schedule.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain continuous lower-resolution hazard grids, lower update pressure, editor-only CSV suppression in player builds, shader heat texture upload, and emergency mock hazards. Middle/high/ultra retain high-resolution diffusion, explicit Vault mirror visualization, updraft signals, telemetry, CSV/binary tuning, and GPU thermal presentation without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or Thermodynamics authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is one generation validation per lane before phase binding and bounded 16-byte/4096-byte config copy on rare reloads. Emission, diffusion, rebase, telemetry scan, signal publish, shader upload, and blackbox loops remain free of per-element descriptor validation; file worker no longer retains raw Vault pointers across frames.
Decision 140 - Fabrication assembler opens local descriptor views and keeps reads pure
Problem: FabricationAssemblerRuntime.cs persisted eight VaultBufferHandleT descriptors, allocated through GetBufferHandleT, resolved all lanes through handle.Resolve(vault), and let TryReadSnapshot, editor stats/debug, and tuning reads call EnsureVaultState(). That meant read accessors could allocate/grow Vault buffers and stale pointer-bearing descriptors could survive relocation before fabrication progress jobs, signal emission, CSV import, telemetry, and GPU upload paths.
Solution: Replace every persisted fabrication lane with VaultGenerationHandleT. Owned lanes allocate through GetGenerationHandleT, borrowed scalability state uses TryGetGenerationHandleT, and all lane views open through method-local IDataVault.TryResolveHandle or TryReadHandle helpers. Read accessors now require runtime to already be initialized and only use read-handle views. Tuning writes use SystemID.CoreDiagnostics writer fence; CSV ingestion opens scratch, timing lookup, and tuning version lanes under bounded writer fences released in finally.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handles because bridge ignores cached pointers was rejected because runtime would still normalize pointer-era descriptor storage. Keeping read accessors on EnsureVaultState() was rejected because read APIs must not allocate, publish, or mutate state. Rewriting existing Burst job structs was rejected because they already consume local NativeArrayT views, carry deterministic Burst flags, and mark non-overlapping arrays with NoAlias; unsafe defect was persistent descriptor storage and hidden resolution.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous quality curve: lower GPU upload count, longer upload stride, low-tier signal capacity, and mock fabrication fallback. Middle/high/ultra retain full shader payload upload, richer fabrication tick/completion signals, CSV timing authoring, telemetry, and visual-overkill assembly edge glow without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or Construction authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime cost is one generation validation per lane before public mutation, dispatcher job binding, telemetry write, GPU upload, or readback. Fabrication progress, signal emission, mock generation, telemetry scan, and shader upload loops remain descriptor-free after local view binding. Designer tuning/CSV writes pay bounded writer-fence atomics and no managed hot-path allocation.
Decision 141 - Retinal adaptation facade resolves through generation descriptors
Problem: RetinalAdaptationVault.cs still opened PredatorRetinalExposure, blindness state, last-published state, light sources, and telemetry ring lanes through direct IDataVault.GetBufferT. file did not persist handles, but it normalized direct mutable buffer route instead of strict pointer-free descriptor route required by SHINOBU202.
Solution: Replace each direct buffer allocation with method-local VaultGenerationHandleT from GetGenerationHandleT, validate expected BufferID, resolve transient NativeArrayT through TryResolveHandle, and assign facade only after every lane meets capacity. returned facade remains native views only; no persistent handle or local collection owner was introduced.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving GetBufferT because facade is small was rejected because migration target is route, not only long-lived storage. Storing generation handles in RetinalAdaptationVaultBuffers was rejected because callers consume arrays and facade should not retain descriptors across owner phases. Expanding into PredatorCognitionDomain.cs was rejected for this loop because that monolith contains broad VaultArrayT debt across many cognition lanes and requires separate blast-radius pass.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing retinal cadence behavior and bounded light capacity. Middle/high/ultra retain current retinal glare, blindness publication, and 300-frame telemetry behavior without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or AI cognition authority. cheap retinal facade remains data route; visual overkill still comes from downstream shader/cognition consumers, not extra facade math.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 cost is one descriptor validation per retinal lane when facade resolves. Per-predator exposure updates, light source priority checks, blindness state publication, and telemetry ring writes remain descriptor-free after owner-phase binding.
Decision 142 - Editor gizmos use registry Vault and descriptor read views
Problem: Arm64AlignmentFaultGizmo.cs and MacroEcosystemHeatmapGizmo.cs used GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated from ordinary editor gizmo drawing. MacroEcosystemHeatmapGizmo.cs also read sector, coordinate, and tuning lanes through direct TryGetBufferT calls.
Solution: Route both gizmos through GlobalRegistry.DataVault. Keep ARM64 fault gizmo on existing Arm64AlignmentTelemetry.TryGetNewestFault(IDataVault, ...) API. Move macro heatmap sector/coord/tuning reads to method-local VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors resolved with TryReadHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping latest-created because these are editor-only diagnostics was rejected because registry-published dependency is available and latest-created should remain bootstrap/crash fallback. Adding new macro heatmap cached handles was rejected because gizmos are read-only diagnostics and should not own ecosystem memory. Touching macro ecosystem runtime ownership was rejected because this pass only fixes editor reader route.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep zero player-build cost because draw paths are editor gated. Middle/high/ultra editor diagnostics retain heatmap and ARM64 fault visualization without changing macro ecosystem DTOs, BufferIDs, or alignment telemetry layout.
Hardware Impact: Runtime i3/MX350 cost is zero in player. Editor scene view pays one registry read per gizmo and three descriptor read validations for macro heatmap before existing bounded draw loop.
Decision 143 - Fabrication smoke fallback registers batch DataVault
Problem: CraftingRuntimeSmokeTester.cs created fallback GlobalDataVault through GlobalDataVault.Create when batch mode had no latest-created Vault, but fabrication runtime now resolves only GlobalRegistry.DataVault. latest-only Vault would leave FabricationAssemblerRuntime.EnsureRuntime() without authoritative registry Vault and break fallback mock data generator expected by CI.
Solution: Replace latest-created probe with GlobalRegistry.DataVault validation. In batch mode only, create fallback Vault and immediately register it through GlobalRegistry.RegisterDataVault before mock fabrication generation.
Rejected Alternatives: Reintroducing latest-created fallback inside FabricationAssemblerRuntime was rejected because runtime owners must use registry dependency route. Creating Vault outside batch mode was rejected because it would hide missing bootstrap order in interactive/runtime contexts. Keeping smoke tester as-is was rejected because it would silently fail mock generator after descriptor migration.
Scalability potential: Low devices and CI keep deterministic mock fabrication setup without touching gameplay truth. Middle/high/ultra retain same mock job shape, shader payload route, telemetry shape, and continuous fabrication quality behavior once registered Vault exists.
Hardware Impact: Player runtime cost is zero. Batch setup pays one unmanaged Vault creation only when no DataVault exists; fabrication mock generation then runs through same registry-backed descriptor lanes as normal runtime.
Decision 144 - Vault diagnostic visual probes use read descriptors
Problem: VaultProbeUtility.cs read existing buffers through direct TryGetBufferT, and VaultMemoryGizmoVisualizer.cs used GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated plus direct TryGetBuffer reads for AUP and hot-entity lanes. These were diagnostics, but they still normalized direct buffer reads and latest-created polling in ordinary editor visualization.
Solution: Move VaultProbeUtility to TryGetGenerationHandleT plus TryReadHandle. Move VaultMemoryGizmoVisualizer to GlobalRegistry.DataVault, descriptor read views for VaultAup64 and VaultHotEntityData, and guarded concrete GlobalDataVault cast only for existing telemetry snapshot API.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping direct reads because diagnostics are low-risk was rejected; diagnostics are long-lived editor consumers and must not train codebase around stale routes. Adding cached handles to gizmo was rejected because SceneView draw path is read-only and should not own Vault descriptor state. Expanding IDataVault for TryGetVaultTelemetrySnapshot was rejected in this loop because it would touch core contracts for diagnostic-only call.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep zero player-build cost for editor gizmo and bounded diagnostic byte probing. Middle/high/ultra retain Vault memory visualization, swap-pop flash inspection, and raw byte probe capability without changing BufferIDs, telemetry layouts, or authority.
Hardware Impact: Runtime i3/MX350 cost is zero for editor-only gizmo paths. Diagnostic probes pay one descriptor read validation per inspected lane; bounded gizmo loop and byte-span scan remain unchanged after view binding.
Decision 145 - Metabolic control editor stops allocating physiology lanes from reads
Problem: MetabolicControlCenterWindow.cs used GetBufferT to read tuning, decompression state, and Haldane coefficient lanes, and then wrote tuning directly through that mutable view. UI refresh could allocate/grow gameplay physiology lanes and slider edit bypassed explicit writer ownership.
Solution: Convert tuning and histogram reads to TryGetGenerationHandleT plus TryReadHandle. Convert slider commits to SystemID.CoreDiagnostics writer fence with release in finally.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping editor GetBufferT because designers need window was rejected; read accessors must not allocate/grow buffers. Creating physiology lanes from this editor was rejected because runtime physiology owns those facts. Migrating larger physiology runtimes in same loop was rejected because they contain broader handle/pointer debt and require separate pass.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep zero player-build cost and cheap editor histograms. Middle/high/ultra retain designer physiology tuning and tissue/M-value visualization without changing physiology DTO layouts, BufferIDs, or runtime quality curves.
Hardware Impact: Runtime i3/MX350 cost is zero. Editor refresh pays descriptor read validation for tuning, state, and coefficient lanes; slider changes pay one diagnostics writer-fence transition.
Decision 146 - Editor tuner windows stop normalizing stale Vault routes
Problem: Three small editor surfaces still normalized unsafe or impure Vault routes: HabitatFluidIncursionTunerWindow.cs read tuning/telemetry through TryGetBufferT and wrote tuning directly, HydrodynamicKccTunerWindow.cs used VaultBufferHandleT plus .Resolve(vault), and NarrativeDagInspectorWindow.cs polled GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated during normal editor drawing.
Solution: Convert fluid and KCC editor reads to TryGetGenerationHandleT plus TryReadHandle; convert tuning writes to SystemID.CoreDiagnostics writer fences released in finally; move narrative inspector to GlobalRegistry.DataVault. KCC missing tuning lanes are created only on explicit write when allocation is not locked, not during read refresh.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping editor direct-buffer reads was rejected because editor windows are long-lived consumers and can outlive Vault relocation. Keeping read-time default writes in KCC was rejected because read accessors must not allocate/grow or mutate global state. Rewriting Quest DAG runtime handles in same loop was rejected because that is broad Quest-domain migration surface; this pass only removed inspector's latest-created dependency.
Scalability potential: Low devices and player builds pay zero cost because these are editor-only windows. Middle/high/ultra retain designer controls, KCC environment visualization, fluid compartment bars, and narrative DAG inspection without changing gameplay truth, DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or continuous quality behavior.
Hardware Impact: Runtime i3/MX350 cost is zero. Editor reads pay one descriptor validation per displayed lane. Editor writes pay bounded writer-fence atomics only on changed sliders; no persistent NativeArrayT fields or cached Vault pointers were introduced.
Decision 147 - Cache B-Tree diagnostics and cold helpers use generation descriptors
Problem: CacheBTreeTopologyXRayWindow.cs still used GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated for editor tuning and telemetry reads, and Cache B-Tree cold helper surface in H8StaticDataContracts.cs still allocated telemetry/tuning lanes through direct GetBufferT. direct routes bypassed descriptor freshness proof and kept ordinary diagnostics tied to latest-created fallback.
Solution: Route editor window through GlobalRegistry.DataVault, read telemetry through TryGetGenerationHandleT plus TryReadHandle, and mutate tuning CSV imports through SystemID.CoreDiagnostics writer fence released in finally. Convert cold helper allocation to GetGenerationHandleT, exact BufferID validation, and TryResolveHandle for method-local native views.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping latest-created in editor was rejected because it is bootstrap/editor crash-only, not ordinary draw/import dependency route. Keeping direct GetBufferT in cold helpers was rejected because it normalizes mutable native views without generation proof. Migrating broader static-data bake/source APIs was rejected because this loop is limited to B-Tree Vault route debt and does not change binary payload identity.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same static-data B-Tree lookup cadence and editor-only diagnostic cost. Middle/high/ultra retain topology x-ray, traversal trace, telemetry waterfall, tuning CSV authoring, and B-Tree telemetry flush without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, Data Monolith identity, save identity, or GlobalQualityWeight authority.
Hardware Impact: Player runtime B-Tree lookup cost is unchanged. Cold setup pays one generation descriptor validation per telemetry/tuning lane; editor telemetry refresh pays one descriptor read validation; CSV import pays one diagnostics writer-fence transition.
Decision 148 - Voxel sculptor editor tuning write uses descriptor writer fence
Problem: ShinobuVoxelSculptorWindow.cs wrote carve debris tuning into CarveDebrisJobState through direct GetBufferint and legacy TryLockBuffer. editor path was bounded, but it still bypassed generation freshness and writer-fence semantics.
Solution: Allocate/borrow CarveDebrisJobState through GetGenerationHandleint, validate exact BufferID, acquire SystemID.CoreDiagnostics writer fence with TryAcquireWriteLock, call existing ShinobuDeltaCrusher.TryWriteCarveDebrisTuning, and release fence in finally.
Rejected Alternatives: Migrating CarveDebrisComputeRenderer.cs in same loop was rejected because it contains broad runtime handle/generation surface that needs separate pass. Keeping TryLockBuffer was rejected because this editor authoring route can use stricter descriptor writer API without changing runtime debris math.
Scalability potential: Low devices and player builds pay zero cost because this is editor-only authoring. Middle/high/ultra retain same carve debris tuning ranges, CSV/binary authoring, and visual-overkill debris caps without changing CarveDebrisJobState, debris DTO layout, BufferIDs, or VFX authority.
Hardware Impact: Runtime i3/MX350 cost is zero. Editor save pays one descriptor validation and one writer-fence transition; debris simulation and indirect draw runtime paths are unchanged.
Decision 149 - VR physical hand presence cold resolver uses method-local generation descriptors
Problem: VRPhysicalHandPresenceIkJobs.cs opened seven fixed hand-presence lanes through direct GetBufferT calls. job DTOs were already explicitly padded and Burst job surface was deterministic, but cold resolver still normalized direct mutable buffer allocation without descriptor freshness proof.
Solution: Add generic method-local TryResolveLaneT helper that allocates/borrows through GetGenerationHandleT, validates exact BufferID, resolves through TryResolveHandle, and verifies capacity before returning native view. Keep existing output arrays and deterministic job ABI unchanged.
Rejected Alternatives: Persisting VaultGenerationHandleT fields was rejected because this static helper has no owner lifecycle and would create descriptor retention for no benefit. Rewriting hand IK job was rejected because hot job already consumes arrays and has explicit DTO layout sentinels; defect was cold Vault route.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing two-hand fixed packet, screen-space fallback, ghost-hand output, and 300-frame telemetry. Middle/high/ultra retain full surface/SDF projection, haptic scrape flags, AUP-local pose lanes, and blackbox telemetry without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, or gameplay authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays seven descriptor validations only when resolver binds lanes. Per-hand IK math, AUP local projection, grab state update, and telemetry write loops remain descriptor-free after binding.
Decision 150 - Leviathan terrain IK cold resolver uses method-local generation descriptors
Problem: LeviathanTerrainIkJobs.cs opened segment, bone, constraint, collider, telemetry, optional SDF, and optional heightmap lanes through direct GetBufferT calls. DTO layouts and deterministic terrain IK job were already explicit, but cold resolver still bypassed generation freshness proof.
Solution: Add method-local TryResolveLaneT helper that allocates/borrows through GetGenerationHandleT, validates exact BufferID, resolves through TryResolveHandle, and verifies capacity. Preserve optional SDF and heightmap lanes by only resolving them when requested count is greater than zero.
Rejected Alternatives: Persisting descriptors was rejected because static resolver has no lifecycle authority and would create retained descriptor state. Rewriting terrain IK jobs was rejected because hot Burst job already consumes local arrays, uses deterministic FloatMode, and carries explicit layout sentinels; defect was only cold Vault route.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep lower segment counts, terrain fallback, and optional zero-count SDF/heightmap lanes. Middle/high/ultra retain full segment capacity, SDF hugging, terrain height samples, collider proxy staging, tail-whip telemetry, and 300-frame blackbox output without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, or Animation/Fauna authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation per active lane only during resolver binding. FABRIK iterations, AUP-local terrain push, SDF/heightmap sampling, collider proxy writeback, and telemetry loops remain descriptor-free after binding.
Decision 151 - Player/save route cleanup uses descriptor proof without changing gameplay truth
Problem: Four gameplay/save surfaces still used direct Vault access: HectonPlayerState.cs allocated player native lanes through generic GetBufferT, HectonPlayerMotor.cs read VoxelSdfTexture3D through TryGetBufferbyte, PlayerInventory.cs read death-penalty rules through TryGetBufferT, and SaveManager.cs allocated WfcOutpostGrid through GetBufferbyte. These routes bypassed generation proof in player movement, inventory, and save persistence seams.
Solution: Convert each route to method-local generation descriptors with exact BufferID validation and TryResolveHandle or TryReadHandle. Preserve fallback behavior in player motor by returning published SDF payload when Vault descriptor proof fails.
Rejected Alternatives: Broadly migrating all player/inventory/save native surfaces was rejected because these files contain unrelated in-flight AUP/layout edits and much larger ownership surfaces. Keeping direct reads because some are cold was rejected because save, inventory, and movement seams are long-lived and rollback-sensitive.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing SDF fallback, player native lane capacities, inventory death-penalty rule route, and WFC save grid shape. Middle/high/ultra retain full voxel traversal, inventory rules, and WFC persistence behavior without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or gameplay authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation at lane binding or command evaluation. Player kinematics, SDF traversal math, inventory rule loops, and WFC serialization remain unchanged after local view binding.
Decision 152 - Atmosphere and bootstrap cold prewarm routes use descriptor proof
Problem: GasDynamicsSolver.cs allocated HabitatBaseAwakeState through direct GetBufferbyte, and GameBootstrapper.cs prewarmed H8Time and RigidbodyAUPs through direct GetBufferT. These were cold paths, but they still trained boot/solver code around mutable native views without descriptor generation proof.

Keeping direct cold prewarm calls was rejected because pointer warden policy targets route normalization, not only hot paths.

Middle/high/ultra retain gas toxicity/hibernation behavior, H8Time scheduling, and global physics AUP prewarm without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, bootstrap identity, or authority route.

Decision 153 - Global physics binding wrapper stores generation descriptors, not pointer handles
Problem: GlobalPhysicsStateManager.cs had private VaultBufferBindingT wrapper that stored VaultBufferHandleT, allocated with GetBufferHandleT, and resolved through Handle.Resolve(dataVault). That wrapper covered rigidbody AUPs, culling lanes, impact events, and physics telemetry, so stale pointer metadata could persist across physics phases.

Preserve existing callers, implicit NativeArrayT conversion, indexer shape, and undersized-buffer reacquire behavior.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting every physics callsite was rejected because private wrapper already centralizes route. Keeping VaultBufferHandleT was rejected because it violates SHINOBU pointer-retention mandate. Broader physics manager changes were not touched because that file has unrelated in-flight AUP, listener, and SignalBus work.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing culling sleep lanes, awake results, impact-event capacity, and AUP arrays. Middle/high/ultra retain full physics culling telemetry, impact feedback, AUP jitter sentinel, and global physics state behavior without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, or physics authority.

Decision 154 - Base module catalog helpers use descriptor proof
Problem: BaseModuleCatalogRuntime.cs allocated six catalog lanes and hydration byte lane through direct GetBufferT, read catalog views through direct TryGetBuffer(...), and tagged telemetry with IDataVault.VaultGenerationID. file is cold/static-data helper, but it feeds construction catalog hydration, socket/cost queries, telemetry, and dump paths, so direct mutable views and broad Vault generation reads violate pointer warden route.

Rejected Alternatives: Keeping direct calls because catalog path is mostly cold was rejected; SHINOBU202 is removing unsafe route normalization, not only hot-path cost. Persisting descriptors in static fields was rejected because these helpers have no owner lifecycle and only need phase-local binding. Rewriting binary hydration, hash lookup, or telemetry DTOs was rejected because bounded defect was Vault access, not catalog math.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same mock catalog fallback, small hydration capacities, immutable binary payload route, and cheap socket/cost queries. Middle/high/ultra retain full construction module catalog hydration, topology lookup, telemetry ring, and blackbox dump behavior without changing Data Monolith identity, save identity, DTO layout, or Construction authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation at catalog bind/read/hydration/telemetry seams. Burst mock generation, binary hydration, hash lookup, socket range query, cost lookup, and telemetry ring writes remain local-array operations after binding.
Decision 155 - Structural integrity borrows voxel SDF through read descriptors
Problem: StructuralIntegrityCalculatorRuntime.cs already owned its structural lanes through VaultGenerationHandleT, but solver borrowed VoxelSdfTexture3D through direct dataVault.TryGetBuffer(...) before and after solver lock window. Allocating/growing SDF lane from structural integrity was rejected because voxel/SDF truth has separate owner. Rewriting solver jobs was rejected because they already consume local NativeArraybyte input and defect was only borrowed lane route.

Middle/high/ultra retain full SDF anchoring, graph stress, collapse signals, shader upload, and 300-frame telemetry without changing voxel DTO layout, structural DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or Habitat/HullIntegrity authority.

Problem: ProceduralCrabLegIKRuntime.cs persisted ten VaultBufferHandleT lanes, allocated them through GetBufferHandleT, and opened them through legacy .Resolve(vault) whenever runtime, registration, origin shift, telemetry, or GPU upload paths needed view. jobs were already data-oriented, but facade carried stale pointer metadata across frames.

Middle/high/ultra retain all-leg raycast mode, analytical two-bone IK, body tilt, indirect draw matrices, origin-shift rebase, and richer visual overkill without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or Animation/Fauna authority.

Decision 157 - Plasma beam VFX facade stores generation descriptors
Problem: ShinobuPlasmaBeamRuntime.cs persisted nine VaultBufferHandleT lanes, allocated them through GetBufferHandleT, and used .Resolve(vault) across editor tuning, mesh snapshots, dispatcher phases, emergency mock beam generation, visual sync, and CSV reload. runtime already fakes beam geometry with procedural vertices and indirect draw args, but Vault facade still retained pointer-bearing metadata.

That kept pointer-era route storage inside GameplayPlayer physiology, including gas-state and CSV scratch routes.
Solution: Convert every physiology Vault lane to VaultGenerationHandleT. Add OpenOrAcquirePhysiologyVaultBufferT, OpenPhysiologyVaultArrayT, OpenPhysiologyVaultBufferT, and IsPhysiologyVaultHandleT. GameplayPlayer-owned lanes now validate exact BufferID, SystemID.GameplayPlayer, nonzero generation, required length, successful TryResolveHandle, and IsCreated before any local native view is returned. Owner initialization is only acquisition path; read/write helpers fail closed if descriptor is missing.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting decompression math, gas toxicity math, tissue compartment defaults, CSV ingestion, blackbox dump format, signal payloads, or job dependency graph was rejected because those systems are separate behavior surfaces. Keeping .Resolve(vault) for editor/mock paths was rejected because those routes are still executable stale-handle surfaces. Adding direct buffers for gas lanes was rejected because it would bypass generation contract.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain bounded physiology rows, quality-weight active compartment scaling, mock depth/gas fallbacks, and cheap shader scalar publication. Middle/high/ultra retain richer gas toxicity, tissue telemetry, CSV tuning, signal output, and visual-overkill physiology shader payloads without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or GameplayPlayer authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation at cold bind, mock/editor read-write, CSV, telemetry, signal publication, and simulation phase boundaries only. Physiology jobs still operate on local native arrays with existing lock chain; no managed hot-path allocation, new job, or hidden main-thread Complete() was introduced by this route migration.
Decision 198 - Spatial audio removes legacy Vault route APIs
Problem: SpatialAudioManager.cs retained multiple audio-owned and borrowed lanes as VaultBufferHandleT, used GetBufferHandleT, ResolveBuffer, .Resolve(vault), direct TryGetBufferbyte for Voxel SDF, and GlobalRegistry.DataVault fallback inside Vault array helper. That kept stale route APIs in virtual voice sorting, acoustic portal data, radar grids, external scalability state, rollback audio suppression, and borrowed Voxel SDF.
Solution: Convert all spatial audio Vault handles to VaultGenerationHandleT. Add TryOpenAudioVaultBufferT, TryOpenBorrowedAudioVaultBufferT, and IsAudioVaultHandleT. Audio-owned lanes validate exact BufferID, SystemID.Audio, nonzero generation, required length, successful TryResolveHandle, and IsCreated; borrowed lanes validate their actual owners: SystemID.GraphicsScalability for scalability state, RollbackNetcodeVault.OwnerSystem for rollback suppression, and SystemID.WorldStreaming for Voxel SDF.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting virtual voice sorting, acoustic portal scratch use, audio source residency, propagation delay, DSP output layout, or mixer policy was rejected because those are behavior surfaces outside this route migration. Keeping persistent VaultBufferHandleT only because file still has native alias fields was rejected; it would leave direct stale-handle APIs in place. Fully removing every long-lived NativeArrayT alias in this loop was rejected as larger audio pipeline rewrite that must be split to avoid compile wall.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain bounded virtual voice budgets, acoustic portal caps, cheap borrowed SDF fallback, and quality-weight audio policy. Middle/high/ultra retain richer virtual voices, acoustic path telemetry, radar upload, DSP material response, and audio overkill without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or authority ownership.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation during cache initialization, borrowed external refresh, and SDF handoff boundaries only. Existing audio jobs still consume current native views; no managed hot-path allocation, new job, or hidden main-thread Complete() was introduced. Residual risk remains: persistent NativeArrayT alias fields should be converted to phase-local opens in later audio-specific pass.
Decision 199 - Tether cable route drops pointer-era Vault handles
Problem: TetherInstance.cs retained twenty-five Physics-owned Vault lanes as VaultBufferHandleT, opened them through GetBufferHandleT, resolved whole buffers and per-slot slices through .Resolve(vault), and used vault.VaultGenerationID as global shortcut before reusing long-lived native views. That left stale pointer-era route semantics in tow cable positions, Verlet solver scratch, visual spline output, tuning, tension forces, and blackbox telemetry.
Solution: Convert every tether Vault lane handle to VaultGenerationHandleT. Add OpenOrAcquireDataVaultCableBufferT, TryOpenDataVaultCableBufferT, and IsDataVaultCableHandleT. Each route validates exact BufferID, SystemID.Physics, nonzero generation, required length, successful TryResolveHandle, and IsCreated before assigning full native view or slot-local subarray. Remove global VaultGenerationID shortcut so bind path revalidates by per-buffer descriptor instead of global Vault epoch.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting Verlet cable solver, tension/snap signal routing, visual bend-point fake, procedural GPU draw ABI, telemetry dump format, or slot reservation model was rejected because defect was stale Vault provenance, not cable behavior. Keeping global Vault generation check was rejected because per-buffer generation handles are proof artifact required by SHINOBU202. Fully eliminating all long-lived NativeArrayT tether view fields in this loop was rejected as larger phase-local view rewrite that must be split to avoid compile wall.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain reduced Verlet segment counts, lower iteration budgets, taut-line visual fallback, bounded telemetry, and fixed slot capacity. Middle/high/ultra retain richer cable sag, more constraint iterations, GPU spline output, tension force publication, creak/snap signals, and visual-overkill material stress without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or Physics authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation at existing tether state bind/phase resolve boundary only. Verlet solve, visual spline build, tension publish, and telemetry writes continue over local native views with existing job graph; no managed hot-path allocation, new job, same-frame readback, or hidden Complete() was added. Residual risk remains: persistent NativeArrayT tether view fields should be converted to phase-local opens in later cable-specific pass.
Decision 200 - Tether AUP support routes use local generation descriptors
Problem: TetherAupVerletJobs.cs kept pointer-era helper routes even though its Burst jobs were already passed explicit native arrays. Telemetry introspection and dump paths used TryGetBufferHandle plus .Resolve(vault), and mock bootstrap used GetBufferHandleT().Resolve(vault) for nodes, constraints, endpoints, spline vertices, force packets, pinned data, telemetry, material rows, CSV scratch, and bootstrap state.
Solution: Add TetherAupVaultRoute, local descriptor helper that opens existing buffers or acquires them only when allocation is legal. Every helper validates exact BufferID, SystemID.Physics, nonzero generation, required length, successful TryResolveHandle, and IsCreated before returning native view. Introspection and blackbox dump are read-only existing-descriptor paths; mock bootstrap is only acquiring path.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting deterministic Verlet jobs, AUP-local float conversion, mock endpoint generator, material row defaults, telemetry dump writer, or cable blackbox format was rejected because those behavior surfaces were not stale route defect. Keeping direct handles in mock bootstrap was rejected because fallback CI data still runs code and must obey same generation proof as runtime systems.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain cheap mock tether count, quality-weight iteration collapse, polynomial cable sway, and bounded 300-frame telemetry. Middle/high/ultra retain richer mock cable motion, higher iteration count, force packet output, material response, and blackbox proof without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or Physics authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation only in telemetry read/dump and mock bootstrap paths. Scheduled Burst jobs still receive same native arrays and dependency handles; no managed hot-path allocation, new job, same-frame readback, or hidden Complete() was introduced.

Generation-change handling now compares per-buffer descriptor generations instead of global Vault epoch.

Reusing Tether AUP helper directly was rejected to keep manager's route proof local and avoid hiding manager blackbox ownership behind support-class name.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain limited active tethers, quality-tier visual bounds, cheap indirect segment impostors, and bounded 300-frame manager blackbox. Middle/high/ultra retain richer procedural tether visuals, more active instances, AUP mock scheduling, and blackbox forensic proof without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or Physics authority.

Rendering buffers, active tether loops, and scheduled AUP jobs keep their existing flow; no managed hot-path allocation, new job, same-frame readback, or hidden Complete() was introduced.
Decision 202 - Habitat fluid incursion removes pointer-era Vault routes
Problem: HabitatFluidIncursionDirector.cs retained Fluid-owned Vault lanes as pointer-era handles and still resolved multiple cold-init, topology, tuning, mass-signal, active/inactive buffer, telemetry, dump, and gizmo paths through .Resolve(vault). migration also needed concrete release path because generation descriptor acquisition increments Vault ownership and clearing descriptors alone would leak refcounts.
Solution: Convert every habitat-fluid Vault lane to VaultGenerationHandleT. Add cached DataVault binding, hot-swap rebind, OpenOrAcquireFluidVaultBufferT, TryOpenFluidVaultBufferT, ResolveFluidVaultBufferT, and IsFluidVaultHandleT helpers requiring exact BufferID, SystemID.Fluid, nonzero generation, required length, successful TryResolveHandle, and IsCreated. DataVault replacement and disable paths now complete pending simulation work, unlock job buffers, release each nonzero descriptor through old Vault, and tombstone all local handles before reacquisition.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting fluid transfer, CSR topology, BFS flood containment, acoustic muffle publication, shader waterline upload, CSV hydration, or mock breach seeding was rejected because behavior already uses bounded cinematic flood model; defect was stale Vault route storage and lifecycle hygiene. Keeping .Resolve(vault) for editor gizmos or blackbox dumps was rejected because those routes still execute and can outlive Vault generation changes. Clearing descriptors without ReleaseBuffer was rejected because it would preserve Vault refcount leak.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain cheap compartment graph, quality-weight solver iteration collapse, bounded 300-frame telemetry, and shader waterline fake. Middle/high/ultra retain richer waterline shader payloads, acoustic flood muffle signals, mass-shift publication, and higher solver cadence without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, blackbox stride, or Fluid authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation at cold bind, fixed/post-fixed/render/editor/CSV/mock/dump boundaries only. Flood solver jobs still consume local native arrays with existing dependency chain; no managed hot-path allocation, tiny job, same-frame schedule/readback loop, or hidden Complete() was added by this route migration.
Decision 203 - Physics force packet buffers use generation descriptors
Problem: PhysicsApplySystem.cs retained four force packet Vault lanes as VaultBufferHandleT and opened them through GetBufferHandleT plus .Resolve(dataVault). Solution: Convert front/back force packet, validation packet, and validation mask handles to VaultGenerationHandleT. Shutdown now releases all four nonzero descriptors through ReleaseBuffer(in handle); validation release uses existing late-frame swap completion helper with forceComplete: true because only release call is cold service shutdown.

Retaining legacy handles because buffers are small was rejected because central force queue is high-authority stale route. Decision 204 - Submarine room mass SoA publish bridge uses descriptor wrappers
Problem: SubmarineFluidDynamics.cs still mirrored room water levels, room volumes, and room local AUPs into shared Vault route through direct TryGetBuffer and GetBufferT calls. Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting flood mass property calculation, submarine hydrodynamic state, room graph ownership, rollback descriptor layout, or consumer ballast code was rejected because those are separate authority surfaces. Allocating empty room SoA rows when no active compartments exist was rejected because previous bridge avoided that cold allocation. Leaving direct GetBufferT was rejected because it bypasses SHINOBU202 generation proof.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain fixed room capacity and cheap post-fixed SoA publishing. Middle/high/ultra retain richer downstream ballast/rollback/stress/cockpit consumers without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or VehiclesPhysics authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor refresh/owner checks at post-fixed publish bridge only. Flood mass jobs, hydrodynamic jobs, signal payloads, and consumer paths are unchanged; no managed hot-path allocation, new job, or hidden completion was introduced.

Problem: HectonShaderGlobalDataVaultBridge.cs already stored shader global slot lane as VaultGenerationHandlefloat4, but cache validation still read vault.VaultGenerationID into cachedVaultGeneration. Releasing method-local descriptors was rejected because GetGenerationHandle does not create per-call refcount lease and these are permanent CoreDataVault rows. Scalability potential: Low devices retain continuous quality-weight sweep budget collapse and minimum bounded sweep. Rationale_SHINOBU_202__late201_1.md
RationaleSHINOBU202
Decision 001 - Non-breaking kernel insertion first
