Problem: repository already has 1700+ references to VaultBufferHandleT compatibility fields and pointer-centric methods. blind ABI rewrite would likely break unrelated systems before generation kernel exists.
Solution: Insert generation-safe API and flat metadata path inside GlobalDataVault first, then migrate consumers against compiling core.
Rejected Alternatives: Immediate repo-wide deletion of pointer fields would create compile wall from unrelated domains and block verification.
Scalability potential: Low tier gets one integer generation compare; middle/high/ultra can enable editor stress relocation and X-Ray diagnostics without shipping those costs.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids hash lookup in new resolve path; expected hot resolve saving is sub-micro per thousands of resolves depending on cache locality.
Decision 002 - Flat metadata mirror, not managed dictionary
Problem: Existing metadata is stored in UnsafeHashMap keyed by BufferID, which is native but still not direct BufferID indexed array required for new handle contract.
Solution: Add NativeArrayVaultBufferMeta mirror sized for 100000 potential handles and update it whenever metadata mutates.
Rejected Alternatives: Managed Dictionaryint, ptr is forbidden and would add GC/object indirection. Replacing entire map in one pass risks breaking current allocator bookkeeping.
Scalability potential: Low uses direct O(1) metadata loads; high/ultra keeps defrag visibility and churn telemetry.
Hardware Impact: About 6.4 MB metadata at 64 bytes per entry; acceptable for core safety and cheaper than UAF crash recovery. i3/MX350 gains predictable cache access versus hash probes.
Decision 003 - Metadata never enters rollback truth
Problem: Generation counters are local memory safety state and cannot be rewound by gameplay rollback.
Solution: Keep VaultBufferMeta in GlobalDataVault runtime memory only and do not expose it to StateRingBuffer/Merkle payload hashing.
Rejected Alternatives: Serializing generation into netcode snapshots would invalidate monotonic safety after resimulation.
Scalability potential: Same behavior across low, middle, high, ultra; no hardware fork.
Hardware Impact: Saves snapshot bytes and avoids rollback-time metadata churn on low-end CPU.
Decision 004 - Legacy pointer handle quarantined instead of ABI demolition
Problem: Existing codebase stores and passes VaultBufferHandleT with pointer/length/stride fields in thousands of call sites, including jobs and editor utilities.
Solution: Add VaultGenerationHandleT as 16-byte pointer-free ABI and route new safety work through it while preserving legacy handle compatibility for compile continuity.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing VaultBufferHandleT in one pass would create uncontrolled compile wall across unrelated domains.
Scalability potential: Low uses pointer-free descriptor resolve. Middle/high/ultra can migrate consumers incrementally and activate force-defrag stress without global breakage.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 gets predictable metadata loads on new path; legacy path remains quarantined until consumer migration.
Decision 005 - Release validation is generation-only
Problem: Full validation of SystemID/type/bounds on every resolve adds ALU and branch cost.
Solution: Gate SystemID, type hash, and bounds checks behind ENABLEUNITYCOLLECTIONSCHECKS. Release path performs flat metadata load and generation compare.
Rejected Alternatives: Hardware-tier validation branches violate no binary quality switch rule and make behavior nondeterministic by device.
Scalability potential: Low through ultra receive identical safety semantics; development builds buy forensic depth with editor-only cost.
Hardware Impact: Low-end CPU avoids hash/type checks in player builds; expected hot path is one indexed load plus one compare.
Decision 006 - Writer authority stored in metadata
Problem: Global mutation guard masks do not expose which system owns specific buffer write.
Solution: Add ActiveWriterSystemID to VaultBufferMeta and claim it with Interlocked.CompareExchange before resolving write view.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting scheduling convention only leaves data races invisible.
Scalability potential: Low fails fast. High/ultra can layer X-Ray and fault visualization over same field.
Hardware Impact: Atomic cost occurs only on write lock acquisition, not read resolve.
Decision 007 - Mock relocation uses metadata generation churn
Problem: Forcing real random memory movement inside live arena can corrupt unrelated systems before consumer migration is complete.
Solution: Add PRESIMULATION-fenced GenerateMockVaultRelocationForValidation that deterministically bumps generations through Burst job.
Rejected Alternatives: Unfenced random MemMove during simulation would be deliberate UAF injector.
Scalability potential: Low runs few mutations; ultra can run larger mutation counts under same continuous maxMutations parameter.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 can stress stale-handle rejection without moving megabytes of payload.
Decision 008 - SHINOBU202 dump is written on blocked UAF
Problem: Access violation prevention is useless without postmortem state.
Solution: On generation mismatch, record current 300-frame ring and write Docs/AgentLogs/DumpSHINOBU202.bin.
Rejected Alternatives: Logging only single stale handle loses pre-fault memory pressure and relocation context.
Scalability potential: Same dump format across all devices.
Hardware Impact: No steady-state cost; IO occurs only on blocked fault.
Decision 009 - Legacy pointer API is quarantined at resolve call, not demolished in one edit
Problem: Static scan now shows 1802 VaultBufferHandleT references and 270 raw pointer lease routes. forced 16-byte rename of legacy struct in one pass would create repo-wide compile wall outside Core memory lane.
Solution: Mark legacy handle type as obsolete, add legacy bridge overloads that convert VaultBufferHandleT into pointer-free generation descriptors internally, and make legacy .Resolve(...), ResolvePointer(...), ref accessors, and tombstone helpers go through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle(...) before deriving any transient pointer.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting handle.ptr during .Resolve(...) was rejected because it preserves UAF risk after relocation. Immediate global consumer rewrite was rejected because blast radius crosses AI, Physics, UI, VFX, Construction, Rendering, and Modding in same batch.
Scalability potential: Low keeps one indexed metadata load and generation compare. Middle/high/ultra can enable strict editor audits and force-defrag stress without shipping managed scanner cost.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes cached-pointer trust from most common legacy .Resolve(...) call path without adding hash-map probes; expected steady cost remains one L1 metadata load plus one integer compare.
Decision 010 - Pointer-retention scanner is editor/CI gated
Problem: "Do not keep long-lived pointers in managers" needs repeatable source gate, not one-time grep pasted into chat.
Solution: Add VaultPointerRetentionScanner under Editor. It writes Docs/AgentLogs/VaultPointerAuditSHINOBU202.md and can hard-fail editor load only when HECTONVAULTPOINTERAUDITSTRICT=1 is set.
Rejected Alternatives: Throwing by default on editor load would currently brick workspace because existing static debt is still above zero. runtime scanner was rejected because managed filesystem IO and source parsing are forbidden in player hot paths.
Scalability potential: Runtime cost is zero across low, middle, high, ultra. CI can enforce gate while player builds remain untouched.
Hardware Impact: No player hardware impact. Editor-only scan cost is O(source bytes) and is manually/CI triggered.
Decision 011 - Memory pressure dump is tied to existing heartbeat
Problem: Task 16 required dumping 300-frame ring when memory exceeds 90% capacity, but previous implementation dumped only on blocked UAF.
Solution: Add heartbeat-side integer pressure check: allocatedBytes 10 = arenaBytes 9, then reuse DumpShinobu202BlackBox().
Rejected Alternatives: Floating-point CapacityPressure01 in branch was rejected to avoid extra conversion and property use inside heartbeat.
Scalability potential: Same threshold across devices; arena size already scales continuously by requested limit and existing vault configuration.
Hardware Impact: One integer multiply/compare per heartbeat; no steady IO unless 90% threshold is crossed.
Decision 012 - Orphan sweep consumes unmanaged live-owner table
Problem: Task 14 requires reclaiming Vault buffers whose owners died without ReleaseBuffer, but scanning Unity scenes or managed services inside Vault would violate Global Authority and inject reflection/managed traversal into Core memory.
Solution: Add SweepOrphanedHandles(...) and Burst SweepOrphanedHandlesJob. Callers supply NativeArraySystemID live-owner table during PRESIMULATION. job marks scene-owned metadata rows missing from that table with VaultMetaFlagOrphanCandidate; main Vault maintenance section then reclaims unlocked candidates, increments generations through tombstone/free, and packs candidate/reclaim counts into 300-frame blackbox Reserved32.
Rejected Alternatives: Direct Unity scene traversal from GlobalDataVault was rejected because Core memory must not own scene hierarchy knowledge. Reclaiming locked or external-view buffers was rejected because live job or bridge still has alias.
Scalability potential: Low devices run sweep rarely with short live-owner table; high/ultra/editor can schedule broader owner audits during maintenance windows. Runtime resolve hot path is unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Sweep cost is O(metadata capacity + liveOwnerCount activeRows) during PRESIMULATION only; zero player-frame pointer validation cost. On i3/MX350 scan is maintenance-only and avoids UAF crash recovery.
Decision 013 - X-Ray waterfall uses fixed UI Toolkit columns
Problem: X-Ray facade exposed current block layout but did not show 300-frame fault/pressure trend requested by Task 17.
Solution: Add fixed 64-column VaultTelemetryWaterfallElement fed from TryGetVaultTelemetrySnapshot(age, ...). Columns encode arena pressure by height/color and generation-mismatch deltas as red pulses.
Rejected Alternatives: Allocating textures or rebuilding VisualElements every refresh was rejected because editor diagnostics must not hide allocation churn. IMGUI repaint-only drawing was rejected because task required UI Toolkit.
Scalability potential: Runtime cost is zero. Editor high-end machines get richer forensic visualization; low-end runtime players do not pay for it.
Hardware Impact: Editor-only fixed 64 VisualElements and fixed arrays; no player CPU/GPU impact.
Decision 014 - Released BufferIDs keep generation tombstone
Problem: Removing metadata on final release erased generation epoch. later allocation with same BufferID could start at generation 1 and theoretically validate stale generation-1 handle.
Solution: Preserve tombstone generation in flat metadata slot when metadata is removed. New allocations call ResolveInitialGenerationForAllocation(key) and start at next epoch instead of resetting to 1.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping freed buffer in active metadata map was rejected because it would look live to ownership scans. managed per-BufferID dictionary was rejected because flat native table already owns this fact.
Scalability potential: Low through ultra get identical safety. hot resolve path stays one indexed metadata load plus generation compare; only allocation/release maintenance pays epoch update.
Hardware Impact: One flat metadata read during allocation and one tombstone write during release. On i3/MX350 this is negligible compared with avoiding stale handle access violation.
Decision 015 - First Core manager migrated to pointer-free descriptors
Problem: source audit found persistent legacy VaultBufferHandleT fields in managers. Leaving every manager on pointer-bearing bridge would keep enforcement story theoretical.
Solution: Migrate BurstTokenBucketJobAdmissionService from five persistent VaultBufferHandleT fields to five VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors. Each accessor resolves through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle(...) into phase-local NativeArrayT, and teardown calls ReleaseBuffer before clearing descriptors.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting all 1800+ legacy references in one pass was rejected as cross-domain compile wall. Keeping this Core service on obsolete handles was rejected because it is small enough to migrate safely.
Scalability potential: Low devices remove cached pointer fields from scheduling service. High/ultra/editor keep same diagnostics because underlying Vault telemetry is unchanged.
Hardware Impact: Hot path remains one descriptor BufferID guard plus Vault generation compare. Teardown adds five cold-path release calls and prevents leaked references.
Decision 016 - Data Monolith arena stops caching NativeArray views
Problem: H8StaticDataArena kept static NativeArraybyte view and three legacy Vault handles, then telemetry used ResolvePointer. Data Monolith payload can be relocated by Vault maintenance; caching native view defeats generation invalidation.
Solution: Store only VaultGenerationHandlebyte, VaultGenerationHandleH8DataMonolithTelemetryEntry, and VaultGenerationHandleint. Every section, localization, hash, file-read, and telemetry route resolves method-local NativeArrayT through TryResolveHandle. Shutdown releases all three descriptors through ReleaseBuffer.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping arena and refreshing it opportunistically was rejected because it remains long-lived alias. Migrating entire Data Monolith compiler/editor was rejected because it is editor-owned static-data tooling and outside this Core runtime alias surface.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same zero-copy static-data reads with generation validation. High/ultra/editor retain Data Monolith telemetry dumps without raw pointer leases.
Hardware Impact: Runtime reads add one flat metadata generation compare when public static-data route resolves arena; this is cheaper than UAF recovery and does not allocate. Shutdown adds three cold release calls.
Decision 017 - StaticDataStore telemetry stops leasing Vault pointers
Problem: StaticDataStore still resolved static-data and B-Tree telemetry rings through pointer-bearing Vault handles. Those rings are shared forensic buffers; relocated Vault allocation would leave stale ring/cursor pointers in manager.
Solution: Replace telemetry fields with VaultGenerationHandleT and add TryResolveBlackBox / TryResolveBTreeTelemetry helpers. Dump and record paths resolve method-local NativeArrayT views immediately before use, then take read-only pointers only for synchronous dump writers.
Rejected Alternatives: Releasing shared telemetry BufferIDs from StaticDataStore.Shutdown was rejected because BabelDictionaryStore and static helper contracts also use same IDs; refcount ownership must be split before destructive release. Keeping ResolvePointer was rejected because whole fault class is cached-pointer trust after relocation.
Scalability potential: Low devices pay one flat generation compare on cold telemetry paths. Middle/high/ultra keep 300-frame B-Tree and static-data forensic rings without persistent manager aliases.
Hardware Impact: Removed five pointer-bearing telemetry descriptors from store. Runtime hot lookup remains B-Tree dominated; telemetry write/dump adds O(1) generation validation and no managed allocation.
Decision 018 - Babel telemetry and fallback aliases are quarantined
Problem: BabelDictionaryStore had five telemetry VaultBufferHandleT fields, Vault-backed ERROR span pointer, and padded dictionary fallback pointer derived through ResolvePointer. telemetry/error routes could be migrated safely; padded dictionary has active lore read jobs and must not be moved while raw pointer job reads it.
Solution: Convert telemetry and BabelErrorUtf8 to VaultGenerationHandleT with local TryResolveHandle calls. Convert padded dictionary fallback to GetBufferbyte so GlobalDataVault marks it as external view and live defrag refuses to relocate that block while raw pointer job path exists.
Rejected Alternatives: partial generation handle around padded dictionary was rejected because it would still leave basePointer and scheduled pointer jobs stale after generation bump. Rewriting B-Tree/lore jobs to pure NativeArraybyte in this pass was rejected as SHINOBU207 ownership and too large for Vault ABI migration lane.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep zero-copy Babel reads and defrag-blocked fallback blob. High/ultra retain B-Tree telemetry and lore job throughput; next owner pass can replace pointer jobs with NativeArray jobs for relocatable overkill.
Hardware Impact: Removed all legacy VaultBufferHandleT / ResolvePointer routes from BabelDictionaryStore. padded fallback may block compaction for one dictionary blob, but avoids UAF on i3/MX350 and Quest-class hardware until lore job is rewritten.
Decision 019 - Core memory diagnostics stop exporting legacy handles
Problem: VaultMemoryContracts, VaultLegacyBinaryArchaeology, and VaultProbeUtility still exposed or consumed obsolete pointer-bearing Vault handle routes inside Core memory lane. Even if bridge resolves safely, leaving those APIs in diagnostics trains future code to persist VaultBufferHandleT.
Solution: Convert sovereignty telemetry ring to VaultGenerationHandleT, convert memory-layout config hydration/writes to generation descriptors plus local TryResolveHandle, and replace public diagnostic TryGetHandle helper with TryGetGenerationHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping obsolete diagnostic wrapper was rejected because no callers existed and API would reintroduce pointer-bearing manager state. repo-wide signature purge was rejected because unrelated domains still own large legacy debt and require staged migration.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same flat generation compare. Middle/high/ultra editor diagnostics retain probe ability without exporting stale pointer descriptors.
Hardware Impact: Hot player paths are unchanged. Cold telemetry/config/diagnostic routes add no GC and avoid future cached-pointer misuse; i3/MX350 pays only existing O(1) Vault metadata resolve when these routes execute.
Decision 020 - Hardware thermal blackbox uses generation descriptors
Problem: HardwareThermalService persisted two VaultBufferHandleT fields and refreshed them through ResolveBuffer. This kept Core runtime manager on pointer-bearing descriptors even though its thermal severity byte and blackbox ring are owned Vault buffers.
Solution: Replace both fields with VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve local NativeArrayT views through TryResolveHandle, allocate through GetGenerationHandleT, and release descriptors through ReleaseBuffer during teardown or DataVault hot-swap.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving this service on legacy bridge was rejected because it is small Core-owned manager with clear Vault ownership. Rewriting hardware policy/scalability behavior was rejected because task is pointer safety, not thermal policy redesign.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same thermal sampling cadence and blackbox size. Middle/high/ultra preserve thermal diagnostics without cached pointer state; no binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one O(1) generation compare when severity byte or 300-frame blackbox is touched. Cold teardown now returns two Vault references instead of leaking them across service reloads.
Decision 021 - SignalBus frame snapshots are phase-local views
Problem: SignalBusT kept static NativeArrayT frameSnapshot alias and legacy VaultBufferHandleT. Because every closed signal lane can survive across frames, this was generic long-lived Vault alias at Core signal scale.
Solution: Remove static NativeArrayT field, convert frameSnapshotHandle to VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve local snapshot view in each read/flush/filter/sort path, refresh descriptor with TryGetGenerationHandleT after generation churn, and release descriptor on lane disposal.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached view for speed was rejected because task is specifically to prevent stale relocatable aliases. Rewriting SignalBus policy, lane lists, or signal DTO layouts was rejected because those changes are outside pointer-safety lane and already have unrelated working-tree edits.
Scalability potential: Low devices pay only flat generation compare when signal snapshots are consumed or flushed. High/ultra keep deterministic snapshot sorting/coalescing and can tolerate Vault relocation stress without stale alias reuse.
Hardware Impact: One O(1) metadata compare replaces long-lived alias hazard across all typed signal lanes. No GC is added; no interface array hot dispatch is introduced by this pass.
Decision 022 - Alignment telemetry proves faults without legacy handles
Problem: Arm64AlignmentTelemetry used static legacy Vault handle and three .Resolve(vault) routes for diagnostic ring that records alignment faults. stale diagnostic ring would weaken exact evidence path used to prove ARM64 layout violations.
Solution: Convert ring to VaultGenerationHandleAlignmentTelemetryEntry, resolve local views for record/read/dump, and release old descriptor if cached Vault instance changes before reacquiring ring.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving SHINOBU204 diagnostic code untouched was rejected because it is Core memory telemetry route and small enough to migrate safely. Adding copied managed ring was rejected because diagnostics must remain Vault-backed and zero-GC in record/read paths.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same 300-entry ring and cold dump path. High/ultra/editor retain richer alignment fault proof without cached pointer handles.
Hardware Impact: Diagnostic record/read paths pay one flat generation compare and no GC. Vault hot-swap no longer leaks previous alignment telemetry descriptor.
Decision 023 - Simulation bucketer tables use generation descriptors
Problem: ModuloSimulationBucketer persisted eight legacy VaultBufferHandleT fields for front/work bucket tables, EWMA cost/load tables, rebalance scratch, frame state, and 300-frame blackbox. Re-init/dispose cleared handles locally without returning Vault references.
Solution: Convert all eight fields to VaultGenerationHandleT, allocate through GetGenerationHandle, resolve method-local NativeArrayT views through TryResolveHandle, and release all non-zero descriptors through ReleaseBuffer after pending rebalance job is completed.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping bucketer on legacy bridge was rejected because this service sits in Core dispatcher cadence path and is small enough to migrate safely. Rewriting bucketing math or unrelated existing quality-curve work was rejected because current pass is pointer safety.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous bucketing cadence and survival distribution behavior. Middle/high/ultra retain rebalance and blackbox telemetry while removing stale descriptor state; no binary hardware branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one flat generation compare when bucketing table is touched. Cold re-init/teardown now performs eight release calls and prevents Vault refcount leaks.
Decision 024 - Lockstep hash sources validate resolved views, not cached ptr
Problem: LockstepStateValidator.TryGetHashSourceBuffer acquired local VaultBufferHandleT, checked handle.ptr for alignment, then called handle.Resolve(vault). That route proved cached pointer, not generation-validated transient view actually hashed for determinism.
Solution: Use TryGetGenerationHandleT and TryResolveHandle to obtain local NativeArrayT view first, then validate alignment through buffer.GetUnsafeReadOnlyPtr() before hashing.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping local legacy handle was rejected because rollback hash proof should not depend on any cached pointer field. Persisting hash-source descriptor was rejected because this method only needs phase-local view.
Scalability potential: lockstep hash cadence remains governed by existing continuous quality/stress curve. Low through ultra keep identical pointer safety semantics with no tier branch.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one flat generation compare only when hash-source buffer is requested; no GC and no additional persistent native state.
Decision 025 - Input bridge facade writes through resolved NativeArray
Problem: H8InputMappingFacade wrote BridgeInputFacadeBindings through local VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and ResolvePointer, leaving bridge hydration on cached-pointer route.
Solution: Allocate or acquire buffer with GetGenerationHandle, resolve local NativeArrayH8InputFacadeBindingEntry through TryResolveHandle, clear via transient GetUnsafePtr() on that view, and write entries through indexed NativeArray access.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw pointer writes was rejected because ScriptableObject bridge sync can run in Play Mode after Vault relocation. Introducing persistent facade-owned handle was rejected because mapping source is serialized facade list, not runtime buffer owner.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same bridge sync behavior; high/ultra get same data route without cached pointer state. No binary tier branch was added.
Hardware Impact: Sync path pays one flat generation compare and one transient MemClear; no additional GC beyond existing serialized editor list.
Decision 026 - Prefab registry binder hydrates bridge DTOs through local views
Problem: H8PrefabRegistryRuntimeBinder hydrated prefab mapping and lore link buffers through local VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and ResolvePointer in both bind and clear paths.
Solution: Acquire BridgePrefabMapping and BridgePrefabLoreLinks with GetGenerationHandle, resolve local NativeArrayT views through TryResolveHandle, clear through transient GetUnsafePtr() on those views, and write DTO entries by index.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw pointer hydration was rejected because prefab registry binding can run during Play Mode after Vault relocation. Persisting static binder handles was rejected because registry asset is authoring source and binder does not own runtime lifetime.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same registry bind route. Middle/high/ultra retain runtime acoustic/lore signal publication without cached Vault pointer state.
Hardware Impact: Bind path pays two flat generation compares and two transient MemClear calls; no added managed allocation.
Decision 027 - Design bridge runtime avoids local pointer-bearing descriptors
Problem: H8BridgeFacadeRuntime used local VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and ResolvePointer for design value bytes, macro header persistence, and 300-frame facade telemetry dump ring. These are local variables, but they still route bridge live-tuning writes through obsolete cached-pointer API.
Solution: Convert each route to GetGenerationHandle or TryGetGenerationHandle, then resolve method-local NativeArrayT through TryResolveHandle. Value writes use transient pointer derived from resolved byte view only for aligned float store; telemetry hash/dump now reads entries through resolved NativeArrayT.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy bridge because handles were local was rejected; source audit policy is to prevent new code from learning ResolvePointer. Persisting bridge handles was rejected because bridge facade asset, not runtime, owns authoring fact.
Scalability potential: Low devices pay one flat generation compare per bridge buffer touched. Middle/high/ultra keep live tuning, macro persistence, and blackbox dumps without cached Vault pointer state; no binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids stale pointer trust in live tuning and blackbox dump routes. extra O(1) generation compare is colder than existing facade iteration, signal publication, and dump IO.
Decision 028 - Content authority ledgers use generation descriptors
Problem: ContentRuntimeServices persisted six VaultBufferHandleT fields across bundle ref counter and content runtime for resident bundle state, telemetry, and pending-load queues. These managers can survive DataVault replacement and were resolving raw pointers from pointer-bearing descriptors.
Solution: Convert all six fields to VaultGenerationHandleT, add local resolve-or-acquire helpers that return NativeArrayT views, derive pointers only from those views inside current method, and release descriptors on ref-counter vault rebind, runtime teardown, and DataVault hot-swap.
Rejected Alternatives: Ignoring content because it had unrelated Addressables/hot-swap changes was rejected; Vault handle edits are separable. Rewriting Addressables ownership was rejected because that is existing SHINOBU203/ContentAuthority work and outside this pointer-safety pass.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same pending-load and telemetry cadence with one flat generation compare per access. Middle/high/ultra retain content blackbox evidence and live residency accounting without stale Vault aliases; no binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 loses persistent pointer-bearing descriptor fields in content manager. Teardown/hot-swap now returns six Vault references instead of leaking or leaving invalid descriptors after service replacement.
Decision 029 - Base homeostasis buffers use generation descriptors
Problem: HomeostasisBrain.cs persisted three legacy handles for global hardware metrics, frame-time samples, and its 300-frame blackbox. This authority controls quality pressure and survives registry DataVault replacement, so stale handles here can poison global throttling.
Solution: Store VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors, resolve or reacquire method-local NativeArrayT views through TryResolveHandle, avoid clearing existing moved buffers after generation churn by probing TryGetGenerationHandle before allocation, and release descriptors during shutdown or DataVault hot-swap.
Rejected Alternatives: Migrating larger HomeostasisBrain.ScalabilityDictator.cs in same pass was rejected because it owns additional job-fenced state and deserves separate review. Keeping base file on legacy handles was rejected because base migration is compact and directly protects global quality authority.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous GlobalQualityWeight path with one flat generation compare per buffer. Middle/high/ultra retain homeostasis blackbox evidence and visual-overkill pressure policy without cached Vault aliases.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes three persistent pointer-bearing descriptors from global pressure manager. Shutdown and hot-swap now return three Vault refs instead of clearing static fields only.
Decision 030 - Scalability dictator buffers use generation descriptors
Problem: HomeostasisBrain.ScalabilityDictator.cs still persisted seven VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and used .Resolve(vault) / GetElementAsRef for health, quality state, tuning, mock load, mock terrain proof, CSV scratch, and 300-frame oscilloscope. This kept highest-level quality authority on pointer-bearing routes after base file was migrated.
Solution: Convert all seven buffers to VaultGenerationHandleT, reuse base TryResolveOrAcquire helper, and resolve only method-local NativeArrayT views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle. Editor/test facades copy structs out of resolved view, sanitize/mutate, and write row back by index. DataVault hot-swap now releases scalability descriptors against previous Vault before dataVault is replaced, after completing pending mock terrain sampler job.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping dictator on legacy bridge was rejected because it is Core-owned and controls GlobalQualityWeight. Holding ref rows from GetElementAsRef was rejected because ref access is derived from cached-pointer compatibility handle. Rewriting continuous scalability math was rejected because existing math already uses smooth weights and this pass is memory safety.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain cheap mock terrain proof and quality telemetry with one generation compare per buffer touch. Middle/high/ultra keep visual-overkill policy, oscilloscope, CSV tuning bridge, and shader-quality globals without any persistent Vault alias.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes seven pointer-bearing descriptors from global pressure dictator. Hot tick writes pay one flat metadata compare for state and telemetry views; teardown/hot-swap now returns seven Vault refs instead of leaking or clearing local descriptors only.
Decision 031 - AUP origin-shift lanes use generation descriptors
Problem: AupOriginShiftCoordinator persisted eight VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and resolved AUP states, velocities, history, telemetry, runtime state, mock camera, CSV scratch, and padded counter through .Resolve(vault). These buffers are direct targets for origin-shift and defrag relocation, so stale descriptors here undermine AUP precision contract.
Solution: Convert all eight descriptors to VaultGenerationHandleT, add local TryResolveOrAcquire helper, and route tick/rebase/editor/CSV paths through method-local NativeArrayT views from IDataVault.TryResolveHandle. On cached Vault replacement, release all non-zero descriptors against previous Vault before clearing local state.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping origin shift on legacy bridge was rejected because this file moves double3 AUP payloads and can run during same maintenance windows that relocate Vault buffers. Rewriting origin-shift algorithms was rejected because existing AUP math already subtracts in double precision before float-local work; this pass is descriptor safety.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain time-sliced rebase batches from GlobalQualityWeight; middle/high/ultra keep larger batches and telemetry without cached Vault aliases. No binary tier branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one flat generation compare when AUP lanes are resolved. 64-byte padded counter remains false-sharing isolated; hot rebase jobs still receive phase-local pointers derived from validated NativeArrayT views.
Decision 032 - Crash blackbox no longer retains Vault aliases
Problem: GlobalTelemetryBus.Blackbox.cs persisted eleven legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and eleven static Vault-backed NativeArrayT aliases. buffers were lifetime-locked, but Core manager retaining native views still violates generation-handle contract and hides release/refcount leaks during crash-path shutdown.
Solution: Convert all blackbox lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT, add local TryResolveBlackboxBuffer helper, and resolve method-local NativeArrayT views in event push, source registration, frame commit, dump writing, MMF flushing, watchdog probing, and editor copy routes. Binding failure and teardown now release every non-zero descriptor after unlocking relocation fences.
Rejected Alternatives: Relying on TryLockBuffer alone was rejected because it prevents relocation instead of proving manager can survive relocation-era handles. Keeping cached arrays only for speed was rejected because this is forensic infrastructure, not sub-0.1 ms gameplay solver.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same 300-frame blackbox and MMF cadence with descriptor validation only on touched lanes. Middle/high/ultra retain richer crash forensics and watchdog coverage without persistent Vault views. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one flat generation compare when blackbox lane is touched; shutdown now returns eleven Vault refs instead of leaking them. Long-lived manager-side NativeArrayT aliases are removed from this file.
Decision 033 - Memory sentinel validates targets under generation locks
Problem: MemorySentinelRuntime persisted ten VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and used TryGetBufferHandle / ResolvePointer to watch external targets. It also unlocked target buffers before consuming validation results and rollback copies, leaving relocation window around stored target pointers.
Solution: Convert owned sentinel lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT with TryResolveOrAcquire, resolve all owned buffers through local NativeArrayT views, and acquire external target pointers from TryGetGenerationHandle plus TryResolveHandle. CompleteValidationJob now keeps locks active through ConsumeResults and releases them in finally after rollback/correction work.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping ResolvePointer in memory sentinel was rejected because it audits stale pointers while using stale-pointer API. Removing target pointers from MemorySentinelTargetDTO in this pass was rejected because scheduled validation job still needs locked phase-local pointers; lock fence now covers their full use window.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing GlobalQualityWeight cadence collapse for validation frequency. Middle/high/ultra can validate more frequently without stale descriptor debt. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one flat generation compare for each sentinel lane or watched target view. rollback copy no longer races against Vault defrag after target unlock.
Decision 034 - Input haptics tuner stops teaching legacy pointer APIs
Problem: InputCurveHapticsTunerWindow.cs was editor-only, but it still demonstrated GetBufferHandle, VaultBufferHandleT, and GetElementAsRef for deterministic input profile/state buffers. That keeps obsolete pointer-bearing access patterns alive in designer-facing code and makes future runtime copy-paste defects more likely.
Solution: Replace local profile/state handles with VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve NativeArrayT views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle inside OnGUI, read rows by index, mutate profile value locally, and write row zero back by index after EditorGUI.EndChangeCheck.
Rejected Alternatives: Ignoring editor code was rejected because Task 17/18 facades are part of SHINOBU202 human-control surface. Releasing descriptors from window was rejected because this window is not owner of ShinobuInputProfile or ShinobuInputCurrentDto; it only observes or edits owner-created buffers through existing Vault route.
Scalability potential: Low devices see no runtime cost because this is editor-only. Middle/high/ultra editor sessions still get live curve/haptics visualization while resolving through same generation descriptor path as runtime managers.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime unchanged. Editor repaint pays two flat generation compares and copies 88 bytes of DTO data, removing all obsolete pointer-bearing source hits from this facade.
Decision 035 - Input dispatcher resolves Vault views per phase
Problem: InputDispatcher.cs persisted twelve VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and used .Resolve, GetElementAsRef, GetElementAsReadOnlyRef, and background-thread inputReplaySnapshotHandle.ptr path. Deterministic input, haptic commands, XR state, and replay snapshot buffers cross frame boundaries, so cached Vault pointers here can produce UAF during defrag or DataVault replacement.
Solution: Convert all input-owned Vault descriptors to VaultGenerationHandleT, add resolve/acquire helpers that return method-local NativeArrayT views, replace ref access with row index copies, release descriptors on shutdown and DataVault hot-swap, and move replay snapshot copying into StageInputReplaySnapshot while local view is valid. replay worker now flushes MMF only and does not dereference Vault memory.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping replay worker on cached Vault pointer was rejected because it is clearest stale-pointer race in file. Removing replay snapshot lane outright was rejected because deterministic bridge still expects Vault-backed snapshot audit row; safer minimal change is generation resolution plus phase-local copy.
Scalability potential: Low devices pay flat generation comparisons for input/haptic/XR lanes and keep existing continuous haptic throttle behavior under pressure. Middle/high/ultra preserve deterministic replay, richer haptic composition, and XR look-at state without storing Vault aliases.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes twelve pointer-bearing descriptors and one background stale-pointer path. replay path still copies same 12 KB payload at its existing cadence; hot input writes add only metadata generation checks.
Decision 036 - System dispatcher owns phase fences through generation descriptors
Problem: SystemDispatcher.cs persisted legacy Vault handles for H8 time, dispatcher blackbox, master job/fence telemetry, presentation suppression, and static raycast command/hit buffers. dispatcher is also system that defines when Vault relocation is legal, so cached pointer-bearing descriptors in this file can invalidate entire "defrag only between phases" safety model.
Solution: Convert all dispatcher-owned descriptors to VaultGenerationHandleT, add single generation resolve/acquire helper that returns method-local NativeArrayT views, and release old descriptors during shutdown or DataVault service replacement. Scheduled raycast buffers keep their existing Vault lock fence while scheduled RaycastCommand job owns local views; handles themselves are pointer-free.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping ResolveBuffer around domain fence array was rejected because AUP hard-fence cleanup can run during relocation pressure. Keeping static raycast handles as legacy pointers was rejected because raycast scheduling spans frames and can outlive compaction window. Rewriting dispatcher scheduler was rejected because this pass is descriptor safety, not topology refactor.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous GlobalQualityWeight behavior for frame pacing, temporal compression, and presentation suppression; middle/high/ultra keep richer master telemetry and raycast scheduling without cached Vault aliases. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays flat generation comparisons when dispatcher lanes are touched. expensive work remains job dependency combining, raycast scheduling, and ring writes; stale pointer access during Vault defrag is removed from phase owner.
Decision 037 - Analytics exporter worker resolves locked buffers by generation
Problem: AsynchronousTelemetryExporter.cs persisted seventeen VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and H8AnalyticsIO worker created NativeArrayT views directly from cached handle.ptr values. exporter also wrote hot ingress events through ingressCursorHandle.ptr and selected ingress handle pointer, leaving both main-thread and background-thread UAF paths.
Solution: Convert every exporter-owned descriptor to VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve main-thread and worker views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, and retain existing owner-tagged Vault locks only as compaction fence while worker is alive. Shutdown releases descriptors only after StopWorker() succeeds and worker locks are removed.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping worker-owned buffers on VaultBufferHandleT.ptr was rejected because lock is relocation fence, not permission for managers to persist pointer metadata. Releasing descriptors when StopWorker() fails was rejected because worker can still be alive and resolving handoff/dump buffers; preserving locks is safer failure mode.
Scalability potential: Low devices still shed routine analytics continuously through GlobalQualityWeight, backlog pressure, and deterministic AUP hashing. Middle/high/ultra keep richer route samples, heatmap debug, network batch size, and disk replay without cached Vault pointer route.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays O(1) generation checks for event ingress and worker scratch resolution. expensive worker path remains RLE/network/disk I/O; stale Vault pointer dereference is removed from both main and background threads.
Decision 038 - Acoustic echo static queue uses pointer-free Vault descriptors
Problem: AcousticEchoLocationRuntime.cs persisted four static VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and resolved pending taps, frame taps, job results, and 300-frame blackbox through cached pointer metadata. Echo tap queues can cross frame/defrag windows, so static queue was UAF candidate even though Burst tracking job itself only needs phase-local views.
Solution: Convert four AISensory lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT, add resolve/acquire/release helpers, and keep all queue drain/drop, job schedule, blackbox, and fault dump access on method-local NativeArrayT views returned by IDataVault.TryResolveHandle. Dispose and DataVault replacement release only descriptors owned by this static runtime; active tracking fence is completed before old descriptors are released.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping ReleaseOwnerBuffers(SystemID.AISensory) was rejected because it can free unrelated AISensory buffers owned by neighboring static services. Replacing tracking job or acoustic scoring model was rejected because this pass is pointer safety; existing quality-weight scoring already gives continuous cheap/expensive behavior.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep direct echo breadcrumb scoring and quality-byte attenuation; middle/high/ultra preserve richer portal/movement/sonar tap density without pointer retention. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation compare when enqueueing, draining, scheduling, or writing blackbox rows. expensive path remains existing O(n) tap scan capped at 32 taps; stale Vault pointer metadata is removed from static sensory queue.
Decision 039 - Path funnel navmesh resolves WFC invalidation lanes by generation
Problem: PathFunnelNavmeshRuntime.cs persisted five VaultBufferHandleT descriptors, relied on legacy handle Length and GenerationID, and resolved mutation/telemetry/runtime-state views through .Resolve(...). fast tick also used TryGetBuffer for WFC grid flags, bypassing generation descriptor route used by migrated consumers.
Solution: Convert path-funnel owned lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT, derive actual lengths from transient resolved views, and route every active-path, cell-mask, invalidation, telemetry, runtime-state, and WFC-grid access through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle. Disable/hot-swap releases only this component's owned descriptors.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping TryGetBuffer for external WFC grid was rejected because it normalizes direct Vault views outside generation descriptor contract. Releasing all SystemID.AIPathfinding buffers was rejected because other pathfinding systems can share owner ID.
Scalability potential: Low devices still use bounded 500-bit masks and ring cursors; middle/high/ultra can increase active path and invalidation capacities while retaining phase-local descriptor resolution. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays flat generation checks when path APIs or tick phases touch Vault lanes. dominant cost remains bounded scan of active corridors against WFC cell masks; stale pointer metadata is removed from path invalidation state.
Decision 040 - WFC laser cut tool writes Vault progress through phase-local arrays
Problem: WfcLaserCutRuntime.cs persisted two static VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and converted their cached .ptr fields into raw float progress and telemetry pointers. same file used GlobalRegistry.ScalabilityTier for visual overkill, producing hard tier branch in user-facing VFX path.
Solution: Convert cut progress and blackbox lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve local NativeArrayT views per cut attempt, and rewrite progress clear/telemetry/dump paths to index those views instead of pointers. Replace tier branching with continuous smoothstep over HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight, modulated by system stress headroom.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping raw pointers as "short-lived" locals was rejected because they were derived from persistent pointer-bearing descriptors and used in gameplay truth writes. Keeping tier switch was rejected because quality-weight already supplies required continuous control scalar.
Scalability potential: Low devices collapse molten/spark overkill smoothly as quality/stress drops; middle/high/ultra regain richer cut visuals continuously without feature pop. No binary quality branch remains in this file.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation checks per active cut attempt and few scalar ops for visual curve. expensive work remains shader feedback and signal fanout; stale Vault pointer writes are removed from tool path.
Decision 041 - Ladder climb IK schedules only generation-resolved views
Problem: ProceduralLadderClimbRuntime.cs persisted five VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and staged its IK solve job through .Resolve(dataVault) views. Disable/destroy only cleared handles, leaving Vault refcount/generation state untouched.
Solution: Convert IK input/output, ladder AUP, telemetry ring, and telemetry cursor descriptors to VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve method-local views before reads/writes/scheduling, and release five owned descriptors after completing any outstanding IK job during teardown or DataVault replacement/loss.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handles because this is presentation IK was rejected; job consumes Vault-backed AUP and telemetry data and can race relocation if manager keeps pointer metadata. Owner-wide release was rejected in favor of exact descriptor release.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same cheap slide/grip solve cadence; middle/high/ultra retain richer IK targets and telemetry without pointer retention. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays five generation checks when staging or reading IK views. dominant cost remains Burst IK solve; stale Vault handle metadata is removed from animation locomotion.
Decision 042 - Tool haptics front/back lanes stop refreshing legacy handles
Problem: ToolHapticsRuntime.cs persisted front/back VaultBufferHandleHapticCommand descriptors and called ResolveBuffer(ref handle) before every haptic buffer access, keeping pointer-bearing metadata alive in manager.
Solution: Convert both lanes to VaultGenerationHandleHapticCommand, cache active IDataVault, resolve local NativeArrayHapticCommand views per haptic operation, and release old descriptors on DataVault loss/replacement or teardown.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping ReadOnlySpan snapshots as only change was rejected because stale descriptor route would still exist before span is created. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact front/back descriptors are known.
Scalability potential: Low devices still compact and decay 16-command buffer; middle/high/ultra keep richer command blending and sinusoidal feedback without pointer retention. No binary quality branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation compare per front/back lane access. dominant haptic work remains bounded command compaction/merge; stale Vault metadata is removed from tool rumble.
Decision 043 - Procedural bone blender schedules only generation-resolved views
Problem: ProceduralBoneBlenderRuntime.cs persisted eleven VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and used .Resolve(vault) in editor, CSV, mock rig, telemetry, GPU upload, and Burst scheduling paths. Disable/destroy and DataVault replacement cleared descriptors without releasing owned Vault lanes.
Solution: Convert all fauna procedural bone lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT, add shared resolve/acquire helper that uses IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, resolve NativeArrayT views only inside active method/phase, and release exact descriptors after completing outstanding solver jobs on disable, destroy, or DataVault replacement.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy descriptors for editor-only routes was rejected because those same handles feed runtime solver and telemetry paths. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact buffer IDs are known and broader release would cross another owner boundary if future lanes share SystemID.AnimationFauna.
Scalability potential: Low devices still collapse update cadence through existing continuous GlobalQualityWeight; middle/high/ultra keep GPU matrix upload and richer procedural bone response without pointer retention. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays eleven generation compares when staging fauna solve and few compares on editor/telemetry reads. dominant cost remains Burst solve and GPU buffer copy; stale Vault metadata is removed from animation path.
Decision 044 - Kinetic character animator removes descriptor and direct-view debt
Problem: KineticCharacterAnimatorRuntime.cs persisted twelve VaultBufferHandleT descriptors, resolved them through .Resolve(vault), and also fetched PlayerKinematicState / VoxelSdfTexture3D through direct TryGetBuffer calls. Teardown and DataVault replacement cleared descriptor fields without releasing Vault lanes.
Solution: Convert all locomotion animation lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT, add generation-checked owned and external resolve helpers, route player and SDF reads through method-local TryGetGenerationHandle + TryResolveHandle, and release exact owned descriptors after solver completion on disable, destroy, and DataVault replacement.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping TryGetBuffer for external read-only lanes was rejected because read-only does not make stale aliases safe after relocation. Releasing all SystemID.AnimationLocomotion buffers was rejected because adjacent locomotion runtimes can share owner ID.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain existing continuous quality-weighted locomotion/SDF degradation; middle/high/ultra keep richer IK and GPU matrix output without persistent Vault views. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays twelve generation compares for owned staging and two local external descriptor resolves on player/SDF frames. dominant cost remains Burst locomotion/matrix work; stale Vault descriptors and direct external Vault views are removed from manager.
Decision 045 - Laser cutter scalability read uses generation descriptor
Problem: LaserCutterDodRuntime.cs had one remaining TryGetBufferHandle route for ShinobuScalabilityState, leaving legacy descriptor path inside otherwise generation-descriptor tool runtime.
Solution: Replace quality-weight read with TryGetGenerationHandleScalabilityStateDTO and TryResolveHandle, keeping resolved NativeArrayScalabilityStateDTO local to ResolveGlobalQualityWeight().
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping old route because it is read-only was rejected; relocation still invalidates pointer-bearing handle metadata regardless of write intent.
Scalability potential: Low/middle/high/ultra visuals continue to use same continuous quality scalar; only descriptor acquisition route changed.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 cost is one generation handle resolve on quality reads. It removes final legacy handle API hit in this runtime without changing cut math.
Decision 046 - Tool kinematics editor facade stops using legacy handles
Problem: ToolKinematicsTunerWindow.cs cached seven VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and used ResolveBuffer(ref handle) / .Resolve(vault) while Play Mode editor tuning can observe and mutate live Vault lanes.
Solution: Convert editor descriptors to VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve local editor views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, and release exactly editor-acquired descriptors when window closes or Vault reference changes.
Rejected Alternatives: Treating editor windows as harmless was rejected because they run against Play Mode memory and can hold stale descriptors across defrag/rebind events.
Scalability potential: Runtime scalability is unchanged; editor facade now observes same quality-weighted tool kinematics state without preserving pointer-bearing handles.
Hardware Impact: No player-frame cost. Editor draws pay generation checks while tuner window is open; stale Vault metadata is removed from facade.
Decision 047 - Tool kinematics runtime drops legacy handles and ref-return API
Problem: ToolKinematicsRuntime.cs persisted fifteen VaultBufferHandleT descriptors, resolved them through ResolveBuffer(ref handle) / .Resolve(vault), and exposed unused public ToolKinematicsVaultAccess class that returned refs via GetElementAsRef.
Solution: Convert all runtime lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve method-local NativeArrayT views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, release exact descriptors on disable/destroy or Vault rebind, and remove unused ref-return accessor class.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping ref-return accessor with generation handles was rejected because returning refs from transient views invites callers to keep byref access beyond safe execution phase. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact ToolKinematics buffer IDs are known.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous LOD hold and beam raymarch limits; middle/high/ultra keep richer tool beam/IK/spark output without persistent Vault descriptors. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays fifteen generation compares while staging tool jobs. dominant cost remains Burst raymarch/beam jobs; stale Vault descriptor metadata and public byref mutation routes are removed.
Decision 048 - Tool durability removes false-positive legacy naming
Problem: ToolDurabilitySystem.cs already used VaultGenerationHandleT and TryResolveHandle, but its local helper was named TryResolveBuffer, which caused broad legacy Vault scans to surface false-positive ResolveBuffer-like route.
Solution: Rename helper and callers to TryResolveDurabilityView without changing allocation, BufferID, DTO, or job behavior.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving name was rejected because audit noise slows detection of real stale pointer routes in tools and animation.
Scalability potential: Runtime scalability is unchanged; durability still uses existing generation-descriptor state lanes.
Hardware Impact: No runtime change. benefit is audit precision: broad scans now separate safe generation views from forbidden legacy resolve calls.
Decision 049 - Vocal warning manager stops storing Vault aliases
Problem: VocalWarningSystem.cs persisted six Vault-backed NativeArrayT aliases and six legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for queue, warning state, and telemetry lanes. Vault relocation after boot could leave manager indexing stale array metadata.
Solution: Replace all six descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, add phase-local VwsVaultViews value, resolve views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle inside queue mutation, slow tick, telemetry, and dump paths, and release exact descriptors during teardown/rebind.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping aliases because VWS has no Burst job was rejected; UAF risk is independent of job scheduling. ReleaseOwnerBuffers was rejected because exact BufferIDs are known and owner-wide teardown hides descriptor ownership mistakes.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same small priority queue and cooldown cadence; middle/high/ultra keep full warning telemetry and radio-degrade presentation. No binary quality branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays six generation compares on VWS mutation/slow paths. This is below clip submission and subtitle routing cost and removes stale Vault metadata from audio warning manager.
Decision 050 - Native audio frame ring resolves buffers per operation
Problem: NativeAudioFrameRingBuffer.cs persisted Vault-backed frames and sharedState aliases plus two VaultBufferHandleT descriptors. native output ring also exports raw pointers to audio bridge, so cached manager aliases were direct relocation hazard.
Solution: Replace both handles with VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve local RingVaultViews value for buffer state, writes, clearing, shared metadata access, and native descriptor creation, and release exact frame/shared-state descriptors on dispose.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping frames/sharedState because ring is internal was rejected; internal managers still survive across defrag. Owner-wide release was rejected because ring owns exactly two known BufferIDs.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain same bounded SPSC copy and overflow drop reporting; middle/high/ultra keep larger ring capacities and native bridge output without retaining stale managed-side Vault aliases.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation compares for ring state/write/descriptor operations. hot cost remains sample copy and native plugin handoff; stale manager-resident Vault aliases are removed.
Decision 051 - Dynamic music resolves DSP buffers from generation views
Problem: DynamicMusicGranularSynthesizer.cs persisted Vault-backed arrays for DSP voices, scalars, tuning, output buffers, biquad, telemetry, CSV scratch, preset rules, grain bank, shared state, and scalability state. It also cached output pointers. bounded Vault relocation would invalidate those aliases while manager, editor facade, audio callback, or scheduled jobs still believed metadata was stable.
Solution: Replace all owned descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, add method-local DynamicMusicVaultViews resolver, pass local views into editor/cold CSV/audio/job/telemetry paths, take raw pointers only immediately before job scheduling or file/native copy, and release exact owned descriptors on teardown. external scalability state is borrowed through TryGetGenerationHandle and resolved transiently.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached aliases because this is audio system was rejected; audio paths are relocation-sensitive and must not retain stale manager-side Vault metadata. Releasing by owner was rejected because synth owns fixed BufferID set and exact release exposes descriptor drift.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous density/cutoff/sample cadence collapse through GlobalQualityWeight; middle/high/ultra keep full granular voices, telemetry, and stinger richness. No binary hardware branch was added.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation checks at scheduling/cold/editor/audio-copy boundaries. hot DSP loop still runs from phase-local pointers inside Burst jobs; stale persistent aliases are removed without adding GC.
Decision 052 - Adaptive stem mixer stops retaining Vault aliases
Problem: AdaptiveStemAudioMixer.cs persisted eleven Vault-backed arrays and eleven legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for stem state, commands, rules, mock signal rows, telemetry, CSV scratch, and scalability state. mixer also used binary low/high scalability fallback after signal ingress.
Solution: Replace owned descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, add method-local AdaptiveStemVaultViews resolver, resolve views before editor/tick/job/telemetry/CSV operations, borrow scalability state through TryGetGenerationHandle, release owned descriptors exactly, and map HectonQualityTier through Smooth01 into continuous 0.1..1.0 fallback weight.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping aliases because mixer is presentation-only was rejected; presentation systems still schedule Burst jobs and can crash after relocation. Binary LowMx350 ? 0.1f : 1f was rejected because it creates hard quality discontinuity.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep slow update cadence and cheap crossfade; middle/high/ultra smoothly restore faster cadence and richer stem blending without branch pop.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation checks on mixer phase boundaries, not per sample. gain is removing stale Vault aliases from adaptive-stem job scheduling and telemetry paths.
Decision 053 - Player critical renderer first removes pointer-bearing ownership
Problem: PlayerCriticalProceduralAudioRenderer.cs is last large audio file with broad Vault debt. It held 50 persistent NativeArrayT aliases and acquired them through pointer-bearing VaultBufferHandleT plus handle.Resolve; teardown used owner-wide release.
Solution: First isolate ownership from pointer metadata: add 50 VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors, make central ResolveVaultBuffer helper use GetGenerationHandle plus TryResolveHandle, and replace owner-wide release with exact release of known descriptors after outstanding audio/SDF/composite jobs are completed.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting entire 11k-line renderer in one pass was rejected because producer thread, sonar jobs, VWS double buffer, and reverb state share lifetime constraints. Keeping VaultBufferHandleT until final pass was rejected because it leaves highest-risk pointer-bearing API in largest audio owner.
Scalability potential: Runtime audio quality behavior is unchanged in this slice. Low/middle/high/ultra renderer math and existing perceptual audio fakes remain stable while ownership metadata becomes generation-checked.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays no new sample-loop cost. Bind/release paths pay O(buffer-count) generation descriptor work; remaining work is phase-local view migration for persistent aliases.
Decision 054 - Player critical low-risk rings move to phase-local views
Problem: After descriptor ownership was fixed, PlayerCritical still kept 50 persistent Vault aliases. smallest safe runtime slice was isolated VWS double-buffer lane plus granular/prologue telemetry and prologue command rings; these are bounded and do not require rewriting full producer DSP graph.
Solution: Remove five persistent NativeArrayT fields and resolve VWS clip buffers, granular telemetry, prologue transition telemetry, and prologue transition command rings through generation handles at operation boundaries. Keep producer sample loops free of per-sample resolve calls.
Rejected Alternatives: Attempting to migrate all frame scratch/reverb/sonar/granular voice arrays in one patch was rejected because those arrays cross audio producer loop and scheduled sonar jobs. Deferring all aliases was rejected because isolated rings were easy to harden immediately.
Scalability potential: No visual/audio quality behavior changed. Low-tier and high-tier renderer fakes keep their existing cadence; postmortem and VWS lanes now survive relocation more predictably.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays O(1) generation checks on VWS submit/playback, prologue queue, and telemetry operations. No inner DSP loop resolve was introduced.
Decision 055 - Player critical granular SOA resolves once per producer block
Problem: PlayerCritical still retained metallic grain bank and eight granular voice SOA buffers as long-lived NativeArrayT fields. Those arrays are mutated in audio-rate code, so resolving them per sample would be correct but too expensive; keeping them as fields preserved stale-alias UAF risk.
Solution: Remove nine persistent aliases, add GranularVoiceVaultViews, resolve view once in CanProduceAudioBlock, pass it through RenderHullStressBlock, RenderStructuralGranularVoices, and MixAndFilterBlock, and update voice arm/trim/slot helpers to mutate local NativeArray descriptors copied from phase view.
Rejected Alternatives: whole-renderer DSP view was deferred because sonar/reverb/frame scratch buffers cross scheduled jobs and require separate dependency pass. Per-voice/per-sample resolution was rejected because it burns audio-thread cycles without improving safety over block-scoped view.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain cheap granular voice budgets and linear envelopes; middle/high/ultra still unlock denser voice counts and interpolation through existing continuous tuning. migration does not add hardware binary branch.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays nine generation validations once per produced block. hot sample loop reuses local NativeArray descriptors and keeps existing O(active voices) granular fake instead of heavier structural simulation.
Decision 056 - Player critical binaural and low-pass state resolves once per producer block
Problem: Binaural ITD delay, ear-shadow history, and final listener low-pass histories remained as long-lived NativeArrayT fields. They are small, but they are mutated every producer block and are still invalid after Vault relocation.
Solution: Remove six aliases, add BinauralFilterVaultViews, resolve it once in CanProduceAudioBlock, pass it by ref through MixAndFilterBlock and ApplyBinauralSpatializationBlock, and resolve same view in ClearLowPassState for cold reset.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping histories as fields because they are tiny was rejected; UAF risk is independent of byte count. Resolving inside SampleBinauralDelay or ApplyBinauralShadowEar was rejected because those functions execute per sample/ear and would add avoidable validation branches.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous binaural mix, underwater shadow cutoff, narcosis chorus, and abyssal low-pass curves stay unchanged from low through ultra. change is pointer-lifetime only.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays six generation validations per produced block. per-sample binaural and low-pass loops use local descriptors and keep their existing arithmetic profile.
Decision 057 - Player critical reverb state resolves once per producer block
Problem: Sabine reverb, cave convolution, and interior FDN delay buffers remained as persistent NativeArrayT fields. These are among larger PlayerCritical buffers and are mutated in hot sample loops, so stale aliases can crash and per-sample resolution would be too expensive.
Solution: Remove four aliases, add ReverbVaultViews, resolve view once in CanProduceAudioBlock, pass local descriptors through Sabine comb, cave convolution, and interior FDN helpers, and resolve same generation view for cold impulse bake and reset clears.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping reverb fields because they are audio-private was rejected; Vault relocation can invalidate audio-private views exactly like cross-domain views. Resolving inside each comb/convolution tap was rejected because it would multiply handle validation by sample count and tap count.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous reverb DSP tier selection, wet mix, openness, and acoustic density curves remain unchanged. Low devices still fall back to cheaper Unity/profile-only paths; high/ultra keep native Sabine/convolution richness.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays four generation validations per produced block. Hot reverb loops keep local NativeArray descriptors and avoid new branches inside comb, convolution, and FDN tap math.
Decision 058 - Player critical transient delay lines resolve once per producer block
Problem: Impact clang and thruster comb delay lines remained as persistent NativeArrayT fields. Both are small compared with reverb, but they are audio-rate mutable delay lines and can become stale after Vault relocation.
Solution: Remove two aliases, add TransientDelayVaultViews, resolve it once in CanProduceAudioBlock, pass it through impact event consumption, hull stress rendering, and thruster rendering, and clear it through method-local view during reset.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping these fields until frame-scratch pass was rejected because they are isolated and cheap to harden now. Resolving in RenderImpactClangSampleInternal or each thruster comb iteration was rejected because it would add per-sample validation.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous thruster pressure/cavitation and impact metallic fakes stay unchanged across low/mid/high/ultra. migration changes lifetime only.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two generation validations per produced block. Hot Karplus/comb loops use local NativeArray descriptors.
Decision 059 - Player critical frame scratch resolves once per producer block
Problem: Hull, sonar, impact echo, thruster, heartbeat, bubble, mix, and stereo scratch buffers were still manager-held NativeArrayT aliases. These buffers are re-used every audio block, so stale aliases would survive Vault relocation and crash in producer path.
Solution: Remove nine scratch aliases, add FrameScratchVaultViews, resolve view once in CanProduceAudioBlock, and pass it by ref into render, mix, and binaural stages. Cold reset and prologue probe paths resolve same view only for duration of their clear/probe operation.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping scratch fields because they are short-lived data was rejected; alias lifetime was manager lifetime, not scratch semantic lifetime. Resolving inside each render function was rejected where producer already has block view.
Scalability potential: Existing continuous quality curves for granular FM, reverb tier, binaural blend, and bubble intensity remain unchanged. Low devices pay one block-level validation set and keep same cheap DSP fakes; high/ultra keep dense procedural output.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays nine generation validations per produced block. Hot sample loops use local descriptors and retain prior arithmetic profile.
Decision 060 - Player critical sonar storage is split into phase-local Vault views
Problem: remaining sonar buffers were highest UAF risk: publish taps, worker taps, DSP echo delay/filter state, SDF hit cache, and composite coalescing scratch were all persistent NativeArrayT fields. Some are touched from read accessors, some from audio producer blocks, and some from scheduled jobs.
Solution: Remove all 15 sonar aliases and split resolution into SonarTapVaultViews, SonarDspVaultViews, and SonarSpatialVaultViews. UI read accessors resolve only tap buffers, audio DSP resolves tap+DSP state once per block, and SDF/composite phases resolve spatial buffers at schedule/publish boundaries. editor smoke test now verifies handle/view usage instead of stale fields.
Rejected Alternatives: single PlayerCriticalAudioVaultViews blob was rejected because TryGetCockpitSonarEchoTaps must stay pure read accessor and must not over-resolve DSP or SDF buffers. Per-tap generation resolution was rejected because it would multiply validation by echo count inside sonar publish loop.
Scalability potential: Sonar keeps existing capped echo tap fake and continuous SDF probe budget. Low devices use fewer probes/ghost taps through existing quality weights; high/ultra can keep richer SDF returns without changing authority or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes all sonar manager-held native aliases. Validation cost is bounded to phase entry: four checks for tap views, six for DSP views, five for spatial views. Delay/filter loops use local descriptors.
Decision 061 - Vocal warning pending queue is collapsed into Vault priority queue
Problem: VocalWarningSystem.cs still owned pendingWarningIds as private NativeQueuebyte allocated with Allocator.Persistent. It was tiny, but it was still manager-owned native allocation outside GlobalDataVault, and it duplicated Vault-backed AudioVocalWarningQueue fact.
Solution: Remove private NativeQueuebyte, pendingNativeCount, prewarm, drain, sentinel registration, and dispose path. TryQueueWarning now resolves VwsVaultViews once, writes cooldown/severity/source state, and inserts warning id directly into Vault-owned bounded priority queue via InsertOrPromote.
Rejected Alternatives: Replacing queue with another Vault staging buffer was rejected because bounded priority queue already handles duplicate suppression, capacity, and priority replacement. Keeping staging queue because it is only 16 bytes was rejected because UAF and ownership violations are independent of capacity.
Scalability potential: Low devices skip extra staging dequeue pass on slow tick. Middle/high/ultra keep same warning priority behavior, telemetry ring, and radio-degrade presentation without changing DTO layout or authority route.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes one persistent native allocation and one TryDequeue drain loop per slow tick. TryQueueWarning already paid six generation checks for VWS state; direct insert reuses same resolved view and does not add sample-loop or job-loop cost.
Decision 062 - Spectrum sonar discovery and telemetry views move to Vault descriptors
Problem: SpectrumSystem.cs owned aupDiscoveryGrid and activeSonarGeoTelemetryRing as local persistent NativeArrayT fields, manually allocated and registered with NativeMemorySentinel. editor smoke test also asserted that old ownership model, making unsafe route self-reinforcing.
Solution: Replace both fields with VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors. AUP discovery grid uses BufferID 71030; active-sonar telemetry ring uses BufferID 71031. TryGetAupDiscoveryGrid, reveal stamping, telemetry writes, and dump code resolve local views from cached IDataVault and release exact descriptors on destroy.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping grid local because it is visor presentation was rejected; sonar reveal memory is read by UI/audio-facing systems and must survive Vault relocation without cached aliases. Resolving grid once per stamped cell was rejected because octant shell fake stamps nine cells and only needs one phase-local resolve.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same cheap octant-shell discovery fake and 300-frame blackbox cadence. Middle/high/ultra can retain richer sonar shader presentation because CPU path still avoids full flood-fill or physics ray loops.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes two local persistent NativeArray allocation/disposal routes. Sonar reveal pays one generation validation per pulse shell, then writes up to nine grid cells through local descriptor.
Decision 063 - Topographical sonar stops persisting pointer-bearing Vault handles
Problem: TopographicalSonarSynthesizer.cs persisted eleven legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for point cloud rows, hit masks, counters, mock SDF/material payloads, 300-frame telemetry, CSV scratch, indirect args, and shader globals. Even without explicit private NativeArrayT fields, legacy descriptors carried pointer metadata and used handle.Resolve, so Vault relocation could leave stale lease path in UI sonar system.
Solution: Replace all eleven descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, cache IDataVault once through ResolveDataVaultCold, resolve method-local views with IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, and release each exact descriptor during teardown after outstanding scan/fade job fences complete. shutdown path now decrements Vault references instead of only defaulting local handles.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handles because system is visual-only was rejected; visual sonar still schedules Burst jobs and uploads GPU buffers from Vault data. Calling GlobalRegistry.DataVault at every resolve site was rejected because registry is cold identity and dependency injection only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous ray-count collapse, mock SDF fake, and GPU point rendering. Middle/high/ultra keep denser point clouds, material LUT color, indirect draw args, and shader globals without changing ownership or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays O(1) generation checks at scan/fade/upload/telemetry phase boundaries. Per-ray SampleTopographicalSonarJob and per-point fade loops use local NativeArrayT descriptors and do not revalidate handles inside hot loop.
Decision 064 - PDA frequency tuning resolves Vault waves through generation descriptors
Problem: PDADecryptionSpectrogramPanel.cs persisted six legacy VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and one shared helper used handle.Resolve(vault) for wave rows, GPU segments, stage targets, and 300-frame telemetry ring. It also cleared descriptors on teardown instead of releasing Vault references.
Solution: Convert six descriptors to VaultGenerationHandleT, make shared helper validate existing handles through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, reacquire descriptors through GetGenerationHandleT when absent or undersized, and release exact descriptors on teardown/DataVault replacement after completing scheduled wave job.
Rejected Alternatives: Releasing inside resolve helper after transient resolve failure was rejected because compaction fence or temporary Vault unavailability must not decrement ownership from hot resolve path. Keeping old helper was rejected because handle.Resolve can use stale pointer metadata.
Scalability potential: Low devices continue to collapse spectrogram point count through continuous GlobalQualityWeight and VRAM clamp. Middle/high/ultra keep denser wave segments, GPU tube rendering, and telemetry without changing minigame truth route.
