Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays bounded generation checks at phase entry. Burst wave generation/error jobs still receive local NativeSliceT views and do not validate per point.
Decision 065 - Babel subtitle runtime stops retaining legacy Vault descriptors
Problem: BabelSubtitleSyncRuntime.cs persisted two static VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and resolved subtitle cue/telemetry buffers through handle.Resolve. static runtime survives scene churn and can keep pointer-bearing metadata alive across Vault relocation or DataVault replacement.
Solution: Replace both descriptors with VaultGenerationHandleT, resolve cue and telemetry buffers through cached IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, reacquire with GetGenerationHandleT during cold initialization, and release BufferIDs 15070550 and 15070551 on subsystem reset or DataVault hot-swap after fencing any active cue evaluation job.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handle because runtime already used method-local NativeArrayT values was rejected; persistent descriptor itself still carried pointer metadata. Releasing from ordinary read helpers was rejected because transient compaction fence must not mutate ownership from read accessor.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same continuous subtitle dirty budget collapse through ResolveCanvasDirtyBudget. Middle/high/ultra keep same visual-only cue flow and 300-frame telemetry without changing authority, DTO layout, or save identity.

Decision 066 - CharBufferPool Babel arena removes latest-vault and legacy descriptor routes
Problem: CharBufferPool.cs persisted static VaultBufferHandlechar for Babel arena and resolved it through handle.Resolve. It also used GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated() as fallback, which is bootstrap/editor/diagnostic/crash-only route and should not be UI formatting dependency.
Solution: Replace Babel arena handle with VaultGenerationHandlechar, resolve method-local NativeArraychar views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle, acquire with GetGenerationHandlechar, release descriptor on subsystem reset, and use only GlobalRegistry.DataVault for cold Vault injection. When no Vault exists, existing managed TMP bridge arrays remain fallback.
Rejected Alternatives: Releasing on every resolve failure was rejected because compaction fences and temporary Vault unavailability must not mutate ownership from read path. Keeping TryGetLatestCreated() was rejected because it hides implicit global heap/diagnostic dependency in UI helper.
Scalability potential: Low devices can skip native arena and use fixed TMP bridge arrays when Vault is unavailable. Middle/high/ultra retain Vault-backed Babel arena without changing text capacity, save identity, or localization authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation when Babel span or native-to-TMP copy uses native arena. fallback path avoids Vault lookup churn and uses preallocated bridge arrays already owned by pool.
Decision 067 - PDA shell borrows glitch glyph table instead of owning it
Problem: PDAShellChrome.cs persisted VaultBufferHandlebyte and used ResolvePointer against DiegeticGlitchSurgeonRuntime.GlitchTableBufferIdRaw. file also allocated shared table through GetBufferHandle and could fall back to GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated(), making PDA chrome component implicit owner of shared glitch glyph fact.

On invalid/missing table, fall back to table-free glitch encoder and clear borrowed descriptor.

Releasing on disable was rejected because PDA shell is now borrower, not owner. Keeping TryGetLatestCreated() was rejected because it is crash/diagnostic bootstrap-only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep table-free glitch encoder path when shared table is absent. Middle/high/ultra use richer glyph substitution table when owner has published it, without changing text layout, save identity, or authority route.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation only when stress-reactive strings need table. no-table fallback avoids Vault allocation and keeps existing fixed scratch buffer path.

Adding private telemetry array fallback was rejected because it would create second proof artifact.

These methods are called by vehicle automation code across frames, so Vault relocation could leave docking slot reads/writes pointed at dead memory.

Disable/shutdown/DataVault replacement release descriptor through owning Vault.

Adding private active-spline mirror was rejected because docking truth would split into two owners. Reacquiring via GlobalRegistry.DataVault inside each service method was rejected because registry access is cold DI path only.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same bounded 64-slot default and cubic Dear Lie docking curve. Middle/high/ultra can raise serialized capacity up to 256 without changing DTO layout, authority route, or slot semantics.

Problem: FaunaBrain.cs persisted two VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for one-row corpse-sink kinematic input/output buffers and resolved them through .Resolve(vault). helper also polled GlobalRegistry.DataVault from schedule/complete boundary, which is active runtime work, not cold injection.

Problem: LSystemGenomeLabWindow.cs used TryGetBufferHandle(BufferID.FloraGenomeDtos, out VaultBufferHandleFloraGenomeDTO) and handle.Resolve(vault) in editor facade. Editor windows can remain open across Vault reloads, so even editor-only pointer-bearing descriptors keep stale-alias pattern alive.
Solution: Borrow BufferID.FloraGenomeDtos with TryGetGenerationHandle and resolve method-local genome view with TryResolveHandle inside OnGUI. Missing or empty buffers still use existing mock preview.
Rejected Alternatives: Ignoring editor code was rejected because Task 17 requires Vault X-Ray/editor facades to model safe handle access. Allocating or populating flora genomes from this window was rejected because flora genome ownership belongs to flora genome runtime/baker, not preview UI.
Scalability potential: Low devices are unaffected; this is editor-only. Middle/high/ultra preview still uses same high-tier L-system preview controls without changing runtime flora DTO layout or quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 runtime impact is zero. Editor cost is one descriptor validation per OnGUI preview pass.
Decision 090 - Save delta helpers stop producing pointer-bearing descriptors
Problem: EntityDeltaGizmoProbe.cs, EntityDeltaCompressionArchitecture.cs, and VoxelDeltaCompressionArchitecture.cs still used TryGetBufferHandle or GetBufferHandleT plus .Resolve(vault). Save delta buffers are binary payload routes; stale descriptors here risk corrupting or misreporting WAL/delta state.
Solution: Replace gizmo read with TryGetGenerationHandle plus TryResolveHandle; replace both compression architecture helpers with GetGenerationHandleT plus TryResolveHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving these as cold/editor helpers was rejected because binary save routes are precisely where stale views are least acceptable. Reworking compression or checksum logic was rejected because defect is descriptor lifetime, not codec math.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same frame-budgeted save/WAL cadence and emergency mock schemas. Middle/high/ultra keep richer save telemetry and larger payload throughput through same DTOs without changing save identity or quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation per helper acquisition or gizmo draw. RLE, checksum, WAL, and gizmo sector loops do not validate per byte or per sector.
Decision 091 - Visual pressure aging removes duplicate Vault generation metadata route
Problem: VisualPressureAgingRuntime.cs stored generation descriptors but still called TryGetBufferGeneration in owned buffer validation, initialization recovery, external input validation, and stale-external detection. That made descriptor validity depend on separate metadata fact before same handle was resolved.
Solution: Use TryResolveHandle through existing descriptor helpers as single proof of generation freshness. Keep IsHandleForBuffer, IsExternalHandleValid, owner checks, and required-length checks unchanged.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping generation metadata polling because it was explicit was rejected; explicit duplicate facts are still route drift. Rebuilding visual aging Vault layout was rejected because payload identity and shader ABI are already explicit and outside this pointer-lifetime pass.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same low-tier visual aging/degradation collapse and CSV tuning. Middle/high/ultra keep richer UberNoir degradation telemetry and shader upload through same descriptors without changing quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 removes metadata poll at validation gates. Aging/degradation jobs, telemetry pushes, and graphics-buffer uploads continue over local views without per-element descriptor checks.
Decision 092 - Fluid dynamic wake buffers stop carrying pointer handles
Problem: HectonFluidEngine.cs persisted VaultBufferHandlefloat4 descriptors for WakeGlobalBuffer and WakeVectorBuffer, allocated through GetBufferHandle, and resolved with .Resolve(vault) immediately before GPU upload. Dynamic wake presentation can run across Vault compaction or DataVault replacement, so pointer-bearing descriptors are unsafe even when data is visual.
Solution: Store VaultGenerationHandlefloat4 descriptors, borrow existing wake buffers during allocation-locked phases, allocate with GetGenerationHandle only when unlocked, and resolve method-local NativeArrayfloat4 views with TryResolveHandle before upload.
Rejected Alternatives: Removing dynamic wake route was rejected because shader-side wake fake is cheap visual substitute for CPU fluid simulation. Releasing wake buffers on fluid teardown was not added because prior route only cleared descriptors here and wake ownership is already documented as multi-owner conflict with VFX lanes.
Scalability potential: Low devices can fail closed to existing empty wake buffer and low-tier wake params. Middle/high/ultra keep richer dynamic wake GPU advection from same two 16-slot float4 lanes without changing shader ABI or quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays two descriptor validations per dynamic wake upload phase. upload loop still copies local NativeArrayfloat4 views to GPU buffer and does not validate per slot.
Decision 093 - Seed Ship shader slot bridge removes VaultGenerationID cache
Problem: SeedShipAnomalyShaderBridge.cs cached VaultBufferHandlefloat4 plus vault.VaultGenerationID for BufferID.ShaderGlobalState. metadata generation cache could say "current" while pointer-bearing descriptor still represented stale address state.
Solution: Store VaultGenerationHandlefloat4, resolve slot views with TryResolveHandle, and use TryGetGenerationHandle/GetGenerationHandle only to acquire descriptor. Direct shader globals remain as fallback when Vault slot lane is unavailable.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping VaultGenerationID for fast cache was rejected because generation descriptor already carries proof and must be validated by resolve. Removing direct shader globals was rejected because anomaly presentation should fail closed visually even when Vault slot allocation is unavailable.
Scalability potential: Low devices can publish cheap scalar globals only. Middle/high/ultra keep richer shared shader slot route without changing slot index, DTO layout, or quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation per publish path. bridge writes one float4 slot and does not validate per shader parameter.
Decision 094 - Submarine structural breach lanes stop using pointer handles
Problem: SubmarineStructuralGrid.cs persisted VaultBufferHandlefloat4 for active breaches and VaultBufferHandleDamageControlTelemetryEntry for damage-control blackbox telemetry. Vehicle structural state can run for long sessions, so stale descriptors here would hit both visual breach upload and proof-artifact telemetry.
Solution: Store generation descriptors, resolve method-local views through TryResolveHandle, and borrow existing descriptors during allocation-locked phases. Allocation remains limited to unlocked Vault phases.
Rejected Alternatives: Migrating entire structural grid private native state was rejected for this bounded pass because it includes many owner-local job arrays and requires separate Vault route card. Keeping two handle fields because data is visual/blackbox was rejected because blackbox proof artifacts and long-lived breach visuals must be relocatable.
Scalability potential: Low devices can fail closed on breach VFX/telemetry during Vault maintenance. Middle/high/ultra retain richer breach plume/repair visuals and blackbox evidence through same BufferIDs without changing DTO layout or quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation at breach and telemetry resolve boundaries. Breach repair jobs and telemetry loops use local views and do not validate per row.
Decision 095 - Terrain seam baseline and blackbox lanes stop caching native aliases
Problem: WorldGenerativeGeologyTerrainSeamApplier.cs persisted VaultBufferHandlefloat per terrain baseline, NativeArrayfloat baseline alias in TerrainApplyState, and VaultBufferHandleTerrainSeamTelemetryEntry for seam blackbox. Terrain apply state can survive multiple reconcile/preview passes, so both handle and stored native view could point at relocated Vault memory.
Solution: Store VaultGenerationHandlefloat and VaultGenerationHandleTerrainSeamTelemetryEntry descriptors only. Resolve method-local NativeArrayT views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle before baseline copy/populate/projection and blackbox record/dump. During allocation-locked phases, borrow existing descriptors with TryGetGenerationHandle; allocate/grow only while Vault is unlocked.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping baseline NativeArrayfloat cache because terrain patching is editor/slow-path was rejected; stale native aliases are cadence-independent. Reworking MapMagic, hybrid projection, voxel blend mask upload, or terrain writeback was rejected because defect is descriptor lifetime, not terrain math. Releasing baseline buffers from TerrainApplyState.ReleaseBaseline() was rejected for this bounded pass because existing state did not own reference-count teardown and terrain baseline BufferIDs are per-terrain compatibility lanes.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing low-tier visual-only seam projection path and can fail closed on missing Vault lanes during compaction. Middle/high/ultra keep richer mask detail, blackbox evidence, and shader blend-mask upload through same BufferIDs without changing terrain payload layout or quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation descriptor validation when baseline or blackbox view is opened. Heightmap sample loops, hybrid Burst jobs, and blackbox dump loops operate on local resolved view and do not validate per sample or per entry.
Decision 096 - Submarine fluid wrapper stops carrying raw Vault pointers
Problem: SubmarineFluidDynamics.cs used generic VaultNativeBufferT wrapper holding VaultBufferHandleT, dereferenced handle.ptr in its indexer, refreshed through TryGetBufferHandle, and polled TryGetBufferGeneration. That one wrapper backed all compartment, bulkhead, hydro, blackbox, and exterior thermal lanes, so single stale pointer could contaminate whole submarine fluid route.
Solution: Replace wrapper storage with VaultGenerationHandleT plus cached length scalar. Ensure acquires/grows via GetGenerationHandleT only while Vault is unlocked and borrows via TryGetGenerationHandleT under allocation lock. Refresh, indexer access, and implicit NativeArrayT conversion open method-local views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Patching each of 28 lane fields separately was rejected because stale alias pattern was centralized in wrapper. Keeping cached NativeArrayT view inside wrapper was rejected because NativeArrayT carries native address and can go stale after relocation. Releasing all fluid buffers on disable was rejected for this pass because existing route only clears wrapper state after dependency fences and ownership/refcount policy for shared vehicle lanes needs separate teardown audit.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing fluid math LODs, visual wake/hydro Dear Lie paths, and can fail closed on Vault allocation lock. Middle/high/ultra retain richer hydro blackbox, mass-property, thermal anomaly, and custom-drag behavior through same BufferIDs without changing quality authority or DTO layout.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation when wrapper opens view. Scheduled Burst jobs still receive local NativeArrayT values and do not validate descriptors inside their loops. stale raw pointer path is removed for all submarine fluid lanes.
Decision 097 - Flora/fauna symbiosis solver moves to generation descriptors
Problem: ShinobuFloraFaunaSymbiosisSolver.cs persisted VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for all major symbiosis lanes, resolved them with .Resolve(vault), and exposed unused GetFloraRef bridge through GetElementAsRef. These buffers feed long-lived AI ecosystem jobs and can cross Vault relocation, so pointer-bearing descriptors are unacceptable.
Solution: Store VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors for all symbiosis lanes. Add local helpers for claim, borrow, and resolve so cold setup uses GetGenerationHandleT only when unlocked, allocation-locked phases borrow existing descriptors, and runtime reads/writes derive method-local NativeArrayT views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: file-wide managed abstraction was rejected because hot path needs flat descriptors and local NativeArrayT views. Keeping byref GetFloraRef bridge was rejected because ref must originate from current phase-local view. Editing simulation jobs was rejected because their inputs already accept NativeArrayT and defect was stale descriptor lifetime, not math.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing capped neighbor samples, mock fish fallback, and reduced ecosystem cadence. Middle/high/ultra retain richer scanner VFX, oxygen emitter, adherence, seed, and acoustic tap lanes through same BufferIDs without changing DTO layout or quality authority.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation validation at view-open boundaries. Flora/fish/link Burst loops still receive local arrays and do not validate per entity or per link.
Decision 098 - Thermodynamics file worker is blocked until Core exposes relocation-pinned lease
Problem: ThermodynamicsHazardGridRuntime.FileWorker.cs keeps binaryConstantsWorkerPtr and csvWorkerPtr from Vault byte lanes for background worker thread. worker can outlive Vault relocation, and current evidence does not show defrag honoring active writer metadata strongly enough to make direct worker writes safe.
Solution: Do not apply cosmetic local TryResolveHandle patch. safe migration is to parse binary constants and CSV overrides into worker-local staged scalar payloads, publish staged readiness with Volatile.Write, and apply to constants on owner/main phase after resolving VaultGenerationHandleThermodynamicsHazardConstants.
Rejected Alternatives: Letting worker resolve NativeArraybyte locally was rejected because resolution returns phase-local view, not relocation-pinned lease. Holding normal write lock was rejected because inspected relocation path does not prove it fences external worker writers. Leaving issue undocumented was rejected because this is real UAF class.
Scalability potential: Low devices benefit from avoiding worker/Vault contention and can keep cheap staged constants. Middle/high/ultra keep richer thermal hazard tuning once applied from owner phase; gameplay truth and DTO layout stay unchanged.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 avoids unsafe background writes into relocatable Vault memory. future safe patch shifts file IO parsing to worker-local memory and one owner-phase descriptor validation before writing constants.
Decision 099 - Toxic outgassing chemistry removes pointer descriptors and public constants pointer escape
Problem: ToxicOutgassingChemistryRuntime.cs persisted VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for every density, chemistry, signal, telemetry, CSV, binary, and header lane, resolved them with .Resolve(vault), exposed constants through ConstantsRef, and exposed raw pointer through TryGetConstantsPointer. These lanes are long-lived, scheduled, and blackbox-visible; stale aliases here can corrupt gas density, chemical exposure signals, and 300-frame dump.
Solution: Store VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors only. Open method-local NativeArrayT views with IDataVault.TryResolveHandle before owner mutation, job setup, telemetry commit, shader publish, CSV parse, and binary probe. Replace constants ref/pointer facade with value read/write calls and update editor tuner to edit local copy before writing it back.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping editor-only pointer was rejected because editor windows can outlive Vault relocation and still model unsafe API usage. Replacing every call with per-cell generation check was rejected because descriptor validation belongs at phase boundaries, not inside Burst loops. Moving toxicity buffers into private native arrays was rejected because atmosphere chemistry state and blackbox data are Vault-owned proof/state lanes.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain low-resolution radial fallback, continuous quality-weight cadence, and cheap nearest-density sampling. Middle devices keep full scheduled diffusion with lower source budgets. High/ultra retain trilinear sampling, richer mock flow/world sampling, shader scalar publishing, and blackbox detail through identical BufferIDs and DTO layouts.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation at each view-open boundary. 32^3 diffusion, flow, exposure, biolum, and telemetry Burst jobs still run over local NativeArrayT views with NoAlias fields and no per-cell descriptor validation. Removing public pointer escape eliminates one relocation UAF class without adding managed allocations.
Decision 100 - Ambient biota service removes cached Vault handles and read-only aliases
Problem: AmbientBiotaDirector.cs persisted six VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and three NativeArrayT.ReadOnly aliases created through IDataVault.CreateAlias. Read-only aliases still carry native addresses, and ambient service exposes them to chunk residency consumers, so relocation could leave consumers reading stale biota AUP/state memory.
Solution: Store generation descriptors for biota AUP, velocity, state, macro-hydration counter, telemetry ring, and telemetry cursor lanes. Resolve local views with IDataVault.TryResolveHandle at phase/service boundaries. Public read-only service properties now return transient .AsReadOnly() wrappers over freshly resolved local views rather than cached aliases.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached read-only aliases was rejected because read-only does not mean relocation-safe. Reworking IAmbientBiotaService contract was rejected because it is cross-domain contract; same return types can be backed by current generation-resolved views. Replacing indirect draw or macro hydration logic was rejected because defect is descriptor lifetime, not presentation math.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain survival capacity, reduced macro visual hydration, organic debris coalescing, and billboard flags. Middle/high/ultra retain larger capacities, indirect draw payloads, visual overkill flags, and blackbox telemetry through same BufferIDs and DTO layouts.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation when opening biota/counter/telemetry views. Drift, spawn, hydration, dehydration, and residency loops still iterate local arrays without per-row descriptor validation. Removing CreateAlias fields eliminates three persistent native-address aliases.
Decision 101 - Cartography handle bundle moves to generation descriptors
Problem: CartographyGridJobs.cs defined CartographyVaultHandles with VaultBufferHandleT fields, allocated them through GetBufferHandle, borrowed through TryGetBufferHandle, and opened all cartography views through .Resolve(vault). PlayerExplorationTracker persists this bundle, so stale descriptors could hit discovery words, telemetry, tuning, scanner profiles, upload payloads, and rollback snapshots.
Solution: Replace every field in CartographyVaultHandles with VaultGenerationHandleT. Unlocked acquisition now uses GetGenerationHandleT, allocation-locked acquisition uses TryGetGenerationHandleT, and TryResolveViews opens all buffers through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting PlayerExplorationTracker was rejected because consumer already depends on bundle API and stale pointer route is centralized inside CartographyVault. Adding per-word descriptor checks was rejected because discovery, RLE, and upload jobs must remain dense data-local loops.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain sparse reveal cadence, packed R8 upload, and surface mask approximations. Middle/high/ultra retain larger visible point budgets, scanner profile tuning, mock exploration data, RLE/debug lanes, and rollback snapshots through same BufferIDs and DTO layouts.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation once per cartography view binding. Discovery, sonar, POI injection, RLE, upload, telemetry, and rollback Burst jobs continue to operate on local arrays without descriptor checks inside word/voxel loops.
Decision 102 - Ecosystem balancer removes pointer descriptors from swarm truth lanes
Problem: ShinobuEcosystemBalancer.cs persisted VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for ambient entity/AUP rows, boid states, frame snapshots, sector/tuning/counter/telemetry/debug lanes, render matrices/custom data/indirect args, spatial hash buffers, CSV scratch, legacy scratch, and species profiles. It resolved them through .Resolve(vault) and kept unused GetAmbientEntityRef bridge over GetElementAsRef, leaving primary swarm simulation exposed to stale native addresses after Vault relocation.
Solution: Store VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors only. Add ClaimVaultHandle and TryOpenVaultView so allocation uses GetGenerationHandleT only when Vault is unlocked, locked phases borrow existing descriptors through TryGetGenerationHandleT, and every owner phase derives method-local NativeArrayT views with IDataVault.TryResolveHandle.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting flocking, spatial hash, macro biomass, HZB/GPU upload, or predator logic was rejected because defect is pointer lifetime, not ecosystem math. Keeping static byref helper was rejected because any ref must originate from current local view, not persisted pointer handle. Adding per-boid descriptor checks was rejected because boid loops must remain vectorizable dense array work.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep continuous quality-weight budget collapse, update stride, reduced neighbor samples, and GPU/indirect fail-closed behavior. Middle/high/ultra retain richer flocking samples, debug cells, indirect procedural draw payloads, CSV-authored species profiles, and blackbox telemetry through same BufferIDs without changing gameplay authority, DTO layout, shader ABI, or save identity.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation only at schedule, CSV, initial-population, GPU-upload, and telemetry boundaries. local-shift, spatial hash, flocking, render payload, macro biomass, indirect args, and telemetry count jobs still consume local arrays without per-row descriptor validation or managed allocation.
Decision 103 - Ecosystem population governor borrows external lanes and releases owned descriptors
Problem: EcosystemPopulationBalancer.cs persisted eight VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and resolved them through .Resolve(vault). Six lanes are owned population buffers, while EntityAUPs and EntityFlags are external truth lanes; treating both as pointer handles risks stale aliases and treating both as owned would violate authority boundaries.
Solution: Convert all eight descriptors to VaultGenerationHandleT. Owned buffers EcosystemPopulationCoefficients, EcosystemPopulationSectorState, EcosystemPopulationCullEvents, EcosystemPopulationTelemetryRing, EcosystemPopulationFreeRing, and EcosystemPopulationCounters use GetGenerationHandleT only when allocation is legal and are exact-released on teardown/DataVault rebind. External EntityAUPs and EntityFlags are borrowed through TryGetGenerationHandleT and resolved only into method-local views.
Rejected Alternatives: Owner-wide ReleaseOwnerBuffers(SystemID.AIEcology) was rejected because SystemID.AIEcology is shared by other ecology runtimes. Rewriting population math or death SignalBus payloads was rejected because unsafe route was Vault descriptor lifetime, not bounded Lotka-Volterra job.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep same cold-tick population governor, free-ring reuse, and tier flee-down requests. Middle/high/ultra keep richer sector/cull telemetry and SignalBus death proof through same DTO layouts; GlobalQualityWeight, save identity, and entity truth ownership are unchanged.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays generation validation at cold setup, sector-state rebuild, job schedule, telemetry write, and signal publish boundaries. Burst job still receives local NativeArrayT values and does not validate descriptors per entity or per sector.
Decision 104 - Apex brain vault bundle moves to pointer-free descriptors
Problem: ShinobuApexBrainVault.cs persisted public bundle of fifteen VaultBufferHandleT descriptors, opened all cognition lanes through .Resolve(vault), and exposed GetStateAsRef over GetElementAsRef. bundle is reused by editor tooling and scheduled cognition jobs, so stale descriptors could corrupt apex state, signals, tuning, CSV scratch, or blackbox telemetry after Vault relocation.
Solution: Convert ApexBrainVaultHandles to VaultGenerationHandleT, acquire unlocked lanes through GetGenerationHandleT, borrow locked lanes through TryGetGenerationHandleT, and bind ApexBrainVaultBuffers through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle. Replace byref accessor with value-copy TryReadState and TryWriteState. Add ReleaseOwnedHandles for exact apex BufferIDs.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping public byref helper was rejected because refs can escape phase-local view. Rewriting cognition scoring, signal queues, CSV parser, or dump format was rejected because those paths already consume local arrays; defect was handle lifetime. Owner-wide release was rejected because SystemID.AICognition is shared by adjacent cognition vaults.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep 5 Hz quality-gated cognition cadence and emergency mock data. Middle/high/ultra retain richer acoustic taps, ambush nodes, signal queues, visual-overkill tuning, CSV hot reload, and 300-frame dumps through same BufferIDs and DTO layouts.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation once per bundle view binding. apex cognition Burst job still receives local arrays with NoAlias fields and does not validate descriptors per leviathan, acoustic tap, or influence node.
Decision 105 - Trade marauder runtime removes pointer descriptors from economy lanes
Problem: TradeMarauderRuntime.cs persisted twenty-three VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for marauder state, inventories, economy weights, sector data, scratch, telemetry, tuning, faction standing, mock inventory, signal scratch, loot, sector hash, CSV scratch, counters, route plans, and visual proxy lanes. It resolved those descriptors with .Resolve(vault) from FrostTick, editor, CSV, reputation, and post-job publish paths, leaving economy proof/state lanes exposed to stale native addresses after Vault relocation.
Solution: Replace every trade marauder lane field with VaultGenerationHandleT. Cold setup now validates existing descriptors with TryGetGenerationHandleT/TryResolveHandle, allocates with GetGenerationHandleT only while Vault is unlocked, and opens method-local NativeArrayT views through TryOpenVaultView. Non-deferred teardown and DataVault rebind release exact owner descriptors through ReleaseBuffer(in handle).
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting pathfinding, offscreen theft, trade negotiation, acoustic ping publication, or visual proxy hydration was rejected because those jobs already consume local arrays and defect was handle lifetime. Forcing JobHandle.Complete() during OnDisable was rejected because dispatcher owns completion windows and hidden teardown stalls violate phase discipline. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact BufferID release is safer than broad owner release under parallel-agent edits.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous GlobalQualityWeight collapse of item evaluation, route solves, and iteration budget. Middle devices keep normal trade simulation with bounded signal scratch. High/ultra keep richer route planning, acoustic signatures, telemetry, and visual proxy payloads through same DTO layouts and BufferIDs.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one generation validation per opened lane at setup/FrostTick/editor/CSV/publish boundaries. node loops, inventory loops, theft negotiation, visual hydration, acoustic signature, and telemetry jobs still operate on local NativeArrayT values with no per-node descriptor validation or managed allocation.
Decision 106 - Alpha Leviathan cognition vault removes pointer descriptors
Problem: AlphaLeviathanCognitionVault.cs persisted public AlphaLeviathanVaultHandles bundle made of VaultBufferHandleT rows and resolved them through .Resolve(vault). bridge also exposed raw TryAcquireBuffers path over GetBufferT/TryGetBufferT, allowing callers to cache native views without current generation proof.
Solution: Convert five Alpha cognition lanes to VaultGenerationHandleT and bind views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle at method boundaries only. TryAcquireBuffers now acquires descriptors first and then resolves transient views, so even compatibility callers pass through generation route. ReleaseOwnedHandles releases only exact five owner descriptors.
Rejected Alternatives: Rewriting tangent-orbit stalking, SDF contour collapse, phase byte compatibility, or blackbox binary dump was rejected because those systems already operate on local arrays and defect was descriptor lifetime. Keeping direct GetBufferT compatibility was rejected because it preserved raw-view cache path. Owner-wide release was rejected because SystemID.AICognition is shared by apex cognition and other predator cognition lanes.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep survival radial fallback, 5 Hz-ish quality-pressure cadence, and cheap tangent-orbit steering. Middle devices keep normal fog-ring stalking and telemetry. High/ultra keep SDF contour weight, visual overkill shader scalars in steering output, richer wake/silt/biolum payloads, and full 300-frame blackbox rows through identical DTO layouts.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays five descriptor validations at acquire/resolve boundaries. Burst stalk job still receives local NativeArrayT values and no per-slot descriptor check; AlphaLeviathanCognitionState=192, AlphaLeviathanSensoryStimulus=176, AlphaLeviathanSteeringOutput=128, and telemetry =64 remain aligned and unchanged.
Decision 107 - Data Archaeology removes pointer descriptors and binary scanner tier gate
Problem: DataArchaeologyRuntime.cs persisted VaultBufferHandleT descriptors for discovery word, notification, and telemetry lanes, resolved them through .Resolve(vault), and repeatedly polled GlobalRegistry.DataVault from private resolver paths. same file also used GlobalRegistry.ScalabilityTier/HectonQualityTier to skip scanner shader points outright on low tiers.

Allocation/grow routes are explicitly named TryOpenOrAcquire so read-style accessors do not hide mutation. Safe teardown/rebind releases exact three owner descriptors. Scanner presentation now uses HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight with smoothstep progress scale.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping TryResolve methods that allocate was rejected because read accessors must be pure by doctrine. Owner-wide release was rejected because SystemID.GameplayTools is shared. Low-tier scanner early return was rejected because binary quality gates create visible feature popping and violate continuous scalability.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep scanner feedback as dim/cheap shader scalar rather than hard-off feature. Middle devices get partial progress visibility. High/ultra retain full scanner shader progress and existing notification/telemetry fidelity through unchanged BufferIDs and DTO layouts.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation at setup, lore sync, notification enqueue/dequeue, telemetry commit, and blackbox dump boundaries. Discovery bit loops and telemetry row writes still use local NativeArrayT views with no per-row descriptor validation; removing binary tier gate avoids branchy presentation policy tied to stale enum state.
Decision 108 - Base atmosphere evicts cached native views and releases descriptors after job fences
Problem: BaseAtmosphereEngine.cs persisted four VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and also cached four Vault-backed NativeArrayT views as fields. Front/back compartment arrays are swapped after cold tick job, so stale native views here could survive Vault relocation or DataVault replacement. original teardown only cleared aliases and descriptors.
Solution: Store only VaultGenerationHandleT descriptors for front/back compartment lanes, CO2 byte lane, and blackbox telemetry. Resolve method-local native views at setup, seed, schedule, mutation, and blackbox boundaries. Swap front/back descriptors after job completes. Public read routes use IDataVault.TryReadHandle; mutation/schedule routes use IDataVault.TryResolveHandle. Exact owner release is immediate when no job is active and deferred through captured generation descriptors when cold tick job fence is still pending.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping cached NativeArrayT fields was rejected because they are raw address aliases even without explicit pointers. Forcing JobHandle.Complete() on teardown was rejected because dispatcher-owned completion windows must remain non-blocking. Owner-wide release was rejected because exact BufferID release is sufficient and safer under shared SystemID.HabitatAtmosphere.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous cold-tick cadence, reduced solve budget, Dalton pressure fake, and byte CO2 scrub lane. Middle/high/ultra keep richer compartment counts, visual-overkill flags, and 300-frame telemetry through same BufferIDs and DTO layouts.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays descriptor validation at setup, schedule, seed, compartment mutation, and blackbox write boundaries. cold tick job still receives local contiguous arrays and no per-compartment descriptor validation; deferred release avoids teardown main-thread stall.
Decision 109 - Surface weather output lane moves to generation descriptor
Problem: HectonSurfaceWeatherDirector.cs kept VaultBufferHandleSurfaceWeatherJobOutput, resolved it with .Resolve(vault) for seed/schedule/complete, and pulled GlobalRegistry.DataVault from output resolver. Disposal also used forceComplete: true, creating hidden teardown stall.

Cache IDataVault during lifecycle setup, acquire output lane through GetGenerationHandleT, and open method-local output views through IDataVault.TryResolveHandle. Disposal now attempts non-forced completion and releases exact descriptor only when fence permits it.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping hot GlobalRegistry.DataVault lookup in TryResolveWeatherJobOutput was rejected because registry is cold DI. Keeping forceComplete: true was rejected because weather output disposal must not seize dispatcher completion window. Rewriting weather math job or AUP-safe origin changes was rejected because unsafe route was output lane descriptor.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep screen-space rain shedding and cheap scalar weather output. Middle/high/ultra retain richer storm/lightning/squall math through same single output DTO and existing continuous weather quality decisions.
Hardware Impact: i3/MX350 pays one descriptor validation at weather output seed/schedule/complete boundaries. Burst job still writes one-element NativeSliceSurfaceWeatherJobOutput with no per-parameter descriptor validation, and teardown no longer forces main-thread wait.
Decision 110 - Cable debug gizmo borrows generation descriptors only
Problem: CablePhysicsDebugGizmo132.cs used TryGetBufferHandle and .Resolve(vault) to draw solver-owned cable nodes and constraints. Even though this is diagnostic code, it kept obsolete pointer-bearing descriptor route alive.

Decision 111 - Cable solver fallback surface removes pointer descriptors
Problem: CablePhysicsSolver132.cs still used GetBufferHandle(...).Resolve(...) for mock bootstrap lanes, mock view binding, telemetry sampling, and blackbox dump reads. Shinobu132CablePhysicsTunerWindow.cs also wrote tuning/material lanes through same legacy pointer descriptor API.

Rejected Alternatives: Cleaning only editor window was rejected because unsafe pointer route would remain in runtime helper surface. Decision 136 - Voxel surface nets facade and byref helpers use generation descriptors
Problem: VoxelSurfaceNetsVault.cs exposed VaultBufferHandleT in its public handle facade, allocated with GetBufferHandleT, borrowed with TryGetBufferHandleT, resolved eighteen lanes through handles.X.Resolve(vault), and retained GetElementAsRef / GetElementAsReadOnlyRef helpers for chunk meshing state. byref helpers were explicit stale pointer bridge.

Replace state byref helpers with method-local state view resolution, explicit bounds checks, and UnsafeUtility.ArrayElementAsRef derived from resolved local view.

Keeping handle GetElementAsRef was rejected because it hides pointer resolution behind legacy handle method. Rewriting meshing jobs was rejected because they already consume local arrays, carry Burst compile directives, and use NoAlias; defect was facade storage and byref access.

Decision 137 - Vehicle damage runtime and contract open local Vault views before pointer use
Problem: VehicleComponentDamageRuntime.cs persisted eleven VaultBufferHandleT descriptors, allocated through GetBufferHandleT, borrowed kinematic config through TryGetBufferHandleT, and used .Resolve, .ResolvePointer, GetElementAsRef, GetElementAsReadOnlyRef, and ResolveBuffer in fixed tick, initialization, CSV reload, editor snapshots, gizmos, root-pose reads, and blackbox dump paths. Change VehicleDamageAccess.GetCellRef to accept in VaultGenerationHandleVehicleGridCellDTO and resolve local view before returning ref.

Keeping legacy byref helpers for editor/contract convenience was rejected because editor windows, gizmos, and contract helpers are long-lived enough to survive Vault relocation. Converting every existing TryLockBuffer call to newer descriptor writer-fence API was deferred because this loop targeted stale handle storage and hidden pointer resolution without expanding lock lifecycle surface.

Middle/high/ultra retain full grid damage mapping, system scalar outputs, telemetry, CSV layout authoring, and blackbox dumps without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or VehiclesPhysics authority.

Problem: AbyssalThermodynamicsSolver.cs persisted sixteen VaultBufferHandleT descriptors and used ResolvePointer, .Resolve, handle .IsCreated, and GetBufferHandleT across tick scheduling, source mutation, sample jobs, boot initialization, CSV profile load, telemetry reads, GPU upload, blackbox dump, and editor gizmos.

Decision 139 - Thermodynamics hazard grid removes stale handles and worker-retained Vault pointers
Problem: ThermodynamicsHazardGridRuntime.cs persisted nineteen VaultBufferHandleT lanes, resolved them through legacy handle APIs, exposed raw constants pointer to ThermodynamicsTunerWindow, and let ThermodynamicsHazardGridRuntime.FileWorker.cs retain Vault byte pointers on background thread. That combination can survive Vault relocation and makes editor/readback accessors mutate state through hidden routes.

Move mirror-grid mutation into explicit PrepareVaultGridReadback() and keep TryGetVaultGridReadback(...) read-only. Convert config worker to cold byte staging arrays; pin only during file reads, then copy into Vault byte lanes on main owner phase under SystemID.Thermodynamics writer fences before parsing constants.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping background thread on Vault pointers was rejected because MMF/disk IO can overlap relocation windows. Moving all config IO to main thread was rejected because it would trade pointer safety for visible frame hitches. Keeping raw editor constants pointer was rejected because editor windows are long-lived consumers and can outlive Vault relocation. Rewriting deterministic Burst job pointer ABI was rejected because unsafe retention defect was descriptor storage and hidden resolution, not scheduled job inputs derived immediately before schedule.
Scalability potential: Low devices retain continuous lower-resolution hazard grids, lower update pressure, editor-only CSV suppression in player builds, shader heat texture upload, and emergency mock hazards. Middle/high/ultra retain high-resolution diffusion, explicit Vault mirror visualization, updraft signals, telemetry, CSV/binary tuning, and GPU thermal presentation without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or Thermodynamics authority.

Decision 140 - Fabrication assembler opens local descriptor views and keeps reads pure
Problem: FabricationAssemblerRuntime.cs persisted eight VaultBufferHandleT descriptors, allocated through GetBufferHandleT, resolved all lanes through handle.Resolve(vault), and let TryReadSnapshot, editor stats/debug, and tuning reads call EnsureVaultState(). That meant read accessors could allocate/grow Vault buffers and stale pointer-bearing descriptors could survive relocation before fabrication progress jobs, signal emission, CSV import, telemetry, and GPU upload paths.
Solution: Replace every persisted fabrication lane with VaultGenerationHandleT. Owned lanes allocate through GetGenerationHandleT, borrowed scalability state uses TryGetGenerationHandleT, and all lane views open through method-local IDataVault.TryResolveHandle or TryReadHandle helpers. Read accessors now require runtime to already be initialized and only use read-handle views. Tuning writes use SystemID.CoreDiagnostics writer fence; CSV ingestion opens scratch, timing lookup, and tuning version lanes under bounded writer fences released in finally.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping legacy handles because bridge ignores cached pointers was rejected because runtime would still normalize pointer-era descriptor storage. Keeping read accessors on EnsureVaultState() was rejected because read APIs must not allocate, publish, or mutate state. Rewriting existing Burst job structs was rejected because they already consume local NativeArrayT views, carry deterministic Burst flags, and mark non-overlapping arrays with NoAlias; unsafe defect was persistent descriptor storage and hidden resolution.
Scalability potential: Low devices keep existing continuous quality curve: lower GPU upload count, longer upload stride, low-tier signal capacity, and mock fabrication fallback. Middle/high/ultra retain full shader payload upload, richer fabrication tick/completion signals, CSV timing authoring, telemetry, and visual-overkill assembly edge glow without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or Construction authority.

Rejected Alternatives: Leaving GetBufferT because facade is small was rejected because migration target is route, not only long-lived storage. Storing generation handles in RetinalAdaptationVaultBuffers was rejected because callers consume arrays and facade should not retain descriptors across owner phases. Expanding into PredatorCognitionDomain.cs was rejected for this loop because that monolith contains broad VaultArrayT debt across many cognition lanes and requires separate blast-radius pass.

Middle/high/ultra retain current retinal glare, blindness publication, and 300-frame telemetry behavior without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or AI cognition authority. cheap retinal facade remains data route; visual overkill still comes from downstream shader/cognition consumers, not extra facade math.

Problem: Arm64AlignmentFaultGizmo.cs and MacroEcosystemHeatmapGizmo.cs used GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated from ordinary editor gizmo drawing. MacroEcosystemHeatmapGizmo.cs also read sector, coordinate, and tuning lanes through direct TryGetBufferT calls.

Adding new macro heatmap cached handles was rejected because gizmos are read-only diagnostics and should not own ecosystem memory. Touching macro ecosystem runtime ownership was rejected because this pass only fixes editor reader route.

Problem: CraftingRuntimeSmokeTester.cs created fallback GlobalDataVault through GlobalDataVault.Create when batch mode had no latest-created Vault, but fabrication runtime now resolves only GlobalRegistry.DataVault. latest-only Vault would leave FabricationAssemblerRuntime.EnsureRuntime() without authoritative registry Vault and break fallback mock data generator expected by CI.

Creating Vault outside batch mode was rejected because it would hide missing bootstrap order in interactive/runtime contexts. Keeping smoke tester as-is was rejected because it would silently fail mock generator after descriptor migration.
Scalability potential: Low devices and CI keep deterministic mock fabrication setup without touching gameplay truth. Middle/high/ultra retain same mock job shape, shader payload route, telemetry shape, and continuous fabrication quality behavior once registered Vault exists.

Problem: CacheBTreeTopologyXRayWindow.cs still used GlobalDataVault.TryGetLatestCreated for editor tuning and telemetry reads, and Cache B-Tree cold helper surface in H8StaticDataContracts.cs still allocated telemetry/tuning lanes through direct GetBufferT. direct routes bypassed descriptor freshness proof and kept ordinary diagnostics tied to latest-created fallback.

Problem: LeviathanTerrainIkJobs.cs opened segment, bone, constraint, collider, telemetry, optional SDF, and optional heightmap lanes through direct GetBufferT calls. DTO layouts and deterministic terrain IK job were already explicit, but cold resolver still bypassed generation freshness proof.

Middle/high/ultra retain full voxel traversal, inventory rules, and WFC persistence behavior without changing DTO layout, BufferIDs, save identity, or gameplay authority.

Rationale_SHINOBU_203.md
SHINOBU203 Rationale
Date: 2026-05-20
Status: PENDING VERIFICATION
Domain: Iterative solver convergence, Jacobi/SOR stability, residual telemetry.
Decision 00: Startup Scope
Problem: prompt spans 20 tasks across power, thermal, telemetry, editor tooling, CSV ingestion, and architecture audit. Directly implementing broad cross-domain systems without source archaeology would risk fake interfaces and compile breakage.
Solution: Start with local archaeology in Assets/Project/Scripts/Habitat/ and Assets/Project/Scripts/Environment/, then implement only against existing solver/data surfaces. DOD pattern: source-first, owner-local, dispatcher phase-bound, zero-GC hot path.
Rejected Alternatives: Creating new global solver framework before discovering actual classes; adding DataVault surfaces without route-card proof; changing public contracts blindly.
Scalability potential: Low uses fewer sampled residual cells and higher tolerance; Middle keeps conservative SOR; High uses stricter tolerance; Ultra uses dense telemetry and visual diagnostics without bloating gameplay truth.
Hardware Impact: Avoiding fake global allocations prevents compile walls and avoids persistent native memory debt on i3/MX350. Estimated gain pending source scan.
Decision 01: Convergence Surface Placement
Problem: prompt names Habitat/Environment, but source scan found active Jacobi residual path in Assets/Project/Scripts/Power/SubmarineOsThermalGridRuntime.cs; Habitat deformation and Environment scans did not expose comparable Jacobi loop.
Solution: Install convergence state inside existing thermal power-grid DataVault surface. DOD pattern: owner-local hot path, no new global manager, no invented dependency.
Rejected Alternatives: Adding standalone solver registry, editing unrelated Habitat deformation jobs, or waiting for new solver interface from another agent.
Scalability potential: Low samples every eighth node with loose tolerance; Middle samples denser; High/Ultra drive tolerance down and SOR up through continuous GlobalQualityWeight.
Hardware Impact: One 16-byte state buffer plus 512-float residual buffer. Avoids per-node atomics in parallel pass. Estimated low-end save versus full residual scan inside every node pass: 8-18 microseconds at 512 nodes on i3/MX350.
Decision 02: SOR And Residual Reduction
Problem: Fixed Jacobi passes could keep running after convergence and could also hide residual growth until final telemetry, allowing NaN avalanches to propagate through double buffer.
Solution: Schedule PowerGridRelaxationJob followed by ConvergenceResidualReductionJob per pass. parallel job writes sampled residuals only; scalar reduction decides convergence, damping, or divergence.
Rejected Alternatives: Atomic max inside IJobParallelFor; managed callbacks between passes; immediate job completion on CPU.
Scalability potential: Low runs omega 1.0 and sparse residual mask; Middle gradually increases omega; High/Ultra run stricter tolerance and denser sampling.
Hardware Impact: Removes atomic contention and early-converged later passes copy buffers instead of recomputing neighbors. Estimated low-end save after convergence: 12-40 microseconds per solve at 512 nodes and 6-degree CSR.
Decision 03: Divergence And NaN Containment
Problem: Non-finite potentials or runaway overshoot can spread through neighbor reads in next Jacobi pass.
Solution: Clamp non-finite/runaway candidates back to source potential, stamp FaultDivergent, and promote solver-level NonFinite/Divergent flags into telemetry counters and black-box dump triggers.
Rejected Alternatives: Letting math.saturate hide non-finite origin; throwing exceptions inside Burst; logging strings from jobs.
Scalability potential: All tiers use same containment path; higher tiers spend saved cycles on tighter residual targets, not different correctness.
Hardware Impact: Branch is cold unless solver destabilizes. Estimated normal-frame cost below 1 microsecond; failure-frame dump is cold post-simulation.
Decision 04: Telemetry And Rollback Boundary
Problem: Convergence values are diagnostics and solver-control state, not gameplay truth. Hashing them would destabilize rollback/netcode state.
Solution: Keep telemetry fields (SolverOmega, TargetTolerance, JacobiResidual) in 300-frame black-box snapshot but leave HashNode unchanged.
Rejected Alternatives: Include omega/residual in state hash; emit debug logs only; allocate managed telemetry rows.
Scalability potential: Low still records enough state for crash forensics; Ultra receives dense residual telemetry through same fixed-size ring.
Hardware Impact: Reuses existing 64-byte telemetry entry by replacing pads. No new per-frame managed allocation.
Decision 05: Base Power Graph SOR Parity
Problem: LogisticsNetworkGraph contained two additional Jacobi loops for base power distribution. One read HomeostasisBrain.GlobalQualityWeight inside job and both used fixed passes with no residual stop.
Solution: Pass GlobalQualityWeight into EvaluateGraphJob, apply same continuous tolerance/omega helpers, break on convergence, and damp omega when residual grows. Added PowerGridNodeFlags.Divergent bit for local containment.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving logistics on fixed Jacobi because thermal grid was fixed; routing logistics through thermal DataVault; adding managed convergence services.
Scalability potential: Low keeps Jacobi-like omega 1.0 and loose tolerance; Middle/High/Ultra use progressively higher SOR and stricter residual targets through shared curve.
Hardware Impact: Stops repeated CSR traversal after convergence. Estimated low-end save: 6-24 microseconds per logistics solve window depending on node count and edge degree.
Decision 06: Thermal Voxel SOR Containment
Problem: HeatDiffusionSolverJob still performed naive Jacobi averaging and only reported NaN after telemetry observed bad cell.
Solution: Add continuous omega/tolerance helpers to AbyssalThermalMath, apply one SOR relaxation per scheduled HeatDiffusionSolverJob pass, write residuals into padded worker slots, and flag CellFlagDivergent when candidate explodes. Divergent thermal dumps now also write Docs/AgentLogs/DumpSHINOBU203.bin.
Rejected Alternatives: Coupling thermodynamics to power-grid convergence DTO; introducing managed debug events; waiting for full cross-system dispatcher ownership.
Scalability potential: Low accepts up to 0.5 Celsius residual; Middle shrinks tolerance; High/Ultra approach 0.001 Celsius while using stronger omega.
Hardware Impact: Dispatcher-level convergence stops later scheduled passes after residual tolerance is met. Estimated low-end save: 10-55 microseconds on 16-32 cubed active grids depending on source density.
Decision 07: Audit Tooling And Live Debug Surface
Problem: project needed proof that blind iteration sites were found, plus editor path to inspect convergence without managed runtime logging.
Solution: Added Tools/JacobiOverheadScanner.ps1, generated Docs/Reports/MATHOPTIMIZATIONREPORT.json, added SolverConvergenceXRayWindow, and extended thermal grid gizmo to draw FaultDivergent nodes. ShinobuLogisticsRouter now applies SOR/tolerance guards inside each scheduled pass so its remaining dispatcher loop is not blind work.
Rejected Alternatives: Manual-only report; runtime UI; spawning debug GameObjects; using log strings from Burst jobs.
Scalability potential: Low shows sparse residual stability and looser tolerance; Ultra uses same telemetry with stricter tolerance and stronger omega, visible through same x-ray window.
Hardware Impact: Editor-only managed arrays do not touch runtime. Router residual copy-forward removes repeated math for stable nodes. Estimated low-end save: 4-14 microseconds per router solve at 1000 nodes.
Decision 08: Cold Relaxation Profile Ingestion
Problem: Tuning omega and residual tolerances through managed config parsing would violate hot-path rules if it leaked into runtime.
Solution: Reused existing ReadOnlySpanbyte CSV parser pattern and added ParseRelaxationProfilesCsv for cold application of JacobiTolerance, BaseOmegaFactor, and ToleranceMultiplier into 64-byte tuning DTO.
Rejected Alternatives: float.Parse, string splitting, ScriptableObject runtime lookups, or storing profile names in managed dictionaries.
Scalability potential: Low-end profiles can inflate tolerance multiplier and damp omega; Ultra profiles can reduce tolerance and keep omega near upper safe band without new branches.
Hardware Impact: Cold boot only. Runtime cost is two extra floats read from tuning DTO; no heap allocation.
Decision 09: Abyssal Thermal Pass-Wide Residual State
Problem: abyssal thermal solver still had outer ping-pong loop over JacobiIterations; residual guard inside cell job could stop only individual cell, not grid pass chain. That left redundant full-grid passes and delayed divergent-grid recognition.
Solution: Added Vault-backed ThermalSolverConvergenceStateDTO1 and residual samples with local BufferIDs 70052 and 70053, explicit layout validation, stochastic residual masking, and ThermalSolverResidualReductionJob after every diffusion pass. residual lane is now ThermalResidualSlot64128 so pass-wide reduction does not scan voxel grid. Terminal convergence makes later passes copy-forward through same ping-pong buffers.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing Core BufferID enum during batch polish pass, forcing main-thread Complete() after each pass, or trusting comment-local guard. Local numeric IDs are recorded in binary ledger to avoid silent ownership.
Scalability potential: Low uses mask 0x7, tolerance 0.5C, and omega 1.0; Middle shrinks tolerance and densifies sampling; High/Ultra sample every cell and drive omega toward 1.62 for visual thermal richness without binary switching.
Hardware Impact: Low-end voxel pass avoids repeated 32^3 solves after tolerance; estimated 12-35 microseconds saved on i3/MX350 when heat field is near equilibrium.
Decision 10: Logistics Pressure NaN Quarantine
Problem: LogisticsFlowSolverJob could write float.NaN to WritePressure on pressure fault. That value could propagate into later pressure reads before finalize sanitized lane.
Solution: Faulted pressure now freezes at previousPressure, stamps LogisticsStateFlags.Divergent, and final telemetry promotes SolverDivergent; no pressure lane receives NaN or Infinity.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving NaN as sentinel; adding managed log; expanding signal surface for single owner-local fault.
Scalability potential: All quality levels keep same containment rule; lower quality simply tolerates larger residuals and earlier pass exits.
Hardware Impact: One cold branch on fault path. Normal-frame cost is below measurable noise; failure containment prevents cascade work and black-box ambiguity.
Decision 11: Ledger Closure And Static Gate Discipline
Problem: Local numeric BufferID casts for SHINOBU203 convergence lanes would become silent ownership debt if not recorded in binary integration ledger. ultra-polish mandate also required proof that no stale NaN sentinels or blind pass loops remained in touched solver surfaces.
Solution: Recorded power lanes 731078/731079 and abyssal lanes 70052/70053 in Docs/ARCHITECTURE/BINARYPAYLOADINTEGRATIONLEDGER.md, updated Docs/ARCHITECTURE/ABYSSALTHERMODYNAMICSSOLVER.md, appended file-backed SELFAUDIT to LOGSHINOBU203.md, and reran static gates. DOD pattern: file-backed authority, static proof before compile, no Core enum churn during multi-agent batch.
Rejected Alternatives: Editing Core BufferID enum during convergence-polish pass; leaving BufferID casts undocumented; launching dotnet build while CPU load was at 100%; relying on chat-only audit text; keeping legacy HectonQualityTier switch for adaptive solver windows.
Scalability potential: Low, middle, high, and ultra tiers now share same documented continuous convergence curve: sparse residual masks and loose tolerance at low pressure; dense residual sampling, wider adaptive solve windows, and tighter omega/tolerance at high quality. No binary low/high switch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: Documentation has no runtime cost. Static gates prevent reintroduction of NaN sentinels and full residual scans; expected low-end protection remains 12-35 us for near-equilibrium thermal voxels and 8-18 us for sparse residual validation on smaller power grids.
Decision 12: Consecutive Max-Iteration Fault Gate
Problem: solver reduction jobs set MaxIterations, but previous telemetry/dump logic only reacted to NaN/divergence. That failed Task 15 requirement to dump 300-frame ring after five consecutive frames stuck at iteration cap.
Solution: Power telemetry now increments CounterMaxIterationStreak and raises SubmarineThermalGridFaultFlags.MaxIterations only after five residual-over-tolerance capped frames. Abyssal thermal telemetry raises TelemetryFlagMaxIterations; AbyssalThermodynamicsSolver verifies last five telemetry-ring frames before dumping unless NaN/divergence demands immediate dump.
Rejected Alternatives: Dumping on first capped frame; treating max-iteration as divergence immediately; using managed log strings or exceptions; adding new Core BufferID for one scalar streak during multi-agent polish pass.
Scalability potential: Low quality legitimately accepts looser tolerance and fewer passes, so gate waits for five consecutive capped frames. High/Ultra still get strict residual proof and dump if solver cannot satisfy tight target repeatedly.
Hardware Impact: One scalar counter update per telemetry frame. Cost is below 1 microsecond; forensic value is high because endurance failures now preserve pre-fault convergence trail.
Decision 13: Thread-Slot Residual Map-Reduce
Problem: residual path was atomics-free, but it still used large grid-sized residual sample lane and reduction over sampled grid indices. That did not satisfy stricter Task 07 wording requiring small per-worker map-reduce surface.
Solution: Added NativeSetThreadIndex to power and abyssal thermal primary solver jobs. Each worker writes its maximum sampled residual into one of 128 pre-cleared residual slots. reduction jobs scan those slots only, then update convergence, omega dampening, max-iteration, and divergence flags.
Rejected Alternatives: Interlocked.Max; full per-cell residual reduction; relying on large residual arrays as proof; adding unmanaged atomics that would block Burst vectorization.
Scalability potential: Low still samples sparse residuals through bitmask; High/Ultra sample densely. In every tier, global reduction cost is bounded by 128 slots instead of grid size.
Hardware Impact: Reduces residual reduction bandwidth from up to 32768 thermal floats to 128 floats per pass. Expected low-end gain is 5-20 microseconds on thermal voxel passes when solver is hot and cache bandwidth is contested.
Decision 14: Renderer Registry Poll Removal
Problem: touched logistics router diff routed pipe flow visuals through GlobalRegistry.TryGet inside PublishFlowVisuals, which is visual-sync path and violates cold-bootstrap registry boundary.
Solution: Cache IConnectionSplineBatchRendererService during EnsureInitialized() and use cached interface in PublishFlowVisuals. If unavailable at cold boot, visual publish path silently skips pipe flow updates rather than polling global service every frame.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping per-frame registry lookup; restoring direct static renderer call; adding new signal lane for single visual consumer.
Scalability potential: All tiers avoid registry traffic in visual publication. Low-tier devices save branch and lookup; high-tier devices keep same visual route if renderer exists at initialization.
Hardware Impact: Small but deterministic. Removes per-frame service lookup and keeps convergence patch inside global-authority rules.
Decision 15: Cache-Line Padded Residual Slots
Problem: worker-slot residual map-reduce removed atomics, but first implementation stored worker maxima in adjacent float slots. That keeps SIMD clean but lets multiple job workers write to same 64-byte cache line, causing MESI invalidation under contention.
Solution: Replace residual lanes with explicit 64-byte DTOs: SolverResidualSlot64128 for power and ThermalResidualSlot64128 for abyssal thermal. Each slot stores MaxResidualFloat at offset 0, FaultFlags at offset 4, and 56 bytes of manual padding. Init, clear, and reduction now schedule over 128 rows, not node/voxel count; each parallel writer owns full cache line.
Rejected Alternatives: Increasing float stride manually; clamping to fewer worker slots; using atomics; leaving dense float lanes because they passed no-Interlocked check.
Scalability potential: Low quality still uses sparse deterministic residual masks; high/ultra still sample densely. memory lane is fixed-size and quality-neutral, so device tier changes do not alter ABI or introduce binary switches.
Hardware Impact: Removes residual-slot false sharing during hot solver passes. Expected low-end protection: 3-12 microseconds in contested power/thermal solver frames on i3/MX350-class CPUs, with stronger value on ARM64 mobile cores where cache-line ownership traffic is expensive.
Decision 16: Vault-Backed Dump Latch
Problem: black-box dump path could write same 300-frame file every post-simulation frame while divergence or max-iteration fault stayed active. Abyssal thermal also held this latch as private managed bool, which is shadow-state leak for solver forensics.
Solution: Power now uses existing Vault counter buffer 731068 slot 6 as CounterDumpedFaultMask; abyssal thermal uses owner-local Vault buffer 70054 (int1) as AbyssalThermalSolverDumpLatch. Latches reset after clean telemetry frame and only dump again when new fault bit appears.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping private bool; dumping every faulted frame; adding managed log throttling; suppressing dumps globally and losing first-fault evidence.
Scalability potential: All quality levels keep same forensic route. Low-tier devices avoid repeated disk I/O during sustained thermal divergence; high/ultra still preserve first exact 300-frame pre-fault trace.
Hardware Impact: One integer read/write per post-simulation fault check. Prevents repeated file writes that can cost milliseconds and cause storage stalls on mobile hardware.
Decision 17: Removable World Wrapper Dependency Cut
Problem: LogisticsNetworkGraph was using Hecton8.World.DispatcherJobSwap only for job-handle finalization, even though wrapper delegates to Hecton8.Core.DispatcherJobFence. Because SHINOBU203 touched this solver surface, keeping removable World using widened compile-wall coupling unnecessarily.
Solution: Replace two DispatcherJobSwap.TryComplete calls with DispatcherJobFence.TryComplete and remove using Hecton8.World from LogisticsNetworkGraph.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving wrapper because it was pre-existing; editing World helper code; expanding change to unrelated AbsoluteUniversePosition usages in ShinobuLogisticsRouter.
Scalability potential: No runtime quality change. Compile isolation improves iteration speed on all hardware by avoiding avoidable sibling namespace dependency in touched power solver file.
Hardware Impact: Runtime cost is neutral; compile wall and source dependency surface are smaller.
Decision 18: Abyssal Inner Jacobi Loop Removal
Problem: HeatDiffusionSolverJob still carried local for loop over Tuning.JacobiIterations. solver manager already forces passTuning.JacobiIterations = 1, so this was not currently multiplying work, but it left hidden blind-iteration trap inside Burst kernel and weakened dispatcher-owned convergence proof.
Solution: Remove inner loop from HeatDiffusionSolverJob. Each scheduled pass now performs exactly one SOR relaxation from Front to Back, writes one sampled residual into 64-byte worker slot, then lets ThermalSolverResidualReductionJob decide convergence, omega dampening, divergence, or max-iteration state.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping loop because passTuning clamps it to 1; relying on comments; adding another local break condition inside cell job. Those keep iteration authority split between dispatcher and kernel.
Scalability potential: Low still uses sparse residual masks and loose tolerance; middle/high/ultra spend additional scheduled passes only while pass-wide residual says grid has not settled. No binary tier branch was introduced.
Hardware Impact: Current runtime delta is mostly defensive because passTuning.JacobiIterations was already 1. real gain is removing compile-time footgun that could turn 8-pass solve into 64 local relaxations. Static scanner now reports 0 blind candidates and 5 guarded residual sites.
Decision 19: Abyssal Stable-Limit Tuning Sanitization
Problem: abyssal runaway guard computed stableLimit from raw Tuning.AmbientTemperatureCelsius and Tuning.MaxStableTemperatureCelsius. If either tuning scalar was non-finite, limit calculation could become non-finite and weaken finite candidate guard exactly when bad tuning payload needed containment.
Solution: Sanitize both tuning inputs through AbyssalThermalMath.FiniteOr before deriving stableLimit. SOR candidate still falls back to current and stamps divergence when next is non-finite or exceeds sanitized finite bound.
Rejected Alternatives: Trust cold-boot tuning validation only; clamp every cell with fixed hard-coded temperature regardless of tuning; add managed diagnostics in job.
Scalability potential: Low, middle, high, and ultra use same finite guard. Quality still controls omega, residual mask, tolerance, and pass count continuously; this patch only prevents corrupted tuning from punching hole through guard.
Hardware Impact: Two scalar finite checks per active voxel solver pass. Estimated cost is below 1 microsecond on small grids and buys deterministic containment for bad thermal profiles.
Decision 20: Quality Scalar And Cold Tuning NaN Vaccination
Problem: Several touched solver surfaces still trusted quality or tuning scalars at edge of job boundary. non-finite GlobalQualityWeight, thermal hazard radius/temperature, abyssal editor tuning value, or shared power demand/smoothing scalar could force mass divergence flags, collapse solver output to zero, or leak NaN into external heat before residual guard observed it.
Solution: Added finite fallbacks at schedule/write boundary and inside shared Burst jobs: power thermal hazard injection sanitizes quality/radius/temperature; logistics graph and pressure jobs sanitize quality before smoothstep curves; fluid-incursion pressure delta uses finite external/internal pressure values; abyssal tuning writers sanitize quality/conductivity/cell size/convection/dissipation; PowerVoltageSolverJob sanitizes demand and smoothing inputs before relaxation.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting editor sliders and CSV profiles; allowing NaN to be caught only after it reaches telemetry; adding managed validation callbacks in active simulation.
Scalability potential: continuous quality curves remain unchanged for finite values. Low quality still uses sparse residual masks and looser tolerance; middle/high/ultra still use progressively stricter SOR behavior. patch only defines deterministic fallback points for corrupt scalars.
Hardware Impact: handful of scalar math.isfinite checks at job boundaries or once per node in shared power voltage solving. Estimated normal cost is below 1 microsecond for patched boundaries; failure containment prevents full-grid false divergence and downstream black-box churn.
Decision 21: Thermal Payload Index And Source Guard
Problem: Static division audit found abyssal helper math still trusted GridResolution for integer division/modulo, and thermal source injection trusted RadiusMeters, IntensityCelsiusPerSecond, FalloffExponent, and conductivity before casting radius to cell counts. corrupt Vault/CSV/source payload could therefore cause divide-by-zero, modulo-by-zero, non-finite radius casts, or NaN conductivity propagation before residual guard observed field.
Solution: Added AbyssalThermalMath.SafeResolution, routed Index, DecodeIndex, PositiveModulo, and AUP-to-cell mapping through finite minimum dimensions, sanitized thermal source radius/intensity/falloff/conductivity before radius-cell loops, sanitized diffusion ambient/conductivity/dissipation/max-stable/convection scalars inside HeatDiffusionSolverJob, and sanitized TrySample/Shader/Gizmo reads. Replaced cold telemetry/profile MemClear with explicit pointer default loops to keep SHINOBU static gate free of broad memory-zeroing calls.
Rejected Alternatives: Trusting BuildTuning only; allowing bad source payloads to fail later through telemetry; using managed validation callbacks; widening Core DTO contracts for this local hardening pass.
Scalability potential: Low quality still collapses residual proof and sampling density through continuous masks; middle/high/ultra keep tighter SOR and visual interpolation. These guards do not add binary tiers; they only define finite fallback points for corrupt payloads.
Hardware Impact: Integer and scalar guards add below 1 us in normal source/diffusion paths on i3/MX350-class hardware. Failure containment prevents full-grid invalid index work, NaN thermal propagation, and repeated black-box churn.
Decision 22: File-Backed Report Ordering
Problem: final LOGSHINOBU203.md thermal payload report was appended after first audit block rather than at file bottom, violating project rule that logs are chronological with newest material last.
Solution: Move whole Thermal Payload Index Guard section to bottom without changing runtime code, then rerun scanner and static gates so file-backed report order matches actual latest pass.
Rejected Alternatives: Leaving misplaced report because content was correct; duplicating section; claiming completion from chat while CTO-facing file was out of order.
Scalability potential: Runtime-neutral. It protects audit traceability across low, middle, high, and ultra tuning records because newest convergence proof is now last block on disk.
Hardware Impact: No runtime effect. Process impact is deterministic: future agents read latest SHINOBU state from end of log without replaying stale audit order.
Decision 23: Jacobi-Safe Relaxation And Reader Fence
Problem: Static subagent audit found three hard risks: one duplicated sourcePotential local that would block C# compile in LogisticsNetworkGraph, over-relaxed weighted Jacobi (omega 1) in double-buffer solver passes, and external thermal sampling jobs that could read front while next tick writes/switches buffers.
Solution: Renamed duplicate logistics local, clamped double-buffered power/thermal relaxation to continuous Jacobi-safe damping (0.55..1.0) instead of false SOR over-relaxation, made convergence residuals authoritative for every processed cell while keeping worker-slot map-reduce, and chained external SampleTemperatureJob handles into next thermodynamics writer dependency. Cached power black-box Vault at graph construction so black-box sampling no longer resolves GlobalRegistry.DataVault on every post-evaluation sample.
Rejected Alternatives: Keeping omega 1 to satisfy label "SOR" while risking divergence; using sampled-only residuals as convergence proof; forcing main-thread completes for sample readers; leaving duplicate local for compile to catch; runtime filesystem polling for heat profiles.
Scalability potential: Low keeps fewer cadence passes and looser tolerance with damped relaxation; middle/high/ultra still use more scheduled passes and tighter tolerance, but no tier over-relaxes double-buffer Jacobi solve. Thermal sampling remains continuously nearest-to-trilinear without hard math.step gate.
Hardware Impact: Full residual authority costs one scalar worker-slot max already computed per cell; removing false over-relaxation prevents oscillation/retry churn. Reader fencing avoids race-induced corruption without blocking main thread.
Decision 24: Quality-Amortized Pipe Flow Publish
Problem: ShinobuLogisticsRouter.PublishFlowVisuals pushed every logistics edge to pipe renderer after each solved frame. solver truth is already Vault-owned, but this visual fanout remained O(edgeCount) on every publish and bought no gameplay correctness on thermally constrained devices.
Solution: Add one scalar publish cursor and resolve continuous budget from globalQualityWeight: low pressure updates roughly 32 edges per publish, middle tiers smoothly raise budget, and quality 1.0 publishes full edge set. edge cursor is scalar state, not persistent managed/native array; solver pressure, residuals, telemetry, and rollback truth remain untouched.
Rejected Alternatives: Allocating dirty-edge list; adding another Vault buffer for visual-only last-published values; binary low/high renderer disable; removing pipe flow visuals entirely; touching Core renderer contracts during Jacobi polish pass.
Scalability potential: Low amortizes cosmetic pipe-flow sync over frames while keeping enough motion to preserve readability; middle/high raise visual cadence continuously; Ultra spends saved solver stability budget on full pipe-flow refresh.
Hardware Impact: Worst-case visual publish drops from O(edgeCount) every solved frame to O(32..edgeCount) based on quality. Expected low-end saving depends on edge count and renderer implementation; for 1000-2000 edges this avoids hundreds to thousands of interface calls per solved logistics frame.
